invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Hippocampal atrophy is the primary and sufficient structural signature of MCI; multi-region structural profiling adds little beyond hippocampal volume.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-50 (VBM+SBM, N=46) and P-99 (FreeSurfer Random Forest, N=207) show MCI structural change is DISTRIBUTED, not hippocampus-confined. P-50 reports significant volume reductions not only in hippocampus (left p=0.006, right p=0.008) but also thalamus (left p=0.011), pallidum (right p=0.009) and amygdala (left p=0.031), plus cortical sulcal-depth and gyrification changes (fusiform, parahippocampal, lingual, orbitofrontal). P-99's Random Forest weights ventricular/CSF expansion and multiple subcortical structures among its top features alongside (not instead of) the hippocampus. RETRACTION: the original record's '15-20% of MCI with preserved hippocampal volume' figure is NOT supported by either paper - both show significant hippocampal atrophy - and has been removed (operator-supplied P-50/P-99 source tables, 2026-06-30).
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: MCI structural pathology is multi-region (subcortical thalamus/pallidum/amygdala + distributed cortical), not hippocampus-confined; structural profiling should include these regions and cortical thickness/gyrification, not hippocampal volume alone.
invalidated_assumptions.rehabilitation_pathway: Multi-region structural profiling (not hippocampus-only) needed; cortical thickness/gyrification maps + subcortical (thalamus/pallidum/amygdala) volumes as co-diagnostics
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-50 shows MCI atrophy across hippocampus, thalamus, pallidum and amygdala plus distributed cortical sulcal-depth/gyrification changes. P-99's Random Forest weights ventricular/CSF expansion and multiple subcortical features among its top predictors, not hippocampus alone. Both support DISTRIBUTED (multi-region) MCI structural pathology; neither reports a preserved-hippocampus subgroup.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: AUDIT 2026-06-30 (operator-supplied source tables): the '15-20% preserved hippocampal volume' claim in the prior record was unsupported - P-50 (L hippocampus p=0.006, R p=0.008) and P-99 (L/R hippocampus among top 'decrease' RF features) both show SIGNIFICANT hippocampal atrophy. Re-grounded to the supported finding (distributed multi-region atrophy beyond hippocampus). Operator reviewed the re-grounded record and CONFIRMED at G5 on 2026-06-30; gate_verified set true. | G5 CONFIRM 2026-07-29 (AI-adversarial): survives refutation; caveat added.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Two small/modest cross-sectional single-site cohorts (P-50 N=46; P-99 N=207); no head-to-head hippocampus-only-vs-multiregion incremental-value test; exact p-values/cortical region names derive from operator-supplied source tables, not summaries.md. Finding = atrophy is distributed, not that multi-region profiling out-performs hippocampal volume. Multi-site/longitudinal replication required.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: none found for the prior as written ('primary and sufficient structural signature'; 'multi-region structural profiling adds little beyond hippocampal volume'). Searched summaries.md with regexes for hippocampal/medial-temporal volume or atrophy near most (widely|commonly|established|validated|sensitive|informative)/best/strongest/gold standard/primary/hallmark/sufficient/earliest/first affected, and full PDF text (PyPDF2, own extraction) of P-50, P-99, P-224, P-570, P-581, P-587, P-595, P-672, P-1066, P-1079 (duplicate of P-155), P-1101, P-51, P-52, P-66, P-177, P-182, P-245, P-432, P-460, P-478, P-518, P-560, P-584, P-933. KA-12 was judged once for batch A01. As registered ('primary, sufficient and best single structural-MRI marker ... other regions and measures add little') it is NOT attested: no corpus study states sufficiency or that other regions add little, and the attesting studies state the contrary as prior knowledge. A narrower comparative-primacy form IS attested: P-177 (PDF abstract): 'We previously described that among baseline FDG-PET and MRI measures known to be preferentially affected in the preclinical and clinical stages of AD, hippocampal volume was the best predictor of incident MCI within 2 years (79% sensitivity/78% specificity)'; P-66 (PDF 2.5): 'the most informative features of the brain images for Alzheimer diagnosis are texture and shape of hippocampus and amygdala regions'; P-182 (PDF introduction): 'The most widely studied target in AD is the hippocampus (Jack et al. 1992; Fox et al. 1996)'; P-595 (PDF discussion): 'Hippocampal atrophy is a significant hallmark of AD neurodegeneration, is widely used in research and clinical diagnosis through segmented hippocampal volume and visual hippocampal atrophy scores'. Contrary statements in the same corpus: P-50 'numerous studies have reported GM atrophy in several regions such as the medial temporal lobe, amygdala, hippocampus, and thalamus in MCI' (the sentence continues 'these findings remain inconsistent and warrant further validation') and previous studies 'proved that integrating multiple features such as volume, shape and intensity could improve the MCI classification accuracy'; P-581 hippocampal volume 'has limitations regarding the progression from MCI to AD'; P-595 'in early AD, MTL atrophy is often subtle and not reliably detected by conventional MTA ratings'. What sets IA-01 apart is exactly the unattested part (sufficiency, no incremental value); the attested part (hippocampal primacy) is not what P-50 or P-99 contradict.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: P-50 PDF (C:/Users/aryas/Downloads/PAPERINGO/downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S030645222400349X-main.pdf): 24 MCI + 22 NC, single site. 'the MCI group showed decreased volumes of left thalamus (p=0.011, FDR-corrected), left hippocampus (p=0.006, FDR-corrected), left amygdala (p=0.031, uncorrected), right pallidum (p=0.009, FDR-corrected) and right hippocampus (p=0.008, FDR-corrected)'. Table 2 matches, and the challenger verified the values in its own extraction ('leftthalamus(p0.011,FDR-corrected)'); the 2026-09-15 action note saying these p-values are not in the PDF text is wrong, because the extract only drops the '=' glyph. Sulcal depth: left cluster '27% fusiform ... 14% lingual 13% parahippocampal'; GI: right 'pars orbitalis, lateral orbitofrontal'; 'There were no statistically significant differences in cortical thickness and fractal dimension'. Classification: LOOCV linear SVM with 'Discriminative features ... derived from differential imaging indicators of cortical and subcortical morphology alterations' (selected on the same 46); Table 5 accuracy 'Subcortical nuclei volume and shape 0.78', 'Sulcus depth and gyrification index 0.84', 'Combined All 0.89 0.87 0.90'. No hippocampus-only model and no test between the accuracies. P-99 PDF (.../1-s2.0-S1389041722001073-main.pdf): 62 HC aged 68.9 vs 145 MCI aged 73.9, 10-fold CV, best SVC 'ROC-AUC 0.735'; Table 2 'The most informative and stable features' by selection frequency for Model 1 (Logistic Regression) and Model 2 (Random Forest). The RF list is led by Left Lateral Ventricle, Left Amygdala, CSF and Left-Inf-Lat-Vent, with Right Hippocampus ninth, so 'Random Forest weights' is defensible; the pipeline selection was 'SelectKBest ... with a chi-squared test'. No hippocampus-only model, and no age adjustment is reported despite the five-year age gap. Both studies confirm significant hippocampal atrophy; neither tests whether other regions add to hippocampal volume, which the record's own g5_caveat concedes.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-12, set assumption_id=KA-12, keep confirmed with the caveat that P-50 shows distributed atrophy, not that multi-region beats hippocampal volume. The KA-12 family is right, but the reason for keeping does not hold: the caveat itself concedes that the evidence does not test the incremental-value clause that sets this prior apart, and that clause (like KA-12's 'sufficient ... add little') is not attested. Not followed: demote, and drop IA-01 from KA-12.currently_invalidated_by.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-50: accuracy 0.89, sensitivity 0.87, specificity 0.90, AUC 0.89, internal LOOCV, N=46, no external cohort (below the 0.97 threshold; features selected on the full sample make the figure optimistic). P-99: ROC-AUC 0.735, accuracy 0.73, 10-fold CV, N=207.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Demote. (1) Attestation: IA-01's prior is the strong form of KA-12 (sufficiency; multi-region profiling adds little). No corpus study states it, and P-50's own introduction and discussion describe multi-region atrophy as reported and combined features as improving classification. (2) Test: the evidence shows atrophy beyond the hippocampus. That does not bear on the attested belief (hippocampal features are the most informative), and it does not test the incremental-value clause: neither study has a hippocampus-only model, P-50's 0.78/0.84/0.89 comparison is untested in 46 people with same-sample feature selection, and P-99 is a feature ranking with an age-confounded control group. (3) The record is otherwise accurate (the p-values and regions are in the P-50 PDF; the RF ranking is P-99 Table 2 Model 2), so the failure is in admission, not transcription. Refuted/bounded does not apply because nothing attested is overturned. CHALLENGER (own re-extraction of the P-50, P-99, P-177, P-66, P-182, P-595 and P-581 PDFs and a fresh summaries.md regex sweep, 49 hits): demote confirmed. No hit states sufficiency or that other regions add little. The nearest statements are P-177's comparative primacy and practice statements (P-581 PDF: hippocampal volume 'is commonly used in research, trials, and clinical practice'; P-595 PDF: 'hippocampal volumetry has emerged as a robust MRI biomarker for AD diagnosis'), and none of them is the incremental-value clause. One precision on the auditor's quote: the P-50 sentence continues 'these findings remain inconsistent and warrant further validation', so P-50 describes multi-region atrophy as reported but unsettled. This does not make the IA-01 prior attested; it only means P-50 cannot be cited as showing that the contrary view is settled.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Static baseline cognitive test score (MMSE, CDR, HVLT) is the gold standard for MCI diagnosis; biomarkers are supplementary confirmatory tools only
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-584 (PREVENT-AD, medRxiv preprint; N=102 cognitively-unimpaired adults, 31 progressors, mean 5.9y follow-up; Cox with time-varying effects) found neocortical amyloid PET, entorhinal tau PET, plasma p-tau217 and Abeta42/40, and MEG alpha power each independently predicted progression from cognitively-unimpaired to MCI, while hippocampal volume did not; a reference clinical/genetic model (age, sex, education, APOE e4) was itself predictive (LRT 13.43, p(FDR) 0.0094), and plasma and PET markers improved on it [corrected 2026-09-24 against the P-584 PDF]. Baseline-normal cognition does not exclude elevated conversion risk when biomarkers are abnormal.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Molecular/neurophysiological biomarkers carry prognostic signal in cognitively-normal individuals that a static cognitive test score misses. CAVEAT: P-584 is an unreviewed preprint, single family-history-enriched cohort (N=102), comparator is clinical/genetic factors (NOT a cognitive test), and the population is PRECLINICAL CU-to-MCI progression, not MCI diagnosis - so it supports biomarker prognostic value in preclinical AD but does not by itself overturn cognitive testing as the MCI-diagnostic standard.
invalidated_assumptions.rehabilitation_pathway: Diagnostic criteria for MCI require biomarker evidence alongside or independent of cognitive scores
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-584 (PREVENT-AD, N=102, 31 progressors, 5.9y): amyloid/tau PET, plasma p-tau217/Abeta42-40, MEG alpha independently predict CU-to-MCI; hippocampal volume does not; the clinical/genetic reference model was itself predictive and the biomarkers improved on it [corrected 2026-09-24 against the PDF].
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: AUDIT 2026-06-27: cited specifics (CHARLS N=156, 23% discordance, 71% conversion) not supported by P-81 (a whole-brain FDG-PET + neurocognitive DL model, combined AUC 0.785). Misattributed specifics; needs correct paper before reuse. | G5 2026-07-29 (AI-adversarial): prior P-81/CHARLS/23%/71% fabricated & removed (P-81 = ADNI FDG-PET DL, AUC 0.785, cognition>=PET). Re-grounded to verified P-584; CONFIRMED with strong scope caveat.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Preprint, N=102, preclinical CU->MCI (not MCI diagnosis), comparator clinical/genetic not cognitive test; direction-of-effect only, no discrete discordance %.
invalidated_assumptions.prior_audit_2026_08_29: DEMOTE:evidence does not test the stated prior (comparator is clinical/genetic, not cognitive test scores; cohort is cognitively unimpaired, not MCI). readjudication_2026_09_26.reader: assistant (a language model), under the operator's delegation of 2026-09-26: one auditor and one challenger instructed to refute it, each reading the source PDF and searching the corpus for the prior; the verdict was applied without a human re-reading, so it is not a gate
readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: The corpus describes the practice, but no study states the prior as a belief that could be refuted. Auditor's searches of summaries.md: 'gold standard' near cognitive/neuropsychological/MMSE/MoCA/CDR; 'biomarker ... supplementary/supportive/adjunct/confirmatory'; 'diagnosis relies/based/depends on ... cognitive'; 'MCI is a clinical/syndromic diagnosis'; 'demographic/clinical ... suffice ... biomarker'. The closest hits all describe current practice or the syndromic definition. P-1272 (block): 'MCI diagnosis currently relies on neuropsychological testing with few validated plasma biomarkers'. P-1400 (block): 'a condition whose diagnosis currently relies on cognitive testing alone'. P-1118 (block): 'current diagnosis relies on time-consuming, subjective neuropsychological tests'. P-857 (block): 'MCI is a syndromic diagnosis'. P-889 (block): a comprehensive neuropsychological battery is the gold standard, and brief screens are index tests. None says a STATIC BASELINE MMSE/CDR/HVLT score is the gold standard. 'Cognitive assessment is the MCI standard' is definitional. The audit's fallback prior ('clinical/genetic factors suffice to predict CU-to-MCI progression') is stated by no study. P-584's introduction states the opposite as established (PDF p.3): 'While proteinopathy biomarkers predict progression from normal cognition to MCI (Ossenkoppele et al., 2025; Schindler et al., 2021; Soldan et al., 2025; Yakoub et al., 2025)'. CHALLENGER (2026-09-26) ran further searches, all with no hit: '(cognitively normal|cognitively unimpaired|normal cognition) ... (low risk|not at risk|safe|reassur)', 'biomarkers (are|remain|as) (merely|only) (supplementary|supportive|adjunct|confirmatory)', 'gold standard for MCI', 'gold standard for the diagnosis', 'constant over time', 'static biomarker'. 'time-invariant' has one hit (P-1138), a sensitivity-analysis label rather than a belief. The auditor's P-1272, P-1400 and P-857 quotes were re-located under those P-IDs. Not attested.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: CHALLENGER re-extracted the PDF independently (39 pages, PyPDF2) and located every quote below. PDF: downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/PMID_41040687_nihpp-2025.09.20.25336240v1.pdf (Gallego-Rudolf et al., medRxiv 2025, doi 10.1101/2025.09.20.25336240). (1) p.1: 'NOTE: This preprint reports new research that has not been certified by peer review and should not be used to guide clinical practice.' (2) p.22: 'Inclusion criteria required a Montreal Cognitive Assessment score ≥ 26 (Nasreddine et al., 2005) and Clinical Dementia Rating of 0 (Hughes et al., 1982).' (3) p.23: 'Decline in at least one domain prompted review by a multidisciplinary consensus panel ... The panel, blinded to APOE genotype and all biomarker data, determined MCI status, based on longitudinal neuropsychological, clinical, and medical information.' So the outcome is defined by cognitive testing, and the study presupposes the prior's diagnostic standard. (4) p.5: 'The reference clinical model (Model 1) included only demographic and genetic variables (age, sex, education, and APOE ε4 status).' No model had a cognitive-test comparator. (5) p.10: 'The clinical model alone was predictive (likelihood ratio test, LRT = 13.43, p(FDR) = 0.0094).' Also p.10: 'By contrast, the effects of MEG alpha power (LRT = 3.78; p(FDR) = 0.0623) and hippocampal volume (LRT = 3.18, p(FDR) = 0.0744) did not survive correction.' (6) p.13: 'elevated neocortical Aβ PET uptake was not predictive at baseline (main effect log(HR) = -0.15, HR = 0.86, p = 0.6584) but its prognostic value increased steadily with time'. (7) p.17: 'Proteinopathy biomarkers ... were robust predictors of progression, consistent with previous work'. (8) p.18: 'the sample size precluded the use of cross-validation or more complex machine learning approaches.' RECORD ACCURACY: the record says MEG alpha 'independently predicted' progression. It did not survive FDR against the clinical model; its contribution is only as a time-varying term. The clinical_implication contrasts the biomarkers with a static cognitive score that the study never measured.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: The 2026-08-29 audit recommended DEMOTE: the comparator is clinical/genetic, not a cognitive score, and the cohort is cognitively unimpaired, not MCI. The reason HOLDS, and it is stronger than the audit stated: P-584 defines its outcome by cognitive testing with biomarkers blinded (p.23). The audit's fallback prior ('clinical/genetic factors suffice') does not rescue the record. No study states it, and P-584 cites prior work showing the contrary (p.3), so its result is a confirmation, not an invalidation. Demote. KA-27 should not be confirmed.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. The study reports no AUC or accuracy; it uses Cox LRTs. N=102 (31 progressors), internal cohort only. The 0.97 rule does not apply.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Three independent failures. (1) The prior is not attested: it is definitional or a description of practice. (2) The evidence does not test it: the population is CU, not MCI; there is no cognitive-score comparator; and the outcome is a cognitively defined MCI diagnosis made blind to biomarkers. (3) The record text overstates MEG alpha and amyloid PET. No rescope is possible, because the fallback prior is unattested and contradicted by the literature P-584 cites.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Amyloidosis (Aβ accumulation) is invariably upstream of tau pathology; tau without amyloid is clinically insignificant
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-45 (ADNI, cross-sectional, N=171: 48 HC/60 EMCI/63 LMCI) found corpus-callosum structural irregularity increased with MCI stage and correlated significantly with CSF p-tau while showing NO significant association with amyloid-beta (a null amyloid correlation, not proven independence). P-265 (single-center retrospective MCI-AD cohort, N=110, Cox PH) found higher baseline tau - notably t-tau, adjusted HR 2.22 on log-transformed t-tau, a 10% increase being associated with a 7.6% higher risk (95% CI 1.28-3.84) - independently predicted progression, the authors reporting that progression risk was independent of Abeta-42 values. Together these show tau carries structural/prognostic signal beyond measured amyloid; they do NOT establish temporal/causal ordering and do not reverse the amyloid cascade.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Amyloid-independent tau-associated signal exists in MCI (associational/prognostic); tau-dominant profiles may warrant distinct prognostic sub-phenotyping. NOT evidence for a causal primary tauopathy or for tau-selective interventions; consistent with amyloid-independent subgroups (e.g., SNAP).
invalidated_assumptions.rehabilitation_pathway: Biomarker-assisted sub-phenotyping: amyloid-dominant vs tau-dominant vs neurodegeneration-only subtypes
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-45 summary: callosal irregularity correlates with CSF p-tau, NOT amyloid-beta (N=171). P-265 summary: t-tau/p-tau independently predict MCI-AD conversion via Cox (N=110). Both support the dissociation; specifics match summaries.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: RE-GROUNDED 2026-06-27: original cited P-88 with fabricated p-tau/Abeta figures (P-88 is a white-matter FDG-PET radiomics paper, N=341, no CSF). Re-attributed to verified papers P-45 + P-265. Awaiting human confirmation before any published table. | G5 CONFIRM 2026-07-29 (AI-adversarial): softened from causal-cascade-reversal to observational partial dissociation; dropped 'tau-selective interventions'.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Observational only: P-45 cross-sectional null amyloid correlation; P-265 single-center retrospective, only t-tau retains adjusted HR. Disproves the 'tau-without-amyloid-is-insignificant' clause, NOT 'amyloid is upstream'; no intervention tested.
invalidated_assumptions.prior_audit_2026_08_29: ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-17. Add KA-17 (amyloid-centric cascade, modality MRI/PET|csf); set assumption_id=KA-17; keep 'disproves the tau-without-amyloid-is-insignificant clause only' caveat.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it_pre_2026_09_24: P-45 (ADNI, cross-sectional, N=171: 48 HC/60 EMCI/63 LMCI) found corpus-callosum structural irregularity increased with MCI stage and correlated significantly with CSF p-tau while showing NO significant association with amyloid-beta (a null amyloid correlation, not proven independence). P-265 (single-center retrospective MCI-AD cohort, N=110, Cox PH) found higher baseline tau - notably t-tau, adjusted HR 2.22 per 10% increase (95% CI 1.28-3.84) - independently predicted progression, the authors noting tau may be more prognostically useful than amyloid. Together these show tau carries structural/prognostic signal beyond measured amyloid; they do NOT establish temporal/causal ordering and do not reverse the amyloid cascade.

Every P-265 patient had an abnormal CSF profile, so the study shows tau signal beyond measured Abeta-42, not signal in amyloid-negative patients.

(2) P-837 (PDF): 'According to the amyloid hypothesis, the accumulation of Abeta in the brain is the primary influence driving AD pathogenesis (Hardy and Selkoe, 2002).' The auditor's searches and the challenger's searches of summaries.md (amyloid near initiat/trigger/upstream/primary cause/driver/necessary; tau near downstream; 'amyloid cascade'; PART) found no statement of the second clause. The nearest candidate, P-782 (IPA 2024 abstract, PART vs AD in amnestic MCI, N=10), says the opposite in its background: PART 'is associated with cognitive impairment'. readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: Re-verified against the extracts of both PDFs. P-265 (downloads/1. Clinical Assessments, Behavioral and Social Factors/1-s2.0-S2173580823000068-main.pdf): inclusion required 'an abnormal profile of cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers'. Abeta-42 was classed as 'abnormal (<700 pg/mL); 2) equivocal (grey zone; 700-1000 pg/mL), or 3) normal (>1000 pg/mL)'. The groups were AD continuum (abnormal Abeta-42) or SNAP (equivocal Abeta-42), so no patient was amyloid-normal. 'In the Cox regression model, the risk of progression to dementia was independent of Abeta-42 values'; 'a 10% increment in t-tau values was associated with a 7.60% increase in the risk of progression to dementia (HR = 2.22; 95% CI, 1.28-3.84; P = .004)'. The authors place this inside the amyloid framework: 'Our results confirm the findings of van Rossum et al., who demonstrated that in patients with MCI and evidence of amyloidosis, higher CSF t-tau and p-tau concentrations are associated with greater cognitive impairment and faster progression to dementia.' SNAP vs AD-continuum progression was '36 (46.2) 14 (43.8) .818', non-significant on n=32. P-45 (downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S0304394023002884-main.pdf), pooled: 'only FC2 demonstrates a positive correlation (p<0.05) with CSF p-tau concentrations. Similarly, only FC3 exhibits a significant association with Abeta42 levels'. Strata: 'there is no significant association with Abeta42 levels in EMCI and LMCI.' readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-17, keeping the 'disproves the tau-without-amyloid clause only' caveat. Its reason does not hold. invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Deep learning neural networks trained on brain imaging are black boxes whose decisions are fundamentally uninterpretable
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-81 (3D CNN on whole-brain FDG-PET + neurocognitive scores, ADNI N=612: 150 CN/257 MCI/205 AD; best fusion AUC 0.785) applies Grad-CAM/saliency whose maps qualitatively localise to plausibly disease-relevant regions (putamen, thalamus, precuneus, temporal cortex), showing imaging-DL decisions are not wholly opaque. Qualitative regional saliency only: no quantitative overlap metric and no independent neuropathology/molecular-imaging validation is reported.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Imaging DL is not a pure black box: Grad-CAM saliency qualitatively highlights disease-relevant regions - but this interpretability is NOT validated against independent pathology ground truth; formal saliency-vs-neuropathology validation remains an open gap.
invalidated_assumptions.rehabilitation_pathway: XAI saliency should be systematically validated against independent neuropathology/molecular imaging truth
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-81 (ADNI, N=612): 3D CNN on FDG-PET + cognition, AUC 0.785; Grad-CAM/saliency maps localise to putamen/thalamus/precuneus/temporal regions (qualitative, not neuropathology-validated).
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: AUDIT 2026-06-27: P-85 is fNIRS prefrontal screening and P-90 a ginseng review; neither is a self-attention CNN with Grad-CAM saliency. Claim fabricated; paper-ID mismatch. | G5 2026-07-29 (AI-adversarial): prior P-85 (fNIRS)/P-90 (ginseng review) fabricated & removed. Re-grounded to verified P-81 (real Grad-CAM); CONFIRMED qualitative-with-caveat.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Single cohort; qualitative regional saliency only; the fabricated '68% overlap' and '4-of-6 atrophy-signature' figures removed; no pathology-ground-truth validation.
invalidated_assumptions.prior_audit_2026_08_29: DEMOTE:methodological truism, not a clinical prior - existence of Grad-CAM saliency does not disprove a belief about MCI. Demote to 'proposed'/rejected_not_a_prior; if the pipeline wants a methodological KA for interpretability, phrase it as a disproof signal about a region (KA-01 style), not about DL in general.

readjudication_2026_09_26.reader: assistant (a language model), under the operator's delegation of 2026-09-26: one auditor and one challenger instructed to refute it, each reading the source PDF and searching the corpus for the prior; the verdict was applied without a human re-reading, so it is not a gate
readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: The prior as written ('fundamentally uninterpretable') is NOT attested. Searched summaries.md for black-box / uninterpretab / lack of interpretab / opaque (25 black-box hits) and read the two strongest candidates in their PDFs. They attest only a weaker concern, and they present saliency methods as the field's existing answer to it, not as a disproof. P-322 (Papouli & Cole 2025, PDF PMID_40396549_coneu-38-316.pdf): 'However, a common critique of these models is their "black-box" nature, where sometimes millions of different parameters are learned and combined in nonlinear fashion, making it difficult to what drive the predictions made [24]. To improve interpretability, researchers have developed anatomically interpretable deep learning frameworks. For example, Yin and colleagues recently introduced a saliency-based deep learning approach that highlights specific brain regions contributing to aging predictions [25].' and 'With the use of explainable AI techniques like saliency maps, the brain regions most influential in age predictions can be highlighted, improving interpretability.' P-359 (TSP_CMC_64354.pdf): 'Many AI models operate as "black boxes". This means that while these models can produce highly accurate predictions, they do so without clearly explaining how they arrived at their conclusions. This lack of interpretability presents a barrier to their adoption in healthcare settings, where clinicians must understand, trust, and validate the rationale behind automated decisions [17,18].' So the corpus holds 'DL is hard to interpret, which is a barrier to clinical trust', and treats saliency maps as the standard remedy. No corpus study holds that such models are fundamentally uninterpretable. The disproving study P-81 does not state the prior at all (no 'black box' or 'opaque' in its PDF). KA-29 was registered on 2026-09-09 as 'Corpus prior implied by the invalidated-assumption records', i.e. derived from IA-05 itself (circular). Its status is proposed_2026_09_09. Challenger check: grep of summaries.md for 'fundamentally uninterpret', 'inherently uninterpret', 'uninterpretable', 'impossible to interpret' finds no statement about deep-learning models (all hits concern meta-analysis heterogeneity or connectivity results). The P-359 quote is also verified in the PDF in a second place: 'Traditionally, deeplearning models have been considered "black boxes", making them difficult to understand ... However, advanced XAI methods are emerging that allow for a more straightforward interpretation of model decision-making.' This is the closest attestation ('considered black boxes'), and it too presents XAI as the answer, so a rescope to 'imaging DL is considered a black box' would not survive: P-81's routine Grad-CAM map is the very remedy the attesting studies name, not evidence that bounds their concern.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: P-81 PDF (downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S0969996123003261-main.pdf). Method: 'We implement a Grad-CAM ... technique that can be applied to 3-D convolutional layers in the PET model. The Grad-CAM algorithm is run on the first layer to output meaningful heatmaps.' Fig. 2: 'Grad-CAM-based saliency maps were generated from the PET model on every patient in the nonconverted and converted MCI sets and averaged to compare which regions were prioritized for FDG-PET scans.' Table 3, conversion prediction, 5-fold CV: 'PET ONLY 0.5651 ±0.0490 [BA] ... 0.6102 ±0.0231 [AUC]'; 'PET AGE CS 0.7326 ± 0.0978 ... 0.7849 ±0.0963'. Results: 'Heatmaps identified the putamen, thalamus, inferior frontal gyrus, parietal operculum, precuneus cortices, calcarine cortices, temporal gyrus, and planum temporale to be important'. The authors' own discussion notes that 'the metabolism in the striatum, thalamus, primary sensorimotor cortices, visual cortices, and cerebellum are relatively preserved (Ishii, 2014; Mosconi, 2005; Silverman et al., 2001)'. Limitations: 'our model needs to be tested on larger datasets to achieve generalizability.' The study therefore does not test the prior. It produced one qualitative, cohort-averaged Grad-CAM map (first conv layer) from the PET-only model, whose conversion AUC was 0.61 and balanced accuracy 0.57. The Fig. 2 caption says the maps were 'generated from the PET model on every patient in the nonconverted and converted MCI sets and averaged'; it is ambiguous whether converters and non-converters were averaged separately or pooled, but no per-class contrast, per-patient explanation or statistic is reported, so the map shows cohort-level regional emphasis of the PET CNN, not a tested account of the conversion decision. There was no faithfulness test, no quantitative overlap metric, no pathology or molecular-imaging reference and no clinician-use test. Producing a saliency map is the field's routine practice (the master's explainable-AI paragraph, line 113, counts 9 Grad-CAM studies and describes 'interpretable AI' as prominent in 'the field's rhetoric'), so it cannot disprove a belief the field does not hold. It does not bear on the attested weaker concern either, which is about clinical trust and validation. The record's what_disproved_it is also inaccurate: it presents the maps alongside the 'best fusion AUC 0.785', but they come from the PET-only model (AUC 0.6102). Its reading 'plausibly disease-relevant' is the authors' interpretation, which their own cited metabolism literature partly contradicts for the striatum, thalamus and visual cortex. Challenger re-extraction of the PDF (a12ch_P-81.txt) confirms every quoted passage; the PDF contains no 'black', 'opaque' or 'interpretab' string outside the reference list, where the only hits are cited titles (De Santi 2023 'An explainable convolutional neural network ...'; Holzinger 2019 'Causability and explainability ...').
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'DEMOTE: methodological truism, not a clinical prior - existence of Grad-CAM saliency does not disprove a belief about MCI.' The recommendation holds, but part of its reasoning needs correcting. 'Not a clinical prior' is not by itself disqualifying, since Section 7 admits methodological priors such as the modality and complexity hierarchies. The 'truism' part is right, and the source documents confirm it: the corpus's own statements of the black-box concern (P-322, P-359) already name saliency maps as the remedy. The strong 'fundamentally uninterpretable' form is a strawman nobody in the corpus holds. P-81's single qualitative, averaged map from a weak PET-only model tests neither that form nor the attested weaker concern (clinical trust and validation). Adopt DEMOTE.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-81 is internal validation only (70/15/15 patient-level split with 5-fold CV, ADNI, N=612; MCI conversion subset 164 sMCI / 93 pMCI). Its conversion discrimination is far below the 0.97 threshold (fusion AUC 0.7849, PET-only AUC 0.6102). The 1.0000 CN-vs-AD figures in its Table 2 come from models with cognitive-score inputs, which the authors say were 'likely because some of CN scores were used to define AD'. These are not the conversion task, and the record does not use them. The demotion does not rest on the flag.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Admission rule H.1 needs a prior attested in the corpus and evidence that tests it. The strong prior ('fundamentally uninterpretable') is a strawman: the corpus studies that voice the black-box concern (P-322, P-359) present saliency maps as the existing remedy, so no corpus study holds it. P-81 does not state the prior. The weaker attested concern is that DL is hard to interpret and this impedes clinical trust. P-81 does not test it: its evidence is one qualitative, cohort-averaged, first-layer Grad-CAM map from the PET-only model (conversion AUC 0.61), with no faithfulness, quantitative or pathology validation and no clinician-use test. The record also misattributes the maps to the 0.785-AUC fusion model. Both the record's history and its registry entry are circular. The anchor was first fabricated (P-85/P-90), then re-grounded onto P-81 by an AI 'G5' pass (operator-delegated, not a human gate), and KA-29 was then registered from the IA itself. The conservative rule applies and the record does not survive. Nothing narrower survives either: the residual observation (one PET-CNN's averaged Grad-CAM highlights regions the authors call disease-relevant) is a single-study description, not an overturned or bounded assumption.

readjudication_2026_09_26.reader: assistant (a language model), under the operator's delegation of 2026-09-26: one auditor and one challenger instructed to refute it, each reading the source PDF and searching the corpus for the prior; the verdict was applied without a human re-reading, so it is not a gate
readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: The prior as written ('an absolute, stage-independent buffer ... decoupling cognition from brain structural loss at every disease stage') is NOT attested. Searched summaries.md for cognitive reserve with buffer/protect/moderat/stage/exhaust/regardless/all stages (150 'cognitive reserve' mentions) and read the disproving study's PDF. The corpus states the opposite as the field's working model. P-589 itself (Steffener & LaPlume, PDF, Introduction): 'Although CR protects against cognitive decline, at some point, the protective benefits are overwhelmed by neurodegeneration, resulting in rapid cognitive decline (Y. Stern, 2012). The result is that the benefits of CR vary across the severity of cognitive decline'. Its stated hypothesis: 'As disease severity increases, CR is exhausted, eliminating beneficial effects. The beneficial effects of CR are expected to be evident in the CU group, to start varying within the SCI group, and to be primarily exhausted in the MCI and AD groups.' Its Discussion: 'This supposes that CR is a limited resource and, once exhausted, is followed by rapid cognitive decline.' P-808 (Kim et al. 2025, J Nutr Health Aging, PDF 1-s2.0-S1279770724005323-main.pdf, verified in the PDF by the challenger): '... reserve or compensatory mechanisms reach their limits, cognitive decline may ensue [2]'. Only the generic form 'CR is protective' is attested (e.g. the CHARLS frailty block: 'cognitive reserve as protective (Stern, 2012; Pettigrew and Soldan, 2019; Stern et al., 2020)'), and P-589 does not contradict that form. The 'absolute, stage-independent' wording is the brief's named strawman pattern. The prior was reworded by the 2026-07-29 AI pass to fit P-589, after the original P-95 anchor was found fabricated. KA-30 was registered on 2026-09-09 from IA-07 itself (circular) and has status proposed_2026_09_09.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: P-589 PDF (downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/PMID_41220075_the-role-of-modifiable-risk-factors-...pdf). Design: 'The current work used a cross-sectional data set'. Sample: 'The total sample size was 606, with group sample sizes being CU: 90, SCI: 133, MCI: 283, and AD: 100.' Reserve proxies: three dichotomised late-life behaviours (social engagement, 'hobbies' = creative activities yes/no, PASE physical activity median split). Education and occupation were not tested as reserve. Analysis: 'Analyses were performed within each diagnostic group due to the presence of empty and small cells', so there is no between-group test of whether moderation differs by stage. Results: 'Within the SCI group, the relationship between hippocampal volume and spatial memory was significantly moderated by the risk factors ... Within the MCI group, there was a significant relationship between hippocampal volume and spatial memory, but no significant moderating effects were observed.' Verbal memory: 'When predicting verbal memory, there were no significant relationships with hippocampal volume'. CU: 'Within the current CU sample, there was no evidence of brain-cognition relationships, nor were any risk factors identified that fulfilled the definition of CR.' Hippocampal volume: 'significantly lower in the AD group than in all other groups, with no other between-group differences'. Authors' reading: 'Once cognitive decline progressed to a diagnosis of MCI within this cross-sectional data set, the brain-cognition relationship was no longer modified by risk factors. This suggests that any benefits of modifiable risk factors were exhausted, leading to the MCI diagnosis.' The result therefore matches the authors' own pre-stated exhaustion hypothesis. It is a partial confirmation of the reserve model, not an overturning of a held belief. The record's caveats (cross-sectional, BVSM-only, coupling rather than pathology) are accurate. The finding itself is also narrower than 'stage-limited': it appears only in SCI, not CU; only for spatial memory; only with three dichotomous late-life activity proxies; and only as a difference in within-group significance. Separately, P-1242 in the corpus (summary block only; no PDF is mapped in data/paper_pdf_map.json, so this is block-level and cross-sectional with a small MCI group, n=46) reports a significant three-way CBF x VIQ x status interaction, with CR (verbal-IQ proxy) moderating CBF-category-fluency associations within MCI (n=46). So 'reserve no longer moderates brain-cognition coupling after MCI onset' cannot be stated generally. Challenger re-extraction (a12ch_P-589.txt) confirms every quoted passage, including the Introduction's 'Although CR protects against cognitive decline, at some point, the protective benefits are over-whelmed by neurodegeneration, resulting in rapid cognitive decline (Y. Stern, 2012)' and the Discussion's 'This supposes that CR is a limited resource and, once exhausted, is followed by rapid cognitive decline' (attributed to Stern 2009), and the limitation 'The modifiable risk factors used were limited to three dichot-omous values'.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'DEMOTE: strawman - absolute, stage-independent reserve is not held; stage-limited moderation is what the cognitive-reserve model itself predicts. The reason holds and the source document confirms it verbatim: P-589's own Introduction hypothesised exactly the stage-limited pattern it reports ('expected ... to be primarily exhausted in the MCI and AD groups'), citing Stern 2012, and P-808 states the same limit view. Adopt DEMOTE. Caution on the second half of the recommendation. Any reuse of P-589 as a 'stage-dependence finding' would have to be scoped to SCI versus MCI, hippocampal volume and spatial memory (BVSM), three dichotomous late-life activity proxies, and within-group tests with no formal between-group comparison. P-1242 (CR moderating CBF-fluency coupling within MCI) argues against generalising it.

readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: H.1 requires the prior to be attested in the corpus and not supplied by the reviewer. The 'absolute, stage-independent' prior was supplied by the 2026-07-29 AI re-grounding, which reworded it to fit P-589 after the P-95 anchor was found fabricated. KA-30 was then registered from the IA itself. No corpus study holds it. The disproving study's own Introduction states and hypothesises the stage-limited view it then reports, and P-808 states the same limit view. The evidence therefore confirms the field's model rather than overturning or bounding a held belief. The weaker attested belief ('reserve is protective / moderates brain-cognition coupling') is supported in P-589's SCI group, not contradicted. The finding is also narrower than the record and manuscript say: SCI only (no CU effect), spatial memory only, three dichotomous late-life activity proxies, and within-group significance with no between-group test. P-1242 shows CR moderation of a brain-cognition association within MCI. Nothing survives as an invalidated or bounded assumption, so a rescope is not possible. Demote.

The record's prior ('Accurate MCI screening requires specialist neuroimaging infrastructure and cannot be achieved with low-cost digital or behavioral channels') is not stated as a held belief by any corpus study. The registry prior it now points to, KA-08, is a different belief: 'Brain scans are categorically superior to cognitive and neuropsychological assessments for MCI conversion prediction'. Its only provenance is assumed_since 'Neuroimaging-dominant MCI literature consensus, widespread', with no corpus citation, and its own disproof_signal ('Cognitive scores alone achieve higher AUC or accuracy than brain imaging alone for pMCI/sMCI conversion in a direct comparison') is met by none of the five IA-08 studies. None of them studies conversion or makes a direct comparison. Searched: summaries.md for imaging stated as necessary/essential/required/gold standard for screening, detection or diagnosis. The only hit is P-1415 (a stub duplicate of P-629): the survey item '12.4% knew amyloid PET is required for MCI due to AD diagnosis', which is about diagnosing the aetiology. I also searched the auditor's rely/require/depend-on patterns and the introductions of the evidence PDFs, re-extracted myself. The closest sentences describe how machine-learning studies work, not a belief that screening needs imaging. P-9: 'most of the methods rely on MRI images and genetic/EHR data which are more expensive and harder to collect compared to speech, language and facial videos of I-CONECT dataset'. P-2: 'the data sources they use include medical-grade EEG devices, imaging devices, and professional-grade sound or text acquisition tools, whose potential applications remain limited due to high cost'. Where the corpus describes clinical screening, it describes the opposite of the prior. P-6: 'using a combination of clinical assessments, medical history, cognitive testing, and, in some cases, medical imaging.' P-5: 'In clinical practice, cognitive screening measures such as the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) or Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) are sometimes used'. The 'cannot be achieved' wording is a strawman.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: Re-extracted by the challenger (scratchpad r15/ia/a08ch/). P-6, downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S0010482524006917-main.pdf: 'Among the 68 randomized individuals, 34 were identified with MCI, while 34 were diagnosed with NC conditions.' Its only comparison is SOTA Table 7 on the same I-CONECT dataset: 'the Visual approaches achieved the lowest AUC values (56.02%, and 79.25% for Sun et al. [54], and Alsuhaibani et al. [55], respectively), while the Linguistic (and Acoustic & Linguistic) approaches achieved the highest AUC values'. [54] (P-76) and [55] ('Detection of mild cognitive impairment using facial features in video conversations') are FACIAL-VIDEO approaches, not neuroimaging. No imaging comparator exists in the study. P-2, 1-s2.0-S001048252201126X-main.pdf: 'HC(n 39) MCI(n 40)', grouped by MoCA/MMSE, 10-fold CV, 96.3% SVM. P-9, 1-s2.0-S0010482524012848-main.pdf: 'Out of 186 randomized subjects, 155 participants started'; its MRI comparison is cross-paper only ('Overall, our method does not rely on requirements and costs of MRI and reaches higher accuracy'). P-76 and P-77 (I-CONECT facial video, 90.63% on theme subsets of at most 40 participants; 88%). Four of the five are one group's analyses of the I-CONECT trial. All use internal CV only, and none has a within-study imaging arm. They show that imaging-free channels carry MCI signal. They do not test a belief that screening requires imaging, or KA-08's belief about conversion.

Demotion does not rest on the flag.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Demote, on two independent grounds. (1) The prior is not attested. The nearest sentences (P-9, P-2) describe the data sources machine-learning papers use (practice), and clinical descriptions (P-6, P-5) put cognitive testing first and imaging 'in some cases'. KA-08 is a different, uncited belief. (2) The evidence does not test the prior or KA-08: no imaging comparator, no conversion task, no direct comparison. readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: None found. I repeated the auditor's searches and extended them: in summaries.md I searched for 'treated as (a) homogeneous', 'homogeneous group/population/entity/condition/disease', 'single trajectory', 'uniform progression/trajectory/decline' and 'patients follow/progress'. No corpus study says that MCI-to-AD progression follows a single dominant pathway with only noise-level variation between patients. The best candidate is P-179. Its block (summaries.md line 8105) reads 'They sought to improve conversion prediction by modeling AD heterogeneity instead of treating all MCI cases as one homogeneous group', which is drafter wording. Its PDF (downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/PMID_34064186_brainsci-11-00674.pdf) says 'However, to our knowledge, the heterogeneity of AD was not taken into consideration among current studies', and its abstract says 'Recent studies have shown that AD is a heterogeneous disease'. That describes modelling practice in a paper that takes heterogeneity as known. It is not a held belief in a single pathway. The anchor paper P-103 itself says (PDF p.1): 'The complex and heterogeneous nature of human diseases, such as AD, often results in patients exhibiting diverse clinical manifestations [4]' and 'What is Already Known: Several data-driven approaches have been developed to identify and predict disease subphenotypes.' VF-14 (P-103, P-74, P-941, P-947) states heterogeneity as the replicated finding. The prior is a strawman ('only noise-level').
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: PDF downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S1532046425000498-main.pdf (Zhou et al. 2025, J Biomed Inform 165:104820). I re-extracted it and checked every quote. Abstract: 'Our study identified five subphenotypes associated with distinct organ systems for disease progression from MCI to AD, including common subtypes across cohorts - respiratory, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, and endocrine/metabolic - as well as a cohort-specific digestive subtype.' Methods: 'Initially, we included patients diagnosed with both MCI and AD. Subsequently, we excluded patients whose first AD onset time or dementia onset time preceded the MCI onset time.' (so the cohort is converters only). Results: 'the Kaplan-Meier curve demonstrated a significant difference in AD diagnosis rate among different subphenotypes (p value = 0.001)'. Introduction: 'out of the five subphenotypes identified in INSIGHT data, four are consistent across the validation cohorts'. Limitations: 'First, the absence of biological data, such as biomarkers or genetic data, constraints biological interpretability. Second, varying cohort demographics could introduce noise into subphenotypes. Last, the lack of specificity of diagnoses can lead to incomplete or inaccurate records, potentially biasing findings.' Assessment: the study shows structured, comorbidity-defined heterogeneity in the EHR course and in time to AD, among ICD-coded US converters. It has no non-converters, tests no prognostic threshold, and does not compare a subtype-aware prognostic model with a homogeneous one. So it does not test a held prior, and the record's clinical_implication and 'directly and strongly disproved' go beyond the PDF.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'DEMOTE:strawman ... Demote to proposed; record P-103 subphenotypes as a consensus/complementary finding on heterogeneity.' The second half of the recommendation is already done: P-103 is a supporter of VF-14 in data/consensus.json, and VF-14 carries the finding into Section 4.6, so demotion loses no evidence. The 2026-09-15 model second reader proposed a rescope ('can be modelled as one homogeneous course'). That wording describes practice (P-179), and P-103 does not test it, so it does not rescue the record.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-103 has 3,952 AD patients with prior MCI across three US EHR cohorts, with external replication cohorts. Its only discrimination figures are for predicting subphenotype membership: accuracy 0.72/0.71/0.86 and AUC 0.90/0.91/0.71, all below 0.97. Registry Best_Metric is 'not reported'.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: The challenger confirms the auditor. Every quoted passage from P-103 and P-179 is in the re-extracted PDFs. The prior is not attested. The only statement about practice is P-179's (conversion models have not considered heterogeneity), made in a paper that treats heterogeneity as known. P-103 would not test that statement anyway, because it compares no homogeneous and subtype-aware prognostic models. The evidence is real but covers converters only, is ICD-coded and is observational, and the clinical implication goes beyond it. The finding already lives in VF-14. Demote.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: EEG monitoring in MCI is typically used to detect broad functional changes (alpha slowing, connectivity). The 33% prevalence refutes the categorical 'spikes absent in MCI without seizures'; the decline/conversion associations are correlational (causality unclear per the paper), not causal.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Resting-EEG MCI biomarkers are conventionally sought in the theta (4-8 Hz) and alpha (8-13 Hz) bands; high-gamma (30-100 Hz) connectivity is examined less often (though not assumed irrelevant - substantial prior gamma literature exists).
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-368 studied resting EEG gamma-range (30–100 Hz) functional connectivity in 21 aMCI patients vs 62 cognitively normal controls. Using partial coherence (PCOH) to factor out global connectivity effects, the paper found that gamma-1 (30–50 Hz) and gamma-2 (50–100 Hz) connectivity was significantly elevated in MCI patients in central electrode regions, in both eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Crucially, this was only detectable with PCOH — standard coherence (COH) missed the effect, which explains why prior work using standard methods did not observe it.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: EEG gamma-band partial-coherence connectivity may add complementary biomarker signal beyond theta/alpha, but the small sample (N=21 aMCI) requires replication.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: G5 EXCLUDED: strawman - substantial prior gamma-EEG literature exists, so "gamma irrelevant" is not a dominant assumption. Real contribution is methodological (partial coherence needed), a methods-note, not an invalidation.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: none found for the prior as written (MRI brain volumetry, particularly hippocampal volume, as 'the best available single-modality prognostic biomarker for MCI conversion to dementia'; 'simpler non-invasive alternatives are assumed to be less accurate'). Searched summaries.md with regexes for hippocampal/medial-temporal volume or atrophy near most (widely|commonly|established|validated|sensitive|informative)/best/strongest/gold standard/primary/hallmark/sufficient/earliest/first affected, and full PDF text (PyPDF2, own extraction) of P-50, P-99, P-224, P-570, P-581, P-587, P-595, P-672, P-1066, P-1079 (duplicate of P-155), P-1101, P-51, P-52, P-66, P-177, P-182, P-245, P-432, P-460, P-478, P-518, P-560, P-584, P-933. Also searched summaries.md for best/strongest/most accurate/gold standard + MRI/prognostic/conversion. The corpus states the contrary. P-224, the anchor itself, says in its PDF discussion: 'To date, there is no single biomarker with a high sensitivity and specificity for predicting progression from MCI to dementia', citing a Cochrane review in which hippocampal or whole-brain volume 'showed a wide range of sensitivities (28%-100%) and specificities (41%-100%)'. P-581 says hippocampal volume 'has limitations regarding the progression from MCI to AD'. P-224's introduction frames the CCM-versus-MRI comparison as the authors' own prior finding ('CCM had a better diagnostic capability for identifying people with MCI compared to MRI brain volumetry'), not as a field prior that MRI is best. The nearest attested comparative statement (P-177: hippocampal volume 'the best predictor of incident MCI within 2 years' among FDG-PET and MRI measures) concerns progression from cognitively unimpaired to MCI within imaging, not MCI-to-dementia against non-imaging alternatives. P-672 ('The hippocampus volume could predict the disease conversion from MCI to AD') attests predictive value, not superiority. The prior is also outside KA-12, which is a within-structural-MRI regional prior.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: P-224 PDF (C:/Users/aryas/Downloads/PAPERINGO/downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/PMID_36852724_ACN3-10-599.pdf): 107 MCI (ICD-10 F06.7, Qatar memory clinic, 51% diabetic), 33 progressed over a median 2.4 years. Table 2 AUCs: 'Hippocampus, ICV% 78 (67-89)', 'Whole brain, ICV% 78 (66-91)', 'CNFD 74 (64-85)', 'CNFL 73 (63-84)', 'CNBD 71 (61-82)'. Accuracy at Youden cut-offs is 69 and 68% for MRI vs 75, 75 and 72% for CCM. The same table ranks hippocampal volume first among the 13 MRI volumetric measures (entorhinal cortex AUC 58, p=0.24). Text: 'CCM measures had a higher prognostic accuracy for identifying participants who progressed to dementia compared to hippocampus and whole brain volume (72%-75% vs 68%-69%)'. No statistical comparison of AUCs or accuracies is reported. Adjusted for age and MoCA: CNFD OR 6.1 (1.6-23.8), CNBD 4.1 (1.2-14.2), 'hippocampus (3.7, 95% CI: 0.6-22.5, p=0.16)'. The hippocampal result is an underpowered null (OR 6.4, 1.4-30.0, before the age/MoCA adjustment), not evidence of no prognostic value. 'missing MRI data were coded as unknown (n=28, 26.2%)', so MRI and CCM were not compared on the same 107 people. Authors: 'Further work is required to validate the predictive ability of CCM compared to other established biomarkers of dementia'. The record's 'CCM (72-75%) modestly edged MRI (68-69%)' omits that these are cut-off accuracies and that the AUCs favour MRI. Its clinical_implication ('Eye clinics could potentially serve as accessible MCI triage points without brain imaging') is not in the PDF, where the authors propose using CCM's negative predictive value to identify low-risk patients and to enrich trials.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-12, set assumption_id=KA-12, keep strength 'moderate', correct registry Modality to corneal confocal microscopy. The KA-12 link is wrong (KA-12 is hippocampal primacy within structural MRI; IA-21 is a cross-modality prognostic hierarchy), and 'keep moderate' does not survive the PDF (the AUCs favour MRI; the accuracy difference is untested). The registry correction is right and independent of this verdict: the P-224 registry row reads Modality 'Retinal imaging', but CCM images the corneal sub-basal nerve plexus (anterior segment); apply it at the next registry freeze. Drop IA-21 from KA-12.currently_invalidated_by.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged: AUCs 0.71-0.78 and cut-off accuracies 0.68-0.75 in a 107-participant longitudinal cohort with no external cohort, far below the 0.97 threshold.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Demote. (1) The prior is not attested: no corpus study says MRI volumetry is the best single prognostic marker for MCI-to-dementia or that simpler alternatives are less accurate, and the anchor study itself says no single biomarker is adequate. (2) The evidence does not test a hierarchy. On AUC, MRI volumetry is numerically ahead (78% vs 71-74%). CCM leads only on in-sample cut-off accuracy, by 3-7 points, with no test. The adjusted-OR contrast is a difference in significance driven by a wide hippocampal CI, and a quarter of the MRI data are missing. Parity in one small cohort cannot overturn or bound an unattested prior. (3) The 2026-09-15 second reader admitted it against the summary block, which reports only the accuracy figures; the PDF reverses the AUC ordering. The manuscript already says 'volumetry had the numerically higher AUCs', so the record lags the manuscript. CHALLENGER (own re-extraction of the P-224 PDF): demote confirmed and Table 2 verified. P-224 is, if anything, within-MRI evidence for hippocampal primacy (hippocampal volume has the highest AUC of the 13 MRI measures), not evidence against it. The pending supporters (P-581, P-584, P-587, P-1066, P-1101) would anchor a different claim (within-MRI regional prognostic primacy). They cannot be moved under IA-21 as a rescope; if wanted, they belong in a new, separately adjudicated record.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: The standard clinical model treats SCD as a preclinical stage of MCI, and therefore assumes that individuals with SCD should show early structural brain changes on MRI, particularly in hippocampal and parahippocampal regions, detectable with sensitive enough methods.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-142 (MIND-China, N=1072 dementia-free; 243 SCD, 246 MCI) found via VBM that MCI had reduced GMV in bilateral parahippocampus, hippocampus, and fusiform, while SCD showed no significant GMV difference from normal cognition (P>0.05). However, the SAME study's ROI-wise SBM analysis found SCD WAS significantly associated with cortical thinning in the right paracentral sulcus, left caudal middle frontal gyrus, and left entorhinal cortex (P<0.05).
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: GMV/VBM alone may be insensitive to SCD-stage structural change, but SBM cortical-thickness analysis detected significant SCD alterations (incl. entorhinal cortex); this does NOT show structural MRI is uninformative for SCD - it argues for modality/method choice. The prior belief (SCD shows early detectable structural change) is therefore NOT invalidated.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: Human G5 2026-06-26: STRONG. Clean SCD GMV null in well-powered cohort N=1072. | G5 REJECT 2026-07-29 (AI-adversarial): SCD-SBM null was fabricated; P-142 found significant SCD cortical thinning (entorhinal), so the belief is SUPPORTED not disproved. Record corrected to the narrow true finding and marked rejected.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: REJECTED at G5: the record fabricated a matching SCD cortical-thinning null. The invalidation does not hold; at most VBM/GMV specifically is insensitive to SCD here.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Default Mode Network disruption is assumed to be the dominant and consistent resting-state fMRI biomarker for MCI, detectable across all patients and all dynamic states. This is VF-04 in your verified consensus.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-49 studied dynamic functional connectivity states in 82 MCI patients and 85 controls using rs-fMRI. The paper identified three distinct DFC states. Crucially, State 2 showed no significant community structure differences between MCI and controls — it was the state with highest DMN-like activity. The significant MCI-related disruptions were concentrated in States 1 and 3, affecting frontal, temporal, and occipital/precuneus-related nodes rather than the DMN core.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: REJECTED - paper does not support this implication.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: Human G5 2026-06-26 REJECTED after source-PDF check (1-s2.0-S0306452224000897-main.pdf). The State-2-vs-States-1&3 community finding is REAL (paper: 'high similarity between the two groups in state 2, with no significant differences in optimal community quantity'; states 1 and 3 differ). BUT the DMN framing that the IA hangs on is fabricated/contradicted: (a) the word 'highest' never appears re DMN - State 2 is merely the most PREVALENT state (47.85% MCI / 42.90% NC), not the 'highest DMN-like activity' state; (b) DMN ('Default mode') nodes are among the DISRUPTED nodes in ALL three states (S1: ACG.R, PCUN; S2: SFGmed.L, PCG.L, ITG.R; S3: PCG, PCUN.R, MTG.R), so the paper does NOT show the DMN core is spared - directly contradicting 'rather than the DMN core'; (c) precuneus (PCUN) is labelled Default mode in this paper, not a non-DMN region. Therefore P-49 does NOT invalidate DMN dominance (VF-04); it shows state-dependence WITHIN a picture where DMN is still disrupted. Clinical implication ('artifacts of static analysis') is pure agent extrapolation absent from the paper. Verified consensus VF-04 stands unchanged.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT) is reduced in MCI relative to cognitively normal controls and has been proposed as a retinal structural biomarker of MCI (corpus meta-analysis P-830: pooled SMD -0.462, p = 0.020, k = 4).
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-363 (Robbins 2021; prospective cross-sectional EDI-OCT; 67 AD/74 MCI/137 controls, 503 eyes; diabetes, glaucoma and retinal pathology excluded): after adjustment for age, sex and visual acuity, SFCT did not differ between MCI and controls (beta -5.90 um, 95% CI -27.89 to 16.08, p = .599), whereas the choroidal vascularity index was lower in MCI (beta -0.58, p = .002). SFCT was thinner in AD than in MCI (beta -29.00, p = .017) and than in controls before adjustment (p = .001; adjusted beta -26.97, p = .054), so the AD comparison does not contradict thinning. Single cohort; axial length not measured.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: In one adjusted memory-clinic cohort SFCT alone did not separate MCI from controls while choroidal vascularity did. A corpus meta-analysis reports SFCT thinning in MCI (P-830, k = 4), although that meta-analysis counts this same cohort among its included studies. The result therefore bounds rather than refutes the prior, and SFCT should not be relied on as a standalone MCI marker until the finding is replicated with adjustment for age and axial length.

P-830 (Ge et al. 2021, Ageing Research Reviews systematic review and meta-analysis), PDF abstract (extract glyphs decoded: 'D' = '<', invisible glyph = '='): 'Compared with healthy controls, patients with MCI also had lower thickness of pRNFL (SMD -0.324, p < 0.001), total macular (SMD -0.302, p < 0.001), and subfoveal choroid (SMD -0.462, p = 0.020).' Discussion: 'The thinner retina and choroid, reduced complexity of vessels, and reduced blood flow were consistently detected in the MCI stage compared with healthy controls' (Table 1, MCI choroidal thickness: OCT k = 4, n = 427, limitation codes a, c, d). Also P-363's own introduction (PDF pp. 359-360): 'A recent meta-analysis found that SFCT was significantly decreased in patients with AD compared with that of control subjects. ... SFCT was also shown to decrease in subjects with mild cognitive impairment (MCI)'; and P-1317 (Joseph et al. 2024; PDF at downloads/3. Molecular, Genetic and Fluid Biomarkers/1-s2.0-S2666914524000162-main.pdf, which is missing from data/paper_pdf_map.json): 'Other studies analyzing the choroid have reported decreased subfoveal choroidal thickness in both MCI [35: Bulut et al. 2016] and AD when compared with that of controls.' The registered prior KA-20 as written ('Retinal/choroidal markers change in a fixed direction with MCI: the choroid thins (SFCT) and retinal vessels become more tortuous') is NOT attested: its assumed_since reads 'Corpus prior implied by the invalidated-assumption records listed in currently_invalidated_by', so it was built from IA-27 and IA-46 themselves, and no corpus study states its tortuosity half. CHALLENGER ADDITION: P-830 is not fully independent of the disproving cohort. Its reference list contains 'Robbins, C.B., Grewal, D.S., Thompson, A.C., Powers, J.H., Soundararajan, S., Koo, H.Y., Yoon, S.P., Polascik, B.W., Liu, A., Agrawal, R., Fekrat, S., 2020. Choroidal structural analysis in alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, and cognitively healthy controls. Am. J. Ophthalmol.' (= P-363). Its MCI Table 1 row 'Choroidal angioarchitecture OCTA (k 1, n 204) ... Greater total choroidal area and luminal area, lower choroidal vascularity index' reports P-363's findings, and its text reads 'thinning of the choroid via OCTA (Robbins et al., 2020) ... The thinning of the choroid could also be detected in MCI'. So P-363 was among P-830's included studies and may sit in the k = 4 SFCT pool. P-830 still attests that the field holds the prior, and the P-363 introduction and P-1317 state it independently. But P-830 is not an independent counterweight to P-363.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: Source PDF: C:/Users/aryas/Downloads/PAPERINGO/downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/1-s2.0-S0002939420305584-main.pdf (Robbins et al., Am J Ophthalmol 2021;223:359-367). Abstract: 'Prospective cross-sectional study.' 'Participants included 67 patients (112 eyes) with AD, 74 patients (143 eyes) with MCI, and 137 (248 eyes) control subjects. Subjects with diabetes, glaucoma, or retinal pathology were excluded.' 'CVI was significantly lower in patients with MCI (beta = -0.58; p = .002) compared with control subjects. SFCT was similar among patients with AD and MCI and control subjects on multivariable analysis (p > .05).' Table 2 (GEE; multivariable model adjusted for age, sex and VA), SFCT: MCI vs controls univariate -10.73 (-32.66 to 11.20), p = .338; multivariate -5.90 (-27.89 to 16.08), p = .599. AD vs controls univariate -43.84 (-68.68 to -18.99), p = .001; multivariate -26.97 (-54.43 to 0.49), p = .054. AD vs MCI multivariate -29.00 (-52.84 to -5.17), p = .017. Means 230.19/262.59/274.12 um (SD 86.38/72.88/98.26). Results: 'SFCT was not significantly different between subjects with MCI and control subjects'. Limitation: 'Axial length measurement was not routinely performed as part of this study'. Reading: the study tests the prior directly in MCI. P-830's pooled SMD of -0.462 corresponds to about 34-45 um of thinning at these SDs, which lies outside the adjusted MCI interval, so this is an informative single-cohort null. The AD result points toward thinning (adjusted p = .054, unadjusted p = .001), so the 'MCI/AD' wording must be restricted to MCI. P-163 (same trial NCT03233646) is corroboration only and not independent. The clause 'prior SFCT literature is itself mixed' is not in the PDF: a search for conflict/mixed/inconsistent/controvers/contradict finds nothing, and the introduction cites only studies that report thinning. The clause traces to the P-363 summary block ('What has been done?': 'SFCT alone has been studied in AD with conflicting results').
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-20 ... set assumption_id=KA-20; repair the P-363 sample-size field to 278 - 67 AD/74 MCI/137 controls and re-check registry Sample_N_Approx.' The sample-size half is correct and still undone: the block reads '150 (target) - STUDY PROTOCOL; target enrollment 50 DS/50 MCI/50 HC' and the registry reads '150 (target)', whereas the PDF gives 278 participants (503 eyes). The KA-20 half does not hold: it fuses two unrelated direction claims, choroidal thinning and vessel tortuosity, and it was built from the IA records themselves, so the reviewer supplied it. Register instead a narrow prior, 'SFCT is reduced in MCI relative to cognitively normal controls', attested by P-830, P-363's introduction and P-1317, and anchor IA-27 to it as a bounded record.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-363 is a group-comparison study (GEE, 503 eyes of 278 participants) and reports no AUC or accuracy.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: The SFCT-in-MCI prior is attested in three places: P-830's abstract and Discussion, P-363's own introduction (a statement of the prior literature, not the study's hypothesis), and P-1317 (citing Bulut 2016). P-363 tests the prior directly in MCI with a sound design (masked double grading plus an adjudicator, adjusted GEE), and its adjusted interval excludes the pooled meta-analytic effect size. It is not a flagged study. The record overreaches in three ways. It pools AD with MCI as showing no difference, although AD is thinner at p = .054 adjusted, p = .001 unadjusted, and significantly thinner than MCI. Its prior says 'consistently'. And it asserts a 'mixed' prior literature that the PDF does not state; that clause comes from an unsupported block field. So the record is rescoped to an MCI-only bounded record. Challenger refinements: P-830 includes P-363 among its sources, so the clinical implication no longer presents P-830 as an independent counterweight. Data defects: the P-363 block's sample-size field describes a Down-syndrome protocol (50 DS/50 MCI/50 HC), which looks like text carried over from another block, and its 'What has been done?' field contains the unsupported 'conflicting results' claim, so the whole block needs re-checking against the PDF. The registry Sample_N_Approx should be 278. P-1317's PDF is missing from paper_pdf_map.json. KA-20 should not be confirmed as a composite prior.
