readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: NOT attested. No corpus study states that amyloid PET improves ML prediction of PD-MCI over clinical or gait features. None states that the field expects amyloid to drive PD-MCI in a way that would make PET add information. The disproving study itself describes the field as sceptical. P-221 PDF abstract p.1: 'although low cerebrospinal fluid levels of amyloid-β42 have been found to predict cognitive decline in PD, hitherto PET imaging of amyloid-β (Aβ) failed to consistently demonstrate the association between Aβ plaques deposition and mild cognitive impairment in PD (PD-MCI)'. Introduction p.2: 'amyloid-β (Aβ) Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging studies have reported conflicting results (17-21), thus failing to consistently demonstrate an association between Aβ plaques deposition and cognitive dysfunction in PD'. Discussion p.7: 'our findings are consistent with recent research that equally did not support an association between increased Aβ deposition and cognitive decline in PD (17,18,44)'. P-525 (Garon 2022, P-221's ref 17; block): 'There is uncertainty about the role of beta-amyloid co-pathology ... Prior PD imaging studies of amyloid yielded mixed results in small, poorly characterized cohorts'. The introduction's 'both cognition and gait dysfunction in PD might share common underlying pathological mechanisms which, at least in part, could be related to Aβ pathology' is the authors' own hypothesis, not a statement that the field holds amyloid PET to improve prediction. The record itself concedes that 'the field's amyloid-PET-helps assumption is strongest for AD-spectrum MCI, not PD-MCI'. The 2026-09-15 second reader grounded attestation in 'the paper's stated aim was to "test amyloid PET utility for PD-MCI prediction"'. That phrase is the summary block's wording, not the paper's. The PDF aim (p.2) is: '(1) identifying the top features associated with PD-MCI among those commonly reported in previous research; and (2) detecting a machine learning algorithm able to distinguish PD patients with MCI from those without'. Search method: summaries.md regex for Parkinson/PD-MCI within 200 characters of amyloid, in both orders (P-221, P-322, P-525, P-590, P-595, P-651, P-659, P-804, P-852, P-985, P-1001, P-1039, P-1398); P-525, P-1001 and P-1398 blocks read; P-221 PDF read in full (the challenger re-extracted it).
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: PDF: downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/PMID_36468069_fneur-13-1010147.pdf (Amboni et al. 2022, Front Neurol 13:1010147). (1) The models are not nested and are not run on the same sample. Methods p.4: '1. Model 1 included age, clinical characteristics (hallucinations/psychosis, depressed mood, anxiety, apathy, sleep problems, FOG), and gait features; 2. Model 2 included quantitative PET features and the top five features of Model 1' and 'A 10-fold cross-validation was used for the first model, while a leave-one-out technique was used for the second model, considering the sample size.' Table 4 headers read 'Model1 (n=75)', 'Model2A (n=36)', 'Model2B (n=36)'. No model is fitted on the top-five features alone in the 36-patient PET subgroup, so PET's incremental value is never isolated. (2) Table 4 figures: Model 1 SVM accuracy 80.0, sensitivity 72.7, specificity 85.7, AUC 0.792; Model 2B SVM 75.0 / 73.7 / 76.5 / 0.751; Model 2A SVM 72.2 / 73.7 / 70.6 / 0.721. The PET models' sensitivity is equal to or higher than Model 1's. No test of difference is reported, and at n=36 a single patient moves accuracy by 2.8 points. (3) Univariate result, p.6: 'A subgroup of PD patients, namely 36 subjects, including 19 PD-MCI and 17 noPD-MCI, underwent amyloid PET imaging ... the two groups did not significantly differ on amyloid PET tracer retention for all brain areas under examination.' (4) Authors' limitation, p.9: 'the small sample size of amyloid PET data could have influenced algorithms predictions of Model 2, thus assuming that the present findings should be confirmed with larger samples.' (5) Authors' conclusion, p.10: 'gray matter amyloid PET tracer retention does not appear to increase prediction'. Record text against the PDF: 'direct head-to-head comparison' is wrong, because sample (75 vs 36), feature set and CV scheme all differ. '>80% accuracy' is wrong: accuracy was 80.0% (specificity 85.7%). 'Often weakened' rests on lower point estimates with no significance test, in a 36-patient leave-one-out design. The record's own caveat ('better read as insufficient power to detect a modest PET benefit') concedes that the study cannot disprove the prior. (6) Challenger addition, PDF p.6: the 'top five features chosen from Model 1' are all gait measures: 'Step length (m), 9.15%; Cycle length (%height), 7.54%; Step length variability (m), 7.38%; Mean velocity (m/s), 7.28%; Stance phase, 7.14%'. So Model 2 is PET plus five gait features. It drops age and every clinical item, which confirms that the Model 1 vs Model 2 contrast does not isolate PET's incremental value.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: The DEMOTE recommendation is right and its reason holds. An underpowered null (PET subgroup n=36) cannot invalidate a prior. And narrowing the prior to PD-MCI moves it to where, by the paper's own introduction, the field does not hold it. The PDF adds two further reasons. First, the Model 1 vs Model 2 contrast differs in n, CV scheme and feature set, so it does not measure incremental value at all. Second, the corpus (P-221's introduction, P-525) contradicts the prior rather than attesting it. The 2026-09-15 blinded model second reader's 'admit' does not survive, because its attestation quotes the summary block's aim, not the paper's. The suggested fallback, keeping P-221 as a complementary finding under the PD-MCI amyloid cluster (IA-41/KA-17), has no host: IA-41 was itself demoted in batch A04 of this round. P-221's univariate SUV null (19 vs 17) is also too small to support a CF, which would in any case need its own admission.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. Best internal result is SVM Model 1: accuracy 80.0%, AUC 0.792 (10-fold CV, n=75). The PET models reach AUC ≤ 0.751 (leave-one-out, n=36). No external cohort; hyperparameters were tuned with an 'Optimization Parameter Loop' and no nested CV is reported. All figures are below the 0.97 threshold, so the demotion does not rest on the flag.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Demote. The prior (in PD-MCI, amyloid PET improves ML prediction over clinical and gait features) is not attested. The disproving paper's own abstract and introduction say amyloid PET has 'failed to consistently demonstrate' any PD-MCI association, and P-525 describes the literature as mixed and uncertain. So the result confirms the field's scepticism rather than overturning a held belief. The evidence also does not test incremental value. Model 2 is not Model 1 plus PET: it is PET plus Model 1's five top gait features, with age and all clinical items dropped, fitted on a different 36-patient subgroup with leave-one-out rather than 10-fold CV. No model on the same features without PET is fitted in that subgroup, and no difference is tested. The null is underpowered, which the authors and the record both concede. The second reader's admit rested on summary-block wording, not the PDF. No narrower form is both attested and tested, so the record is not rescoped.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: The hippocampus (medial temporal lobe) is the most informative single brain region for structural-MRI detection of MCI and for predicting progression from normal cognition to MCI.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-570 (Chen et al., Alzheimer's & Dementia; ADNI n=1,319 training, independent in-house cohort n=308 testing) compared a cerebellar model (lobule radiomic features plus cerebellar structural-network properties) with a hippocampal-subfield radiomic model built with the same feature-selection and machine-learning procedure. For MCI versus normal cognition the cerebellar model outperformed the hippocampal model on the independent test set (AUC 0.864 vs 0.715; DeLong p<0.01). For progression from normal cognition to MCI over six years (ADNI only, 371 participants, 137 progressors; features chosen by stepwise selection, no independent test cohort) the cerebellar model had the higher AUC (0.818, 95% CI 0.733-0.904, vs 0.659, 95% CI 0.547-0.77; no between-model test reported) and separated risk groups (HR 4.75, log-rank p<0.001) where the hippocampal model did not (log-rank p>0.05). SCOPE: the hippocampal model had the higher AUCs for AD versus normal cognition and AD versus MCI, significantly so only in the training set (test AUC 0.899 vs 0.854, p=0.200; 0.832 vs 0.662, p=0.157). The detection comparison was not symmetric: the cerebellar model drew on 2,730 candidate radiomic features plus cerebellar network properties, the hippocampal model on 630 radiomic features with no network construction described. Bounded, not refuted: a single retrospective two-cohort radiomics study in which only the MCI-versus-normal-cognition advantage was tested and significant.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Early-MCI detection pipelines should not assume that hippocampal features are the best single-region input: in one two-cohort study a cerebellar radiomic-network model detected MCI better than a hippocampal radiomic model. The result awaits multi-site replication with harmonised acquisition and a feature-matched comparison, and does not displace hippocampal features at the AD stages.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-570 summary/registry: MCI-vs-NC test AUC 0.864 (cerebellar) vs 0.715 (hippocampal), DeLong p<0.01; NC->MCI conversion cerebellar 0.818, clinical 0.666, hippocampal 0.659, combined 0.852; Cox HR 4.75. Hippocampal wins AD-vs-NC (0.899) and AD-vs-MCI (0.832).
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: Batch P-570..P-579 (2026-07-28). Adversarially source-verified SUPPORTED (high): all six figures match Table 2 / Results of pdf_extract_570. Claim correctly scoped to early MCI (hippocampus still superior at AD stages). Relates to IA-01 (P-50) and IA-21 (P-224). PENDING human G5 confirmation before status flip. | G5 CONFIRM-with-caveat 2026-07-29 (AI-adversarial): grounding verified vs summary; overclaim softened; scope/power caveat added.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Single retrospective two-cohort radiomics study (first head-to-head of its kind). Superiority scoped to EARLY MCI detection / NC-to-MCI conversion only (hippocampus remains superior at AD stages, as the record states). Associational; radiomics sensitive to scanner/segmentation; external test set modest (n=308). Needs prospective multi-site harmonised replication.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_delegated_verdict_2026_08_22: CONFIRM. All six benchmark figures, DeLong significance, Cox HR 4.75, the AD-stage scoping and both cohort Ns (1319 ADNI + 308 Dalian) verified verbatim in measured fields. Claude delegated judgment 2026-08-22 (operator-delegated resolution of all pending-review records; every supporter independently re-verified against its summaries.md block by a fresh verification agent this session).
invalidated_assumptions.prior_audit_2026_08_29: ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-12. Set assumption_id=KA-12 and make P-570 the anchor entry in KA-12.currently_invalidated_by; keep the 'early MCI only; hippocampus still wins at AD stages' scope.
invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief_pre_2026_09_26: The hippocampus (medial temporal lobe) is the optimal single brain region for early MCI detection and MCI-conversion prediction; other regions such as the cerebellum (traditionally viewed as motor-only) add little independent signal.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it_pre_2026_09_26: P-570 (Chen et al., Alzheimer's & Dementia 2025; ADNI n=1319 + independent in-house n=308) built cerebellar-lobule radiomic + structural-connectome models and benchmarked them head-to-head against hippocampal models. The cerebellar model SIGNIFICANTLY outperformed the hippocampal model for MCI-vs-NC detection (test AUC 0.864 vs 0.715; DeLong p<0.01) and for NC-to-MCI conversion (AUC 0.818 vs 0.659; combined clinical-radiomic 0.852; cerebellar Cox HR 4.75, hippocampal model not separating risk groups). SCOPE: the hippocampal model still outperformed the cerebellar model for AD-vs-NC and AD-vs-MCI (AUC up to ~0.90-0.998), so the invalidation is bounded to EARLY MCI detection/conversion, not the whole AD continuum.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication_pre_2026_09_26: For early/preclinical MCI detection and conversion-risk stratification, cerebellar radiomic-network features carry independent, sometimes superior signal; early-detection pipelines should not be hippocampus-only. Hippocampal features remain preferred for AD-stage classification.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: Attested in a narrowed form, carried mainly by P-177; the other quotes are supporting only (practice-level or AD-diagnosis statements). PRIMARY: P-177 (C:/Users/aryas/Downloads/PAPERINGO/downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/PMID_33749642_nihms-1843971.pdf, abstract): 'We previously described that among baseline FDG-PET and MRI measures known to be preferentially affected in the preclinical and clinical stages of AD, hippocampal volume was the best predictor of incident MCI within 2 years (79% sensitivity/78% specificity)'. Its summary block frames the study as an attempt 'to improve short-horizon progression prediction beyond standard hippocampal volume metrics', i.e. hippocampal volume is the benchmark to beat. SUPPORTING: P-66 (.../1-s2.0-S0899707124002316-main.pdf, section 2.5): 'the most informative features of the brain images for Alzheimer diagnosis are texture and shape of hippocampus and amygdala regions' (AD diagnosis and two regions, so it supports the hippocampal-radiomics feature family, not single-region primacy for MCI). P-595 (PDF introduction): 'hippocampal volumetry has emerged as a robust MRI biomarker for AD diagnosis', and (discussion) 'Hippocampal atrophy is a significant hallmark of AD neurodegeneration, is widely used in research and clinical diagnosis'. P-581 (PDF): hippocampal volume 'is commonly used in research, trials, and clinical practice'. P-182 (PDF introduction): 'The most widely studied target in AD is the hippocampus (Jack et al. 1992; Fox et al. 1996), and indeed, multiple studies have reported hippocampal volume loss in MCI relative to controls'. These last four describe standard practice rather than a comparative belief and would not attest the prior on their own. NOT attested, and dropped: KA-12's registered 'sufficient ... other regions and measures add little', and the record's 'cerebellum (traditionally viewed as motor-only)' clause, which P-570 itself states only as superseded ('Traditionally associated with motor control, the cerebellum is now recognized for its critical involvement in cognitive processes'). Contrary statements in the corpus show the primacy view is held but contested, which fits a bounded, not refuted, outcome: P-50 (multi-region atrophy); P-581 ('it has limitations regarding the progression from MCI to AD'); P-595 ('in early AD, MTL atrophy is often subtle and not reliably detected by conventional MTA ratings'). Search: the challenger's own regex sweep of summaries.md (hippocampal/medial temporal within 160 characters of most widely/commonly/established/validated/sensitive/informative/reliable/used, best, gold standard, strongest, primary marker, earliest, first affected, well established, reference standard, most studied; 49 hits, P-369 excluded as a known fabricated block), plus the auditor's PDF list; own PyPDF2 extraction of P-570, P-224, P-50, P-99, P-177, P-66, P-182, P-595, P-581 and P-672.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: P-570 PDF (C:/Users/aryas/Downloads/PAPERINGO/downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/PMID_39535490_ALZ-21-e14361 (3).pdf), challenger's own extraction. Cohorts: 'ADNI database ( n=1319, 574 NCs, 530 MCI, and 215 AD patients) and in-house database ( n=308, 102 NCs, 104 MCI, and 102 AD patients'. Comparators: 'we also constructed hippocampal models using the same feature selection and machine learning methods as for the cerebellar models', BUT the candidate pools differ: 'a total of 2730 cerebellar radiomic features ... and 630 hippocampal radiomic features (105 features x2 [1 CA1-3 +1 CA4/DG +1 subiculum])'. Section 2.5 constructs structural networks for the cerebellum only ('nodes represent 26 cerebellar lobules'). The final MCI-vs-NC cerebellar model 'incorporated 16 radiomic features and 1 network property' (AdaBoost), while the hippocampal classification model is radiomic-only (SVM). For the conversion models the paper speaks of 'hippocampal radiomic-network features' (section 2.8), so the asymmetry is stated for detection only. The 105 features per ROI are '18 histogram (first-order) features, 14 shape-based features, and 78 texture-based features'. The PDF does not say volume is among them, so the auditor's '(shape features include volume)' is not in the source, and the comparator should be described as hippocampal-subfield radiomics, not hippocampal volumetry. Table 2 MCI vs NC: cerebellar 'Test set 0.864 0.7921 0.7379 0.8485 (0.7931-0.8991)'; hippocampal 'Training set 0.6866 ... SVM <0.0001', 'Test set 0.7152 0.6733 0.7864 0.5556 (0.6450-0.7854) <0.01' (DeLong). AD vs MCI: hippocampal test 0.8324 vs cerebellar 0.6617, P=0.157. AD vs NC: hippocampal test 0.8985 vs 0.8538, P=0.200. 'the DeLong test validated that the hippocampal models significantly outperformed the cerebellar models for both AD versus NC ( P<0.0001) and AD versus MCI ( P<0.01) in the training sets'. Conversion: 'The NC subjects ( n=371) were followed up for 72 months' (described under ADNI; no follow-up is described for the in-house cohort); 'Using forward stepwise regression, we selected the optimal radiomic and network feature subsets for both cerebellar and hippocampal models'; 'the cerebellar model achieved an AUC of 0.818 (95% Cl: 0.733-0.904), outperforming both the clinical model (AUC =0.666 ...) and the hippocampal model (AUC =0.659, 95% Cl: 0.547-0.77)', with no DeLong test reported and no independent test cohort. Cerebellar 'hazard ratio (HR) of 4.75 (adjusted for age, sex, education, and APOE ) and a log-rank test result of P<0.001', while 'the hippocampal model did not exhibit significant differences between risk subgroups (log-rank test, P>0.05)'; that is a difference in significance, not a test of difference. Discussion: 'when differentiating MCI from NC subjects, the cerebellar model exhibited relatively superior accuracy and robustness compared to the hippocampal model'; 'this study highlights the importance of considering region-specific models when investigating different disease stages'. So the formally tested, externally validated contrast is MCI vs NC only (DeLong p<0.01 on the in-house test set of 206): a cerebellar radiomic-plus-network model against a hippocampal radiomic-only model drawn from under a quarter of the candidate features. The auditor's list of record errors is confirmed: 'SIGNIFICANTLY ... for NC-to-MCI conversion'; 'AUC up to ~0.90-0.998', which quotes training AUCs; and 'independent ... signal', with no incremental test.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-12, set assumption_id=KA-12, make P-570 the anchor entry in KA-12.currently_invalidated_by, keep the 'early MCI only; hippocampus still wins at AD stages' scope. Mostly right: P-570 is a genuine within-study head-to-head test of hippocampal primacy and the early-MCI scope is correct, so the anchor role holds. Two corrections: KA-12's registered wording is not attested and must be narrowed to the comparative-primacy form quoted above, and 'hippocampus still wins at AD stages' overstates, since the hippocampal AD-stage advantage was significant only in training.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. The anchoring figure is an independent-test AUC of 0.864 (registry V3, external in-house cohort n=308); cerebellar training AUC 0.944. The hippocampal comparator's training AUCs of 0.9975 (AD vs MCI) and 0.9979 (AD vs NC) are near-ceiling internal figures on n=1,319 with an external test. They do not anchor the record, but the record should not quote '0.998' as the AD-stage scope (the test AUCs are 0.83 and 0.90).
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Rescope, bounded (auditor's verdict upheld, text tightened). The narrowed prior is attested chiefly by P-177, which states that hippocampal volume was the best of the FDG-PET and MRI predictors of incident MCI and treats it as the standard to beat. P-66, P-595, P-581 and P-182 show that hippocampal measures are the field's standard structural target; they support the comparative form but would not attest it alone. P-570 tests the prior directly, in a designed head-to-head with an independent test cohort and a DeLong test (MCI vs NC, p<0.01). It bounds rather than refutes, for five reasons: it is one study; only the MCI vs NC contrast is tested and significant; the conversion contrast is ADNI-only, stepwise-selected, CI-overlapping and untested; the hippocampal model keeps higher AUCs at the AD stages (non-significant on test); and the detection comparison favoured the cerebellar side, with over four times the candidate features plus network properties the hippocampal side lacked. The record must now state that last point because it bears on how much the inversion means. The challenger considered demotion, on the ground that the best-attested half (NC-to-MCI prediction) is the untested half. But the tested half (MCI detection) rests on the same primacy view (P-177 'preferentially affected ... best predictor', P-595 'robust MRI biomarker for AD diagnosis', P-66 'most informative features'), so the case for survival in bounded form is made. Not performance-flagged (anchoring test AUC 0.864, n=1,319 plus 308 external).

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Event-related-potential (ERP) markers decline monotonically along the SCD -> MCI -> AD continuum, so a worse clinical stage implies more attenuated ERP sensory/cognitive components.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-144 (Vergani et al. 2025; one cross-sectional memory-clinic cohort, N = 178: 119 SCD / 40 MCI / 19 healthy, 115/38/19 after outlier exclusion; ERPs during a sustained visuo-attentive task): the authors report attenuated sensory (P1, N1, P2) and cognitive (P300, P600, P900) components in SCD relative to healthy subjects, with no further attenuation in MCI. On every amplitude feature except the P300 peak the MCI mean was at or above the SCD mean, and no feature was significantly lower in MCI than in SCD. Four features were higher in MCI than in SCD (P2 integral p = 0.014, P1 peak p = 0.027, N1 integral p = 0.036, P600 peak p = 0.037; Bonferroni-adjusted across the three group contrasts, not across the 12 features), giving a non-monotonic HS > MCI > SCD ordering for those features; the paper's aggregate analyses were weaker (normalised integral SCD vs MCI a trend, p = 0.068; normalised peak p = 1.0; percentage-deviation contrast significant only for the P2 integral). The P300 peak followed the monotonic ordering (healthy > SCD > MCI, no step significant), as the authors note. Task-accuracy means fell from healthy to SCD to MCI, with only SCD vs MCI significant. Caveats: small healthy group; MCI about seven years older and less educated, with features age-regressed in a sample where age and group are confounded; groups defined clinically and mostly ATN-negative where CSF/PET was available (46/58, including 17/24 MCI); no AD group.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: In the early clinical continuum (healthy, SCD, MCI), not every ERP component can be read as a linear severity index: in one cross-sectional, largely biomarker-negative cohort, several early sensory features and the P600 peak were more attenuated in SCD than in MCI, while the P300 peak followed severity. Interpretation should be stage-aware and component-specific. 'Compensatory recruitment' is the authors' interpretation of the amplitude increase, not a demonstrated mechanism, and the per-feature effects are modest and uncorrected across features; longitudinal, biomarker-staged replication with a larger control group is needed.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-576 summary: SCD attenuation vs HS (sensory+cognitive components); MCI compensatory enhancement reversing SCD decline -> non-monotonic pattern. Caveat: small HS group (n=19); direct SCD-vs-MCI contrasts mostly trend-level, P600 the clearest reversal.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: Batch P-570..P-579 (2026-07-28). Adversarially source-verified SUPPORTED (high): non-monotonic V-shape confirmed in abstract/S3.3/S3.4/Fig1E of pdf_extract_576; behavioural decline monotonic (dissociation). Relates to IA-28 (P-362, N400). Small-HS caveat noted. PENDING human G5. | G5 CONFIRM-with-caveat 2026-07-29 (AI-adversarial): grounding verified vs summary; overclaim softened; scope/power caveat added.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Single cross-sectional cohort (V2), small imbalanced healthy group (n=19; ~6:1 vs SCD). The non-monotonic finding is clearest/robust for P600, trend-level for other components; 'compensatory recruitment' is an interpretation of amplitude increase, not a demonstrated mechanism. Belief challenged/not-supported rather than definitively 'disproved'.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_delegated_verdict_2026_08_22: CONFIRM with provenance caveat: the core non-monotonic V-shape and group Ns (119/40/19) are summary-grounded, but the P600-clearest/trend-level and behaviour-monotonic clauses are EXTRACT-sourced (pdf_extract_576) and not verifiable from the summary block as written. Claude delegated judgment 2026-08-22 (operator-delegated resolution of all pending-review records; every supporter independently re-verified against its summaries.md block by a fresh verification agent this session).

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief_pre_2026_09_26: Event-related-potential (ERP) markers decline monotonically along the SCD -> MCI -> AD continuum, so a worse clinical stage implies more attenuated ERP sensory/cognitive components.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it_pre_2026_09_26: P-576 (Vergani 2025; N=178: 119 SCD/40 MCI/19 HS, cross-sectional): SCD showed attenuation of sensory (P1/N1/P2) and cognitive (P300/P600/P900) ERP components vs healthy; MCI did not decline further - instead ERP components showed a compensatory-type enhancement (clearest and statistically robust for P600, trend-level for other components) that reversed the SCD downward trend, producing a non-monotonic (V-shaped) ERP pattern across HS-SCD-MCI, while behaviour declined monotonically - dissociating ERP amplitude from clinical severity in this single cross-sectional cohort (small HS group, n=19).
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication_pre_2026_09_26: ERP amplitude may reflect compensatory neural recruitment and cannot be read as a monotonic severity index across the early continuum; interpret stage-aware. Based on a small cross-sectional sample; needs longitudinal/larger-control confirmation.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: Attested. In its general form the prior is stated by the disproving study itself (P-144, the canonical ID of the Vergani 2025 paper; P-576 is its dedup stub). From the Conclusion of PDF downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S2213158225000300-main.pdf: 'ERP dynamics, in particular, revealed critical discontinuities in cognitive decline, challenging the assumption of a linear progression from health to pathology. These deviations could reflect compensatory mechanisms and cerebral resilience, disrupting expected ERP monotonicity. Our methodology captures these nonlinear changes, offering insights beyond standard markers like amplitude attenuation or latency slowing'. Fig. 1E caption: 'Dashed line traces the hypothetical monotonic trend which has been altered by the features values.' An independent corpus study instantiates the monotonic expectation for P3: P-489 (PDF 1-s2.0-S2405844023028487-main.pdf) reports 'there was a gradual decrease in the amplitude and increase in the latency of the P3 potential from the HC group to the AD group'. P-28 treats P300 as a progression marker: 'N200 and P300 latency have been considered as promising biomarkers in the early diagnosis and progression assessment of AD and MCI'. So the prior is not a strawman, but the only corpus statement of it for all components is the disproving study's own framing, which the master already discloses for most priors ('most were registered from the contradicting records themselves').
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: PDF: downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S2213158225000300-main.pdf (Vergani et al. 2025, NeuroImage: Clinical 45:103760; identical DOI to the P-576 stub). Abstract: 'SCD patients exhibited significant attenuation in both sensory (P1, N1, P2) and cognitive (P300, P600, P900) components compared to HS, with cognitive components showing performance-related gains. In contrast, MCI patients did not show a further decrease in any ERP component compared to SCD. Instead, they exhibited compensatory enhancements, reversing the downward trend observed in SCD.' Table 2 (SCD n=115, MCI n=38, HS n=19, Kruskal-Wallis, SCD vs MCI p): 'Peak P1 2.75 (2.31) 2.93 (1.75) 2.93 (2.23) * 0.027'; 'Peak P600 1.4 (1.21) 1.58 (1.28) 1.8 (1.03) * 0.0369'; 'Int P2 568.9 (337.54) 645.3 (322.53) 819.81 (420.93) * 0.0136'; 'Int N1 207.96 (213.91) 247.04 (198.54) 375.49 (246.17) * 0.0358'; but 'Peak P300 3.34 (1.56) 3.06 (1.57) 3.43 (1.66) 0.0839'. Section 3.4 on aggregated integrals: 'Significant differences were observed between HS and SCD (H = 25.95, p < 0.0001) and HS and MCI (H = 9.747, p = 0.0053), with a trend between SCD and MCI (H = 5.197, p = 0.0678).' Discussion: 'Interestingly, the P300 is the only component that appears to show monotony with the clinical condition, i.e. its attenuation follows the severity of the clinical condition.' Behaviour (Section 3.2): 'accuracy showed a significant group effect (H = 6.53, p = 0.04) ... driven by a significant contrast between SCD and MCI (H = 5.921, p = 0.044) ... no significant differences were found between HS and SCD (H = 0.059, p = 1.000) or HS and MCI (H = 3.572, p = 0.176)'; 'The F-Measure did not show significant differences'. Confounds: MCI age 72.75 vs SCD 65.40 vs HS 62.53 years and education 10.32 vs 13.41 vs 14.95 years (age corrected with a Huber regressor); 'ATN Negative (46 of 58; 29 SCD of 34, 17 MCI of 24)'; 'Weaknesses: ... low healthy subject number (focused on SCD vs. MCI), monocentric study without follow-ups'. The study does test the prior: the direct SCD-vs-MCI contrast (115 vs 38) shows a clinically worse group with larger amplitudes on four of 18 features, all in the same direction, and this contrast does not depend on the small HS group. It tests the prior only within the HS-SCD-MCI segment (there is no AD group), in one cross-sectional cohort with syndromic groups, and for some components: P300 followed the monotonic ordering. So the belief is bounded, not refuted. The record's text overstates in three places. (1) 'clearest and statistically robust for P600': P600 peak p = 0.037 is one of four comparable SCD-vs-MCI effects, uncorrected across 18 features, and the P2 integral is the strongest, which the authors themselves call 'the most sensitive integral in distinguishing SCD from MCI'. (2) 'trend-level for other components': the P1 peak, P2 integral and N1 integral are also significant, and P300 continued downward. (3) 'behaviour declined monotonically': only the accuracy means are ordered, and only SCD vs MCI differs significantly. The record also names the dedup stub P-576 as its anchor. CHALLENGER ADDITIONS (re-read of the same PDF): (a) Multiplicity. Methods: 'The multiple comparison correction used for ERP dynamics was the FDR Benjamini-Hochberg, while for all the other test was Bonferroni.' The Table 2 p-values are Bonferroni-adjusted across the three pairwise group contrasts only (H = 8.06 on 1 df gives raw p ~0.0045, x3 = 0.0136; many cells are capped at 1), not across the 12 amplitude features; none of the four SCD-vs-MCI effects would survive a further correction across features. (b) The paper's own aggregate and percentage-deviation analyses are weaker than Table 2: normalised peak 'no significant differences were found between SCD and MCI (H = 0.454, p = 1.000)'; normalised integral 'a trend between SCD and MCI (H = 5.197, p = 0.0678)'; and 'In the comparison between SCD and MCI (Fig. 5C), the differences were less evident. Significant deviations were found only in the P2 integral (11.84 %), while the N1 integral (15.82 %) showed smaller and non-significant variations.' (c) What the pattern rests on is direction consistency: the MCI mean is at or above the SCD mean on every amplitude feature except the P300 peak (11 of 12, N1 peak read as magnitude), and no amplitude feature is significantly lower in MCI than in SCD (115 vs 38). (d) SCD-vs-HS attenuation in Table 2 is significant for the N1 peak and integral, the P2 integral, the P600 and P900 peaks and integrals and the P300 integral, but not for the P1 peak (p = 1), P1 integral (p = 0.086), P2 peak (p = 0.49) or P300 peak (p = 1); the abstract's P1 attenuation comes from the instant-by-instant dynamics (Fig. 3). (e) The P300 monotonic ordering the authors note holds for the peak (3.43 > 3.34 > 3.06, no step significant) but not for the P300 integral (401.84 HS, 349.58 SCD, 356.94 MCI). (f) Age: MCI 72.75 vs SCD 65.40 years; neural features were age-regressed with a Huber regressor on a sample in which age and group are confounded, so the MCI-over-SCD direction depends partly on that age model. (g) Of those with CSF/PET, 17 of 24 MCI were ATN-negative, so the MCI group is largely not on the AD biomarker continuum the prior names.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-21. Add KA-21 (ERP monotonic attenuation, modality eeg) and set assumption_id=KA-21 with P-576 as anchor.' Partly right. A registered prior is needed, and a monotonic-ERP-attenuation prior fits this record. But (a) the anchor is now wrong: the 2026-09-16 dedup made P-576 a stub ('must not be cited as evidence. Use P-144'), so identified_in and the record text must name P-144. (b) KA-21's wording, 'ERP cognitive components (N400, P300/P600 family) attenuate monotonically', fits the evidence poorly. In P-144 the P300 does follow the monotonic ordering, and the non-monotonic features are the sensory P1, N1 and P2 plus the P600. N400 enters KA-21 only through IA-28, which this batch demotes. If KA-21 is kept, it should be reworded to the general form ('ERP component amplitudes attenuate monotonically with clinical stage'), with IA-35 as its sole linked record. It remains proposed: this is a model re-adjudication under operator delegation, not an operator confirmation.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-144 reports no discrimination metric: the registry has Best_Metric 'not reported', task T4, and the study reports ERP group statistics only. It is not in the Section 3.5 performance-validity list.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: The prior is not a strawman and is stated in the corpus: P-144 frames 'the assumption of a linear progression from health to pathology' and 'expected ERP monotonicity', and P-489 independently reports a graded HC > MCI > AD P3 decline. The disproving study does test the prior at group level. The key SCD-vs-MCI contrast (115 vs 38) shows the clinically worse group with larger amplitudes on four features (p = 0.014 to 0.037), and that contrast does not depend on the small healthy group. The test is bounded in four ways: one cross-sectional cohort; syndromic, mostly ATN-negative groups; no AD group; and P300, the component the independent attestation concerns, which followed the monotonic ordering. This is a bound on the general belief, not a refutation. The record text needs the minimum correction on three counts: the anchor must be P-144, because P-576 is a dedup stub not to be cited; 'clearest and statistically robust for P600' and 'trend-level for other components' misstate Table 2; and 'behaviour declined monotonically' overstates Section 3.2. Data-quality note for the orchestrator: summary_match and evidence_from_summary were checked against the P-576 stub block. The canonical P-144 block in summaries.md is raw extract spillover and carries a CLAUDE.md reject phrase ('Contents lists available at ScienceDirect'), so it should be re-summarised. That does not block this verdict, because the P-144 PDF was read directly. The manuscript's Section 4.2, Section 9.1 and Version B sentences need narrower wording to match. CHALLENGER CHECK (2026-09-26): verdict rescope/bounded upheld after re-reading the P-144, P-489 and P-28 extracts; all quoted passages are real. Attestation is thinner than it looks: the general all-component form is stated only by the disproving study's own framing ('challenging the assumption of a linear progression from health to pathology'), and the independent statement (P-489: 'a gradual decrease in the amplitude and increase in the latency of the P3 potential from the HC group to the AD group ... suggesting the presence of diminished neuroelectrical activity consistent with cognitive impairment throughout the course of AD') is P3-centred, the one component P-144 does not contradict. P-489's generalisation to neuroelectrical activity across the course of AD is enough to count the belief as attested rather than a strawman, under the master's disclosure that most priors were registered from the contradicting records. The evidence survives as a bound, not a refutation, because it rests on direction consistency across 11 of 12 amplitude features plus four per-feature effects that are not corrected across features, with an age-by-group confound and a largely ATN-negative MCI group. The auditor's replacement text overstated the statistics (it presented the four p-values without their correction scope, omitted the paper's own null aggregate-peak and single-feature Fig. 5C results, restated the abstract's SCD attenuation of P1/P2 which Table 2 does not show for the peaks, and called the P300 monotonic without restricting it to the peak); the new_text above corrects these.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Mild cognitive impairment involves generalised impairment of visual short-term/working-memory (VWM) binding and semantic memory during object/scene processing.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-607 (Allegretti 2025, Cortex; MCI n=30 accuracy / 21 eye-movement) found the MECHANISMS of object-scene VWM binding preserved in MCI - semantic-inconsistency detection benefit, first-pass gaze-duration benefit, and attentional prioritisation showed no significant group interaction across younger/older/MCI (a null result = no detectable difference, not proven equivalence) - while overall MCI detection accuracy remained significantly lower than older controls (b=-1.37, p<0.001).
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Attentional/compensatory mechanisms supporting object-scene binding appear preserved at the group-mechanism level in this modest MCI sample and MAY be leverageable for rehabilitation - pending replication in adequately powered, subtype-resolved, longitudinal samples. Challenges GENERALISED binding/semantic impairment, not raw performance.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-607: VWM object-scene binding + attentional control preserved in MCI; semantic-inconsistency prioritisation and gaze-duration benefits held across all groups; challenges generalised impairment. MCI n=30/21 (not ~9); overall MCI accuracy still lower.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: Prior ATTESTED. P-13 (Discussion 4.2; PDF downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S0022395623004247-main.pdf), in the context of screening MCI for conversion to AD: "Hippocampus volume of MRI has been established as the best predictive marker for AD (Teipel et al., 2013 ). It is a sensitive predictor of future impairment and progression from mild to more severe stages of AD (Gordon et al., 2013 )." Weaker statements that also bear on it: P-177's report of its own earlier finding that "hippocampal volume was the best predictor of incident MCI within 2 years" (the cognitively-unimpaired-to-MCI transition, not MCI to dementia), and P-581 itself, which states practice rather than belief: "Hippocampal volume, often expressed as a fraction of brain or intracranial volume, is commonly used in research, trials, and clinical practice." In the same paragraph P-581 says it "has limitations regarding the progression from MCI to AD", so the disproving source does not itself hold the prior. Search: summaries.md grep, plus a scan of the PDF text before the References of 159 non-duplicate corpus papers whose blocks mention hippocampal volume/atrophy or cortical thickness (scratchpad/r15/ia/a02audit_attest.py; hits in a02audit_attest_hits.json). The challenger re-extracted the P-13 PDF and found the quote verbatim.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: P-581 PDF (downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/PMID_40420356_ALZ-21-e70310.pdf). (1) Sample: "Note that the survival analysis (described below) includes all 196 MCI participants" (the record's N=826 is the whole cognitively-unimpaired-to-AD sample; MCI C N=86, MCI NC N=110). (2) The comparator was chosen on the same data: "only the AD signature of the cortical diffusivity measure that best distinguishes the two MCI groups at the regional level will be included." (3) Log-rank tests of each marker, N+ vs N-: PerpPD+ "chi-square =20.189; Pvalue<0.001"; HVF "chi-square =13.009; Pvalue<0.001"; CT signature "chi-square =19.461; Pvalue<0.001"; CVF "chi-square =0.778; Pvalue>0.05". Hippocampal volume was therefore itself significantly prognostic. (4) The only head-to-head test: "The log rank (Mantel–Cox) analysis performed to compare the N+ curves showed that only the PerpPD+signature curve was significantly different compared to cortical volume fraction (chi-square =4.051; Pvalue <0.05). No other significant difference was found in the comparison between curves." (5) The superiority claim rests on medians: "Participants who were positive for PerpPD+signature exhibited a median survival time of ≈1.5 years earlier than those identified through reduced hippocampal volume". Those medians come from N+ groups of different size at baseline (Table 5: PerpPD+ 42 of 196 vs HVF 74 of 196), because each cut-point is the crossing of the cognitively-unimpaired and AD density curves. A smaller, stricter positive group can be expected to have a shorter median, so the medians are not comparable across markers. No HR, C-index or AUC is reported. (6) "MT, PK, and GR are currently employed at a company, Oxford Brain Diagnostics. SAC has a patent (WO2016162682A1) related to the diffusion MRI analysis used in the present study." Conclusion: the design addresses the prior, a head-to-head prognostic comparison in MCI, but its formal test against hippocampal volume is null. "Outperformed hippocampal volume" is the authors' descriptive reading, and their own pairwise test contradicts it, so what_disproved_it overstates the PDF.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: "ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-12. Set assumption_id=KA-12." This is not a demotion recommendation. Its reason is right as far as it goes: the record named no registered prior, and KA-12 (hippocampal primacy) is its topical home. The prior is also attested outside the IA ledger (P-13), so the link is not purely circular. But the audit did not examine the evidence, and its recommendation is moot, because the evidence neither overturns nor bounds the prior. The demotion rests on the source document, not on the audit.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-581 reports no AUC or accuracy, only survival analysis, and logs/appraisal_worksheet.csv marks it performance_suspect_set = no (V2, N=826). The performance-validity rule does not apply. The failure is statistical: the between-marker test is null, the comparator was selected in-sample, and the authors disclose a commercial and patent interest.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: The prior is a real field belief, attested by P-13, so the record does not fail on attestation. It fails on evidence. P-581 tested the prior with pairwise log-rank comparisons of survival curves and found no significant difference between the cortical diffusivity signature and hippocampal volume. The only significant difference was against cortical volume fraction. The record's 'outperformed hippocampal volume' rests on shorter N+ medians and larger per-marker chi-squares. Neither is a between-marker test, and both are confounded: the positive groups differ in size (42 vs 74 of 196), and the diffusivity metric was picked on the same data. The authors also disclose a commercial and patent interest. A 'parity' rescope would treat a non-significant difference as a bound on a 'best' claim, which the admission rule does not accept. The record also misstates the analysed N (826 vs 196 MCI). Challenger: every quote was re-checked against the extracts, and no missed evidence was found. The pairwise N+ tests also show no difference between hippocampal volume and the CT signature, so nothing in P-581 bounds hippocampal primacy. Demote upheld.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: None found. The prior as registered, "Cortical thickness is the structural MRI marker of MCI-to-AD conversion", is a definite-article strawman: no corpus study states that cortical thickness is THE conversion marker. KA-12 is status proposed_2026_08_29 and was registered from these same IA records, so linking the record to it is circular. Search: a summaries.md grep and a scan of the pre-References PDF text of 159 non-duplicate corpus papers mentioning hippocampal volume/atrophy or cortical thickness, with primacy patterns (scratchpad/r15/ia/a02audit_attest.py). Nearest statements, none of which attests the prior: P-1158 "regional cortical thickness provides a biologically meaningful and highly reliable biomarker that can detect subtle atrophy patterns characteristic of neurodegenerative diseases" (reliability); P-1089 "As is well established, the reduced cortical thickness of the rostral ACC can predict the conversion from amnestic MCI to AD with psychosis" (one regional predictor in a subgroup); P-536 "Cortical thickness was adopted as the AD signature" (practice). P-560's own introduction cites evidence against the prior: "Bertoux and colleagues [8] showed that sulcal width better classified AD patients compared to cortical thickness." Its discussion adds that prior studies found sulcal width "in most cases superior to other typical morphological evaluations, such as volumetry or cortical thickness".
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: P-560 PDF (downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/PMID_38640154_jad-99-jad231192.pdf). (1) Design: 37 MCI, "At follow-up, 12 MCI were classified as MCInc and25 as MCIc", single site, 1.5T, follow-up "after an average of 28 ±15 months", "pathophysiological biomarkers were not available in this cohort". (2) The headline AUC is in-sample and best-of-selection: "results are reported only for the feature that achieved the best discrimination performance for each contrast". The authors state that the sample was too small to "build training and test sets", so a Leave-One-Out repeat was run and "returned AUC and accuracy values on average 2-4% lower with respect to the values of the in-sample analysis reported in this section". Table 4 "Right S.T.i.post. 1.6 ±0.2 2.1 ±0.5 0.001 0.907". The 0.907 is therefore the in-sample AUC, not the LOO AUC the record implies. Features were selected on the full sample. (3) The thickness result is a null in a 12-vs-25 contrast: "There were no regions whose CT differed significantly between MCInc and MCIc." (4) There is no between-measure test. The authors compare significant against non-significant: "sulcal width achieved better outcomes than cortical thickness for each of the group comparisons performed. This is especially evident in the case of the comparison between MCIc and MCInc, where no alterations of cortical thickness were statistically significant." Conclusion: an underpowered thickness null plus a best-of-many in-sample AUC neither overturns nor bounds the prior. The record's own g5_caveat concedes 'possible Type II error'.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: "ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-12. Set assumption_id=KA-12 with strength 'weak' (N=37, LOOCV, underpowered thickness null); correct the P-560 Validation Type to V1." The weaknesses it names are correct, but they disqualify the record rather than grade it: under the admission rule an underpowered null is not a disproof. The KA-12 link fails because the thickness-specific prior is not attested. V1 is defensible for the registry Best_Metric, since 0.907 is the in-sample figure (the registry currently codes V3), but that recode belongs to the registry lane.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged by the rule. The headline AUC is 0.907 (MCIc vs MCInc) and the highest reported is 0.957 (AD vs MCInc), both below 0.97, and the appraisal worksheet marks P-560 performance_suspect_set = no. The demotion does not rest on the flag, although the 0.907 is an optimistic in-sample, best-of-selection estimate on 37 MCI.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: There are two independent failures, and either is sufficient. First, attestation: no corpus study states that cortical thickness is the conversion marker. The nearest statements concern reliability (P-1158), a regional subgroup predictor (P-1089) or practice (P-536). The disproving study's own introduction and discussion cite prior evidence that sulcal width beats thickness. The KA-12 registration is circular. Second, evidence: the thickness result is an underpowered null (12 vs 25). The sulcal AUC is the best of many Bonferroni-screened features, reported in-sample on 37 people, and there is no statistical comparison between the two measures. The record also mislabels the 0.907 as an LOO AUC. No narrower form survives, because even a milder prior is not bounded by an underpowered null. Challenger: all P-560 quotes were verified verbatim. Demote upheld.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Higher-order functional-network representations capture discriminative information that low-order pairwise (Pearson) functional connectivity misses, and so classify MCI against controls more accurately.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-516 (Guo 2021; ADNI rs-fMRI, MCI vs HC, 143 participants/299 scans; linear SVM, subject-level five-fold CV, t-test edge selection) compared Pearson networks (PC1) with 'correlation's correlation' networks of increasing order (PCn). The second-order network was already less accurate than PC1 at all four feature-selection thresholds, accuracy fell further as order rose (towards chance at the convergent network), and PC1 had the best sensitivity and specificity. Fusing PCn with PC1 did not improve accuracy or specificity in most settings and gave small sensitivity gains. All metrics are figure-only, with no significance tests; at each fixed t-test threshold the higher-order networks also retained fewer edge features than PC1, so order and feature count are not separated.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: For rs-fMRI classification of MCI against controls, correlation's-correlation networks should not be assumed to add accuracy over ordinary Pearson connectivity: in one small ADNI sample they reduced it, and low-plus-high-order fusion gave at most small, untested sensitivity gains. The bound covers this construction and sample, not other high-order connectivity methods.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: Higher-order PCn correlation networks lose discrimination as order increases (accuracy converges to ~50%); higher order does not beat the simple low-order network.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: Adversarial source-verification: summary_match=true, confidence=high. Caveat: exact metrics reported figure-only in source. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW. Manual curation batch manual_curation_2026-07-29_P380plus. Proposed by Claude (actor) from 205 grounded finding-cards; adversarially source-verified against each cited summary block (workflow B) - grounding_ok=true. NOT human-confirmed; do not treat as gate-passed until reviewed. | G5 CONFIRM-with-caveat 2026-07-29 (AI-adversarial): grounding verified vs summary; overclaim softened; scope/power caveat added.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Single study, single clinical dataset (ADNI); exact metrics figure-only. Disproof is scoped to CLASSIFICATION ACCURACY under escalating order (n>2): PC2 and PCn+PC1 fusion still add SENSITIVITY, so higher-order reps are not devoid of value. Overturns 'escalating order automatically improves accuracy', not 'correlation's-correlation adds nothing'.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_delegated_verdict_2026_08_22: CONFIRM. Accuracy-decays-to-chance with PCn order and the sensitivity-only fusion gain both verbatim in Outcomes; figure-only metrics caveat and N=143 subjects/299 scans verified. readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: P-79 (Wu et al. 2026, Expert Systems with Applications, an MCI-detection study; PDF downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S0957417425046184-main.pdf, Introduction; the challenger found the text verbatim): "most existing DFCN-based approaches primarily focus on cross-window temporal dynamics while modeling only pairwise relationships between regions of interest (ROIs) within each window. Such approaches disregard how inter-regional function extends beyond simple pairwise interactions, with high-order cooperation among multiple brain regions often reflecting more informative pathological patterns. Moreover, functional connectivity matrices constructed purely from correlation or mutual information neglect high-order topological structures and network hierarchies within each window, potentially limiting both diagnostic accuracy and biomarker discovery." P-516's own Introduction attributes the correlation's-correlation belief to earlier work (verbatim): "the two sequential PCs (denoted as PC2 in this paper) provide a high-order statistic that, in theory, can encode more complex relationship ... Chen et al. (2016) revealed that PC2 can encode the complex interactions between different ROIs, and Zhang et al. (2016) found that PC2 is more sensitive to AD identification." Limits: P-79 builds its high-order networks by regression (NRR), not by correlation's correlation, and no corpus study other than P-516 itself mentions PC2. The belief that raising the order of PCn beyond n=2 helps is NOT attested: it is P-516's own research question ("what will happen if continuing the correlation operation to construct much higher-order BFN by PCn(n>2)").
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: PDF downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/PMID_34497485_fnins-15-696639.pdf (Guo et al. 2021). Abstract: "(1) with the increase of n, the discriminative ability of PCn-based BFNs tends to decrease; (2) fusing the PCn-based BFNs (n>1) with the PC1-based BFN can generally improve the sensitivity for MCI identification, but fail to help the classification accuracy." Sample and design: "299 scans (including 154 HCs and 145 MCIs) from 143 participants"; "five-fold subject-level cross validation (5-F CV), to ensure that fMRI scans of the subject do not appear in both training and testing sets"; "Linear support vector machine (SVM) ... with default parameter C = 1"; "t-test is used to select edge weight features prior to the classification task". The paper does not state whether this selection was nested within the training folds. Figure 6 caption: "with the increase of n, the ACC of PCn-based BFN tends to decrease in all the cases." Figure 7 caption: "the SEN and SPE of PC1 is better than other cases." Figure 9 caption: "the fusion of low- and higher-order BFNs fails to improve the ACC and SPE in most cases, but generally improves SEN." Section 4.1: "Especially when the BFN converges with a big n, the ACC approaches 50%"; "PC1 includes the largest number of features (207 features) and the number of features selected by PCn decrease with the increase of n." The challenger rendered Figures 6, 7 and 9 (pages 6 to 8). At p=0.001/0.005/0.01/0.05, MCI accuracy is about 68.5/72/73.5/77% for PC1 and about 63/64/65.5/68.5% for PC2, and about 55 to 58% for the convergent network. PC2 sensitivity is at or below PC1 at every threshold (about 64.5 vs 65, 60 vs 67, 67 vs 70 and 71 vs 71.5%). Fusion raises sensitivity by about 1 to 2 points. There is no numeric table, no spread across folds and no significance test. Two record errors are confirmed. PC2 alone did not improve sensitivity; only PCn+PC1 fusion did. And the source's own conclusion partly confirms the prior as the record words it.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-15; set assumption_id=KA-15; keep the caveat that PC2/fusion still adds sensitivity. This was applied. The caveat instruction is only half right: fusion adds a small, untested sensitivity gain, but PC2 alone does not (Figure 7). KA-15's registration is circular, as for IA-15, and P-79 and P-516's introduction supply the attestation. KA-15 says 'prognostic', but P-516 is a diagnostic MCI-versus-control task, so KA-15 should read 'prognostic or diagnostic' if IA-40 stays linked. No demotion was recommended. A rescope is needed because the evidence does not overturn the prior as the record words it.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. The highest MCI-versus-HC accuracy is about 77% (read from the figure), under subject-level five-fold CV, with 143 participants and no external cohort. This is far below the 0.97 threshold. A separate weakness, not a flag: all metrics are given only in figures, with no significance tests.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: The challenger re-extracted P-516 and P-79, found all quotes verbatim, and rendered the P-516 figures. This confirmed the auditor's figure readings and both record errors: PC2 alone does not improve sensitivity, and the 'toward chance' result tests a proposition nobody attested. The accuracy form of the higher-order prior is attested independently by P-79, an MCI study, and for PC2 specifically by P-516's introduction citing Zhang 2016. The within-study PC2-versus-PC1 comparison tests it directly, and the direction is the same at all four thresholds (4 to 9 points). But it is one small sample with figure-only results and no significance tests, feature count changes along with order, and the paper does not say whether feature selection was nested. That bounds the accuracy prior for this construction; it does not refute higher-order connectivity in general. Demotion was considered again and rejected, because the prior is attested outside the record and the comparison is direct. The auditor's rescope stands, with one added limitation (the feature-count confound) in what_disproved_it and a more specific note for Section 7.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: None found. No corpus study states that amyloid is a primary determinant of PD-MCI. P-525 PDF: 'There is uncertainty about the role of beta-amyloid (Abeta) co-pathology and its contribution to the variability in PD-MCI profile and cognitive progression'. P-221 PDF: 'Several mechanisms are likely to contribute to cognitive decline in PD', and 'although low cerebrospinal fluid levels of amyloid-beta42 have been found to predict cognitive decline in PD, hitherto PET imaging of amyloid-beta (Abeta) failed to consistently demonstrate the association between Abeta plaques deposition and mild cognitive impairment in PD (PD-MCI)'. Both describe amyloid as a contested contributor, not as the primary determinant. Searched: summaries.md for Parkinson within 200 characters of amyloid/Abeta with driv/determin/main/primary/contribut (the only hit is P-525's own conclusion), the P-221 and P-525 PDFs, and the P-1325 block. The prior is the negation of P-525's hedged conclusion.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: Source: downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/PMID_35300351_fneur-12-760518.pdf. Cross-sectional, N=25: 'There were 8 Abeta+ and 17 Abeta- PD-MCI.' The conclusion is hedged: 'suggest that Abeta may not be the main pathogenetic determinant of cognitive deterioration in PD-MCI, but it would rather aggravate deficits'; 'led us to speculate about the independent role of amyloid load'. The positive result supports a contributory role: 'PD-MCI-Abeta+ showed worse performance in the overall executive domain (p=0.037)', and cortical amyloid correlated with executive score (paracentral r=-0.57, p=0.005). The atrophy observation applies to both groups: 'cortical VBM patterns were similar in PD-MCI with and without Abeta deposition, and excluded the presence of middle-temporal atrophy'. Limitations: no APOE screening, and no control group of healthy participants or PD without cognitive deficits. There is no follow-up. Challenger note: P-221, not cited by the record, is itself a PD-MCI vs PD-noMCI comparison ('we failed to find any significant difference in all examined cortical and subcortical areas'). It cannot rescue the record, because the prior remains unattested and changing the anchor study would make a new record, not a rescope.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-17 with PD-MCI scope and 'weak' strength. Its reason does not hold. KA-17 is an Alzheimer amyloid-cascade prior inferred from this record and IA-03, so it provides no independent attestation. P-525 does not show KA-17's disproof signal (prognostic signal in amyloid-negative MCI): it is cross-sectional and non-prognostic. A 'weak' label does not cure a missing attestation. Demote.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-525 is a PET/MRI association study with no classifier, AUC or accuracy (N=25).
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: The prior fails independence. No corpus study says amyloid is the primary PD-MCI determinant: P-221 and P-525 both call it a contested co-pathology, and the prior was written as the negation of P-525's hedged conclusion. The evidence does not rescue it. The only positive result supports a contributory role for amyloid, and 'not the main determinant' is the authors' speculation from 25 patients, with no comparator, no APOE screening and no follow-up. The record states that speculation as a finding and attributes a both-group atrophy observation to the amyloid-negative group alone. Filing it under an AD cascade prior (KA-17) compounds the problem. The verdict is demote; only manuscript_uses was corrected.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: FDG-PET prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion depends on brain-wide/global hypometabolism, which is uninformative in amyloid/tau-negative individuals.

readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: PDF downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/PMID_39470016_ALZ-20-8979.pdf (Terstege 2024), re-extracted and re-read by challenger. Retrospective ADNI, 399 baseline MCI, two-way ANOVA + multiple logistic regression, no AUC/accuracy. Framing: 'to revisit the question of RSC hypometabolism as a predictor of MCI to AD conversion. To extend and validate prior findings, we compared subjects ...'. Whole cohort: 'Decreased brain-wide FDG-PET SUVr was observed in the MCI-AD groups (Figure 2D; two-factor ANOVA; main effect of conversion status: F(394)=8.258, p=0.0043)'. Regression sits in Section 3.3 (pathology-classified analysis): 'Furthermore, using multiple logistic regression with sex, Aβ-PET SUVr, tau-PET SUVr, and either RSC FDG-PET SUVr or brain-wide FDG-PET SUVr, it was determined that RSC FDG-PET SUVr is a significant predictor of transition from MCI to AD (|Z|=3.181, p=0.0015) while the FDG-PET SUVr is not (|Z|=1.390, p=0.1645).' Amyloid/tau used only 'when available' ('many subjects living with MCI have an unknown Aβ status'), so regression N < 399 and unreported; separate models, so a Z comparison, not a formal test. Subgroup: 'Examining individuals who were negative for both Aβ and tau pathology, decreased FDG-PET SUVr was only observed in the RSC of MCI-AD subjects (Figure 2G; two-factor ANOVA; main effect of conversion status: F(44)=4.727, p=0.0351) and not on a brain-wide level (Figure 2H)', about 48 subjects, group difference, no prediction statistic. Discussion: 'Conversely, brain-wide hypometabolism was predictive of conversion to AD only in Aβ and tau-positive individuals', which agrees with the prior's second clause. The record's 'in whole-cohort logistic regression' with 'ADNI N=399' is inaccurate.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'DEMOTE:strawman - nobody holds that FDG-PET prediction depends on brain-wide/global hypometabolism; the AD FDG signature is regional (posterior cingulate/retrosplenial), so the finding confirms the field view; the amyloid-negative clause rests on a ~46-subject group-difference test.' The reason holds, and the PDF makes it stronger: P-569 presents RSC hypometabolism as a long-standing predictive finding it sets out to 'extend and validate', and P-512, P-574 and P-578 attest the regional view. The subgroup is about 48 (df 44 in a sex x conversion ANOVA), not 46. The secondary suggestion (P-569 as VF support for regional hypometabolism) is a separate candidate and is not endorsed here.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-569 reports no AUC or accuracy (only |Z| and F statistics), N=399. It is not in the Section 3.5 set (P-200, P-197, P-119, P-1). The demotion rests on non-attestation and on the study not testing a held prior.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: H.1 requires the prior to be attested in the corpus. KA-44 was registered from the record itself, and no corpus study states either clause as a field belief. The anchoring study's introduction says the opposite and frames the work as a validation. invalidated_assumptions.assumption_type: FC as proxy for effective connectivity
invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Functional-connectivity strength is a good proxy for effective (directional) connectivity strength.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-542 (Huang 2022; ADNI-2, N=130 across CN/EMCI/LMCI/AD, cross-sectional DCM over 7 DMN/SAN/CEN ROIs): directional (effective) connectivity declined progressively from full connection in CN to none in AD, detectable as early as EMCI; the authors interpret this, extending prior FC meta-findings (Xu et al. 2020), as indicating FC strengths are poor indicators of EC strengths in AD - a discussion-level inference, not a within-study quantitative FC-EC contrast.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: In this small resting-state ADNI-2 setting, undirected FC may not capture directional network disruption that effective-connectivity modelling reveals; directional (causal) modelling is worth adding, but the FC-cannot-substitute conclusion needs confirmation in larger/independent AD-MCI cohorts before generalisation.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: Effective (directional) connectivity declines from full connection in CN to none in AD; FC strengths are poor indicators of EC strengths in AD (unlike healthy), disruption detectable at EMCI.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: none found. Searched summaries.md for 'effective connectivity', 'directional connectivity', 'directed connectivity', 'causal connectivity' and read candidates P-542, P-905, P-410, P-497. The challenger also searched 'proxy for effective', FC proxy and surrogate wording (0 hits). The corpus states the textbook distinction instead: P-542 introduction: 'As opposed to the FC quantified with measures of statistical dependencies, EC corresponds to the parameter of a model that tries to explain the cause of such dependencies (Friston, 2011)'. P-905 block: 'Functional connectivity (undirected) had been widely reviewed, but directional EC findings were scattered'. The P-410 block ('Prior work measured undirected functional connectivity; the directionality distinguishing pMCI from sMCI was unknown') describes practice, not a belief. The only statement that FC and EC correspond is Neufang et al. (2011), a healthy-subject finding outside the corpus. KA-45 is status proposed_2026_09_09 and was registered from the IA-43 record.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: PDF downloads/5. Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Biomarkers/PMID_36590062_fnhum-16-1060936.pdf (Huang, Jung and Nam 2022), re-extracted and re-read by the challenger. 'In this study, 34 AD patients, 31 LMCI patients, 34 EMCI patients, and 31 CN subjects were selected and analyzed' (N=130). Cross-sectional ADNI-2 rs-fMRI, spectral DCM over 7 ROIs with PEB. No FC measure is computed. Abstract: 'The results showed that the connections reduced from full connection in the CN group to no connection in the AD group' (at a posterior-probability threshold of 0.99). The FC-EC sentence restates another paper: 'Considering the relationship of EC with FC, Neufang et al. (2011) found that two connectivities are significantly related in healthy subjects. Yet they pointed out this kind of similarity is disrupted in AD patients. FC strengths are not good indicators of EC strengths in AD patients.' Xu et al. (2020) appears in a different paragraph ('A meta-review of past MCI studies by Xu et al. (2020) suggested increased FCs in MCI patients were located in the precentral gyrus ...'), so the record's Xu attribution does not match the source. Authors' caveat: 'Due to the relatively small sample size of the current study, further investigation of AD progression is still needed'.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'DEMOTE:no within-study test of the prior - FC is a poor proxy for EC is the authors' discussion-level extension of prior literature. Demote to proposed; keep P-542 EC-decline as a consensus/complementary finding.' The reason holds, and it understates the problem. P-542 computes no FC at all, and the FC-EC sentence restates Neufang et al. (2011), a study outside the corpus, rather than extending Xu et al. (2020). Both the record and the P-542 block misattribute it. The secondary suggestion (a VF/CF for the EC decline) is a separate candidate, and one small cross-sectional study cannot show convergence. Not endorsed.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-542 reports no AUC or accuracy (DCM posterior probabilities, ANOVA, step-wise regression with R2 about 0.12). It is not in the Section 3.5 set.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: The record fails H.1 on three independent grounds. (a) Attestation: no corpus study holds that FC strength is a proxy for EC strength, and the corpus states the standard distinction instead. (b) Test: P-542 computes no FC, so it cannot compare FC with EC. The sentence the record relies on cites Neufang et al. (2011). (c) Anchor: the attribution to Xu et al. (2020) does not match the PDF. What P-542 does show, a decline in EC in one small sample, overturns no attested prior, so the record cannot be rescoped. Demote to proposed. The challenger re-read the PDF and agrees with the auditor.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: In ATN staging, A+T+N- and A+T+N+ MCI patients can be merged for progression modelling.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: None found. Searched summaries.md for 'tortuos': hits only in P-125 (amygdala shape on MRI, irrelevant), P-255 (the disproving study) and P-1317. Scanned the full text of the 147 retinal/ocular corpus PDFs (auditor script a05aud_scan.py). The challenger re-checked P-830, P-1317 and P-255 directly. P-830 (the corpus retinal meta-analysis) has no tortuosity statement; its Discussion names only 'reduced complexity of vessels'. P-255's introduction: 'The results have been inconsistent in regard to cognitive impairment, with some studies finding an association between retinal microvascular parameters and cognitive impairment [9-11], while others did not [12,13]. To our knowledge, two studies have investigated the association between retinal microvascular parameters and presence of MCI in people with type 2 diabetes, also reporting conflicting results [14,15].' Its discussion reports that one T2D study 'found greater venular tortuosity ... in those with MCI' (venular) and another 'found no associations'. P-1317 (non-diabetic) relays one pilot: 'Pead et al also reported an increased superonasal retinal arterial tortuosity in MCI compared with controls', and itself found no tortuosity difference ('Our study did not find any evidence of significant differences in arterial or venous tortuosity between MCI and controls'). P-255 ref. 29 (Sandoval-Garcia, prospective T2D cohort, cerebrovascular events) gives no direction in the extract. KA-20 was built from this record and IA-27, so the reviewer supplied it.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: Source PDF: C:/Users/aryas/Downloads/PAPERINGO/downloads/1. Clinical Assessments, Behavioral and Social Factors/1-s2.0-S1751991826000331-main.pdf (Pedersen et al., Primary Care Diabetes 2026). Abstract: 'We included 578 eyes of 307 individuals with type 2 diabetes of whom 182 had MCI and 125 had normal cognition. ... arteriolar tortuosity was associated with MCI in the multivariable analysis (OR 1.44 [95 % CI 1.08-1.92]; the less the tortuosity the higher the risk). ... we found an AUC of 0.73.' Results: 'an AUC of 0.62 in the model in which we included all retinal microvascular parameters, but when adding the baseline characteristics ... the AUC increased to 0.73'. Table 2: arteriolar tortuosity n = 315 eyes, crude OR 1.31 (1.01-1.71), crude AUC 0.48, adjusted OR 1.44 (1.08-1.92), adjusted AUC 0.70 against a reference of 0.66. Limitation: 'there is a potential for spurious associations due to multiple testing.' Methods 2.4: 'Results are reported as OR (per SD increment)'. Results: 'venular width (OR 0.79 [95% CI 0.63-0.98]; the higher the width the less the risk) and arteriolar tortuosity (OR 1.31 [95% CI 1.01-1.71]; the less the tortuosity the higher the risk)'. Reading: this is one cross-sectional association in T2D, one of eight parameters tested, with an authors' warning that it may be spurious. The record attaches the combined-model AUC (0.73) to tortuosity. The source's own direction is also internally inconsistent: an OR above 1 per SD increment is glossed as 'less tortuosity, higher risk', while venular width is glossed consistently, and no scale definition in the PDF reconciles the two. So even the reversed direction the record reports is not securely shown. There is no attested T2D arteriolar prior for the study to test.

KA-20 was built from this record, no corpus study states the arteriolar-tortuosity prior in T2D, and the source itself calls the literature conflicting. Do not confirm the tortuosity half of KA-20; the record should leave the IA ledger.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Olfactory recognition MEMORY is impaired already at the MCI(-AD) stage and is therefore a sensitive prodromal marker.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-281 (Audronyte 2023; single-site, cross-sectional, N=90 = 30 CN / 30 MCI-AD / 30 mild-dementia-AD): olfactory recognition memory was significantly impaired in AD dementia but MCI-AD did NOT differ significantly from CN, while verbal memory WAS already impaired at MCI-AD. In this small cross-sectional cohort olfactory recognition-memory deficits were not detected at the prodromal (MCI-AD) stage - a null in 30/group is 'not supported here', not a proven absence - and the 'emerges later' staging is inferred cross-sectionally, not tracked longitudinally.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: None found for the prior as written. Searched: summaries.md for olfact|odou?r|smell|sniffin|UPSIT and for 'olfactory (recognition|memory)|odou?r (memory|recognition)'. The hits are only in the P-281 block (lines 20770-20839) and in the P-677 identification meta-analysis. The P-281 PDF was read in full. P-281 is the only corpus study of olfactory memory in MCI, and it describes the question as open and contested, not as a belief the field holds. PDF Introduction: 'Olfactory impairment has recently gained attention as a common and early sign of AD that precedes cognitive decline by several years (8-10). However, most studies have focused on odor identification testing, and other olfactory functions have rarely been analyzed. Especially sparse are data regarding olfactory memory.' and 'the results are inconsistent, with some authors finding olfactory memory to be affected in patients with AD (18, 19), while others found only odor identification to be impaired, with no deficits in olfactory memory (20).' PDF Discussion: 'Data on patients with early-stage AD are limited. In a study performed in 2008, authors found no olfactory memory deficits in prodromal AD (MCI patients) (20). However, in a more recent work, researchers revealed olfactory memory to be impaired in MCI, as well as in patients with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) (18).' The corpus attests only a broader belief about olfactory impairment, carried by odor identification (P-412, P-677, P-738). Narrowing it to recognition MEMORY as a 'sensitive prodromal marker' is the reviewer's projection. The PDF contains no 'sensitive'. Registry prior KA-47 has status proposed_2026_09_09 and was generated from this IA record itself.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: Source: downloads/2. Animal Models and Pre-clinical Mechanisms/PMID_37332995_fneur-14-1165594.pdf (P-281; DOI 10.3389/fneur.2023.1165594). N = 90 (30 CN / 30 MCI-AD / 30 MD-AD). MCI-AD was a clinical diagnosis: 'biomarkers of amyloid deposition and neuronal degeneration were not tested'. Result: 'The MCI-AD and CN groups did not differ significantly [in both cases, Kruskal-Wallis test, p < 0.05; post hoc analysis revealed significant differences between the MD-AD and MCI-AD groups and between the MD-AD and CN groups (p < 0.05), and no significant difference between the MCI-AD and CN groups (p > 0.05)]'. Authors: 'these changes did not reach the level of statistical significance during the prodromal stage of the disease (MCI due to AD).' Limitations: 'the cross-sectional design limited the accuracy of the conclusions regarding longitudinal changes during the course of AD ... in order to confirm these results, further research with larger samples of participants is needed.' The paper gives no effect size, CI or exact p for the MCI-AD versus CN contrast, and no power analysis. At 30 per group there is 80% power only for d of about 0.74, and about 48% for d = 0.5. The verbal-memory comparator reached significance because its effect was very large (Cohen's d = 2.518, 2.992, 3.108), so it does not show that an olfactory deficit of ordinary size would have been detected. This is an underpowered null on one Sniffin' Sticks recognition paradigm. It does not show sparing at MCI-AD, and the 'verbal memory preceded it' ordering is a cross-sectional inference.
