The 'complementary staging observation' half names no admissible record type, because no second corpus study tests olfactory recognition memory. The related gap candidate G-CAND-201 is already rejected. Earlier admits (second reader 2026-09-15; worksheet 2026-09-19 item 32) checked the record against the summary block only.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Cognitive impairment in vascular / late-life depression is largely secondary to depressed mood and remits as mood lifts - a mood-driven epiphenomenon rather than an independent treatment target.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-621 (prospective single-blind RCT, N=116 VaDep-MCI, Fujian Medical University Union Hospital) augmented escitalopram with the 5-HT1A agonist tandospirone citrate vs escitalopram alone. The tandospirone group showed significantly greater improvement in Semantic Verbal Fluency (Weeks 4 and 8) and Trail Making Test B-A (Week 8) on GEE, while RAVLT / Digit Span / Clock Drawing were stable in both arms. A formal mediation analysis showed these cognitive gains were NOT mediated by depression improvement - so the cognitive benefit is independent of antidepressant mood response.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: In one single-blind, eight-week trial in vascular-depression MCI, adding the 5-HT1A agonist tandospirone to escitalopram improved semantic verbal fluency and Trail Making Test B-A more than escitalopram alone, and mediation analysis did not attribute the gains to mood response; cognition may be a treatment target in its own right, pending double-blind, multi-centre replication.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-621 summary: single-blind RCT (N=116), tandospirone+escitalopram vs escitalopram; significantly greater Semantic Verbal Fluency (Wk 4,8) and TMT(B-A) (Wk 8); 'Mediation analysis showed these effects were not mediated by depression improvement'; plasma 5-HT correlated with depression severity (r 0.347).
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Bounded, not refuted: single-blind, single-centre RCT (116 randomised, 108 analysed per protocol, 8 weeks); 2 of 5 primary cognitive tests improved (SVF, TMT B-A) and 3 were stable in both arms; HAMD change did not differ between arms at Weeks 4 and 8; the authors state the trial did not primarily aim to examine mechanism of action. Residual scope: VaDep-MCI, 8 weeks, SVF and TMT B-A. [revised 2026-09-24 against the P-621 PDF; the earlier 'strongest belief-overturning class' wording was removed]
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: DISCOVERED + G5-verified 2026-07-30 (AI-adversarial frontier mining): survived grounding + gold-rubric + FP-taxonomy + novelty gates; 5 sibling candidates rejected (4 EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE, 1 spurious-aggregation VF). Grounded verbatim in P-621; novel - the other 48 IAs are all imaging/biomarker/ML, none neuropsychiatric/pharmacological.
invalidated_assumptions.prior_audit_2026_08_29: ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-24. Add KA-24 (psychiatric cognitive impairment is mood-state-dependent/distinct from MCI, modality clinical_survey) and set assumption_id=KA-24 with P-621 as anchor.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication_pre_2026_09_24: Executive/language cognition in vascular-depression MCI is a direct pharmacological target (5-HT1A augmentation), not merely a downstream consequence of mood; cognitive endpoints should be measured and treated independently of depression response.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat_pre_2026_09_24: Single-blind, single-centre RCT (N=116, 8 weeks); cognitive benefit limited to executive/language domains and to the vascular-depression population. Strongest belief-overturning class (RCT + formal mediation) but awaiting double-blind, multi-centre, longer-horizon replication before generalising beyond VaDep-MCI.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: None found. Searched: summaries.md (pseudodementia, state-dependent, mood-dependent, reversible, remits/remission/remitted, secondary to depression, trait vs state, epiphenomenon, transient, cognition improving with treatment of depression) and the PDFs of P-621, P-774, P-365, P-1393, P-559 and P-27 (plus P-787, P-777, P-643 via the batch scan). No corpus study states, as a belief the field holds, that cognitive impairment in vascular or late-life depression is secondary to mood and remits as mood lifts. The corpus states the OPPOSITE as established: P-365 (PDF) 'Almost 50% of older adults with remitted MDD (rMDD) remain cognitively impaired following treatment (1,3)' (its reference 5 is Nebes et al. 2003, 'Persistence of cognitive impairment in geriatric patients following antidepressant treatment'); P-559 (PDF) 'Cognitive deficits are widespread in the course of depression and can occur before the occurrence of depression or during episodes of depression or can persist after the episode of depression has resolved.'; P-27 (PDF) cognitive symptoms are 'persisting in 32.4 % to 44 % of patients even during remission'; P-774 (PDF) 'impairments of executive function, memory, and information processing speed persisted in individuals with RGD. These findings potentially imply that the cognitive dysfunctions might be trait characteristics of geriatric depression patients.' P-621's own reference list includes Bhalla et al. 2006, 'Persistence of neuropsychologic deficits in the remitted state of late-life depression'. The closest statements to the prior's 'not an independent treatment target' clause describe practice, not a belief: P-621 'the current clinical paradigms for the treatment and evaluation of VaDep have insufficiently addressed this disorder'; P-559 'in the clinical diagnosis and treatment of depression, the cognitive impairments are overlooked.' The linked registry prior KA-24 is status proposed_2026_08_29, was generated from the IA records themselves ('Corpus prior implied by the invalidated-assumption records'), and states a different belief (psychiatric cognitive impairment is 'distinct from MCI, so it does not carry MCI/dementia risk'). Challenger re-search of summaries.md (pseudodementia, reversible cognitive impairment, secondary to depression/mood, state-dependent, mood-dependent, epiphenomenon, cognition improving or remitting with depression) found nothing further. The only near hit is summary-writer prose in the P-774 block ('a rationale for cognitive monitoring in remitted geriatric depression rather than discharge on mood remission'). That is the summariser describing practice, not a study stating the field's belief. The same block records the persistence finding against the prior ('Cognitive impairments in executive function, memory and processing speed persisted in remitted geriatric depression, which the authors interpret as trait rather than state characteristics').
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: Source: downloads/1. Clinical Assessments, Behavioral and Social Factors/1-s2.0-S0022395622006926-main.pdf (P-621). Design: 'In this single-blind, randomized controlled study, 116 participants were randomly assigned to the tandospirone (tandospirone citrate-escitalopram) and control (escitalopram) groups.' Assessors, not patients, were masked: 'All assessments were carried out by two neurologists ... masked to the grouping and medication of patients.' Primary endpoints were five tests; two moved: 'the tandospirone group displayed more pronounced changes in SVF score at Weeks 4 and 8 [by 0 (95%CI, 0 to 1.0; p 0.018); 1 (95%CI, 1.0 to 1.0; p <0.001) ...], and TMT (B-A) score at Week 8 [by -9.0 (95%CI, -14.0 to -3.0; p 0.009)]. Meanwhile, RAVLT, DST and DCT scores were relatively stable in both groups' (Table 2 prints p 0.038, not 0.018, for SVF at Week 4, and its footnote says only boldface p values survive Bonferroni correction). Mood: 'HAMD score changes were not significantly different between the groups at Weeks 4 and 8, but were markedly distinct at Weeks 1 and 2.' Mediation: 'The definite effects of augmentation therapy with tandospirone citrate on cognitive function were not mediated by depression alleviation.' Because the arms did not differ in HAMD change when the cognitive differences appeared (Weeks 4 and 8), the group-to-HAMD path had nothing to carry, and a null indirect effect in 108 per-protocol patients is an underpowered null, not a demonstration of independence. Authors' own limits: 'the present trial did not primarily aim to examine the mechanism of action of tandospirone in improving cognitive function'; 'this was a small sample study of relatively short duration, raising the possibility of type II errors'; 'the trial design can be improved by combining escitalopram with placebo in the control arm to make double-blind possible and to better control measurement bias'; 'this study used the PPS rather than the full analysis set (FAS) as the major analysis set, which may have resulted in an expansion of positive results.' What the trial tests is whether an add-on 5-HT1A agonist improves two cognitive tests more than an active SSRI comparator; it does not test whether cognitive impairment in vascular depression remits as mood lifts (no remission-stratified analysis, no untreated comparison, 8 weeks). The record's sentence 'so the cognitive benefit is independent of antidepressant mood response' says more than a non-significant mediation supports.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-24 ... set assumption_id=KA-24 with P-621 as anchor.' Its reason does not hold. (1) KA-24's belief ('Cognitive impairment in late-life psychiatric disorders is mood-state-dependent and distinct from MCI, so it does not carry MCI/dementia risk') is not IA-49's prior, and P-621 tests neither dementia risk nor distinctness from MCI: every participant already met MCI criteria and outcomes stop at Week 8. (2) KA-24's provenance says it was implied by the IA records, so anchoring IA-49 on it supplies the prior from the record under test, which the Appendix H.1 independence rule excludes. (3) KA-24 is still only proposed. Registering it would not repair the attestation failure; the correct action is demotion.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not met (not applicable). P-621 is a randomised trial reporting median score changes and GEE group-by-time p-values; it reports no AUC or accuracy and is not in the Section 3.5 performance-validity flag list.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Demote on two independent grounds, either of which suffices. First, the prior is not attested: nowhere in the corpus is the belief that cognitive impairment in late-life or vascular depression is mood-secondary and remits with mood stated as the field's position. The depression-cognition studies in the corpus (P-365, P-559, P-27, P-774, and P-621's own reference list) state persistence after remission as established. So the prior as written is a reviewer-supplied foil that the corpus already contradicts, and P-621 cannot overturn a belief the corpus does not hold. The 'not an independent treatment target' element appears only as a description of clinical practice (P-621, P-559), which the brief excludes. Second, the evidence does not test the prior. P-621 is a single-blind, single-centre, active-comparator, per-protocol trial of an add-on drug; two of five primary tests improved over eight weeks. Its 'independent of mood' conclusion rests on a non-significant mediation, run when the arms did not differ in mood change at the relevant weeks. The authors disclaim any mechanistic aim and warn of type II error and per-protocol inflation. The record's 'independent of antidepressant mood response' overstates this, as does the manuscript's 'behaved as a direct pharmacological target'. There is no attested prior, so no narrower bounded form survives; rescoping would mean inventing a new prior. P-621 can still be cited as a single small trial result, but not as an overturned or bounded assumption, and not as the review's 'RCT-class exemplar'. Process note: this audit regenerated the scratchpad files a10_extract.py, a10_P-621.txt and a10_P-642.txt from the same PDFs, overwriting the drafter's copies. No repository file was touched. Challenger: verdict confirmed after my own extraction of the P-621 PDF. The Table 2 SVF Week-4 p of 0.038 (text: 0.018), the HAMD non-difference at Weeks 4 and 8, the null mediation statement, and the 'did not primarily aim to examine the mechanism of action' disclaimer all check out verbatim. The manuscript quotes at lines 185, 240, 723 and 726 are exact.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Immersive virtual reality is a richer delivery vehicle for the same cognitive-training content as non-immersive computerised games, so it should be at least as effective in MCI - and 'digital cognitive training' can accordingly be treated as one intervention family in synthesis and in guidelines.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-642 (frequentist network meta-analysis, 28 RCTs, 1621 participants, five databases to December 2024, PROSPERO CRD42025636363) separated immersive head-mounted-display VR from non-immersive serious games and found them moving in OPPOSITE directions on global cognition. Non-immersive serious games beat control on both scales - MMSE MD 1.63 (95% CI 0.69 to 2.62) and MoCA MD 2.84 (0.61 to 5.01) - whereas immersive VR produced a statistically significant MMSE DECLINE versus control, MD -1.18 (95% CI -2.18 to -0.20), with no MoCA effect (-0.12, -2.19 to 2.07). Serious games ranked first by SUCRA on every outcome (ADL 77.1%, GDS 83.5%, MMSE 75.4%, MoCA 96%). The authors flag the VR decline as unexplained and note prior reports of transient cognitive decline after VR training, plus sensory overload and motion sickness limiting VR tolerability in older users.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Immersive VR should not be substituted for non-immersive computerised training in MCI on the assumption of equivalence, and syntheses or guidelines that pool the two will average a signal of possible short-term harm against a signal of benefit. Practically: reserve immersive VR for supervised settings with technical support, and prefer home-deliverable non-immersive serious games where the target is global cognition.
invalidated_assumptions.rehabilitation_pathway: Non-immersive tablet or computer serious-game training with minimal supervision for the global-cognition target; immersive VR only under supervision, with short-term cognitive monitoring built in.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-642 summary: 'SG significantly improved global cognition versus control on MMSE (MD 1.63, 95 % CI 0.69 to 2.62) and MoCA (MD 2.84, 95 % CI 0.61 to 5.01), whereas VR showed a significant MMSE decline (MD -1.18, 95 % CI -2.18 to -0.20)'; open problems list 'unexplained short-term MMSE decline under immersive VR'.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: PENDING HUMAN REVIEW. Batch manual_curation_2026-07-31_P620plus. IMPORTANT CAVEAT that must travel with this record: every VR-versus-SG contrast in P-642 is INDIRECT - the network is star-shaped with no closed loops because no direct head-to-head trial exists, so formal inconsistency testing was impossible and the estimate rests on the transitivity assumption. The VR decline is a versus-CONTROL estimate, which is the arm that does not depend on transitivity, so it survives that caveat; the VR-versus-SG ranking does not. Ties to ACTOR-G-023 and to the retained false-positive record C-229.
invalidated_assumptions.human_evaluation_note: CONFIRMED. P-642 provides clean evidence and the transitivity caveat is properly scoped: the VR-versus-control estimate survives ACTOR-G-023's caveat, the VR-versus-SG ranking does not.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: Partial. Attested in the corpus: the belief that immersion gives equal or greater cognitive benefit. P-642 (PDF, introduction): 'This multisensory approach enhances neuroplasticity through enriched environmental stimulation, potentially leading to greater cognitive improvements than conventional therapies [10].' and 'Some studies suggest that VR interventions may offer advantages in enhancing cognitive function and emotional regulation due to their high level of immersion, which enhances training efficacy [21,22].' Discussion: 'Unlike earlier reviews, this study highlights that increased immersion in VR does not necessarily translate into superior cognitive outcomes.' P-841 (summary block, quoting the review): 'In the present review, VR-CRTs resulted to be at least as effective as CRT regardless of the level of immersion.' That is a finding, and it compares VR with face-to-face cognitive rehabilitation, not with computerised games. Not attested: the second half, that ''digital cognitive training' can accordingly be treated as one intervention family in synthesis and in guidelines'. P-642 itself reports that earlier syntheses kept the modalities apart ('these are predominantly pairwise meta-analyses. This means they can only answer questions like "Is VR better than control?" or "Are SG better than control?"'). The linked prior KA-23 is status proposed_2026_08_29 and was generated from IA-50 itself.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: Source: downloads/1. Clinical Assessments, Behavioral and Social Factors/1-s2.0-S0163834325002191-main.pdf (P-642), text plus the Fig. 3 forest plots, which I rendered and inspected. MMSE (Results 3.6): 'SG demonstrated significant cognitive improvement compared to control (mean difference 1.63, 95 % CI: 0.69 to 2.62), while VR was associated with a significant decline compared to control (mean difference -1.18, 95 % CI: -2.18 to -0.20). The indirect comparison between VR and SG showed no statistically significant difference (MD 0.45, 95 % CI: -0.87 to 1.88). Probability ranking analysis (Fig. 4) indicated that SG had a 75.4 % likelihood of being the most effective intervention for MMSE improvement, while VR had a 24.6 % likelihood, and control was most likely to rank lowest (99 %).' These numbers cannot all be true. The network is star-shaped ('no direct head-to-head trials between VR and SG were available'; 'no closed loops were present'), so the network estimates are coherent by construction: VR vs SG = (VR vs control) - (SG vs control) = -1.18 - 1.63 = -2.81 (SE about 0.70, so significant). The reported 0.45 equals 1.63 - 1.18, which is the value you get if VR vs control were +1.18. A ranking in which control is 99% likely to be lowest and VR has a 24.6% chance of being best is also impossible if VR sits significantly below control. The other outcomes repeat the pattern: MoCA indirect 'mean difference of 2.71 (95 % CI: -0.36 to 5.75)' = 2.84 - 0.12, implying VR +0.12 rather than the reported -0.12; GDS indirect -2.22 = -3.18 + 0.98. The GDS forest plot also shows VR vs Control at about +2.7 with a CI of about 0.9 to 4.5, against the text's 'MD 0.98, 95 % CI: -2.63 to 4.52'. The quality section says '12 of the 19 studies scored >=7 points' although 28 studies were included. So the load-bearing VR MMSE 'decline' contradicts the paper's own indirect estimate and rankings. The pattern fits a sign reversal of the VR-vs-control estimates, under which VR would have improved MMSE against control. Also, the comparator was not inert ('The control group consisted of conventional approaches, including usual care, standard cognitive training programs, traditional rehabilitation therapies, or no intervention'), so 'decline versus control' is not a within-person decline. The authors themselves hedge: 'the observed MMSE decline should be interpreted cautiously as a short-term phenomenon rather than evidence of long-term cognitive deterioration'; 'the results should not be interpreted as definitive indications of superiority for either modality'; 'VR and SG should be viewed as promising but still provisional approaches'. Every VR-vs-SG contrast (ADL, GDS, MMSE, MoCA) was indirect and non-significant, so the prior that VR is at least as effective as SG is not contradicted by any significant estimate. The record's 'moving in OPPOSITE directions' and the manuscript's 'possible harm' both rest on the incoherent number. The record's 'The authors flag the VR decline as unexplained' is also inexact: the authors call it 'unexpected' and offer explanations (acute fatigue, simulator sickness). Challenger re-check (own extraction of the same PDF plus the rendered Fig. 3/Fig. 4 pages): the MMSE forest plot in Fig. 3 plots 'VR vs SG' at about +0.45 and 'VR vs Control' at about -1.18 in the same panel, so the figure is incoherent as well as the text, and its row labels are themselves inconsistent ('Control vs SG' is plotted at +1.63, the SG-favouring value). The Fig. 4 MMSE rank probability of SG being best (75.4%) matches the reported indirect estimate, not the reported VR decline: with MD 0.45 and SE about 0.70 (CI -0.87 to 1.88), P(SG better than VR) = Phi(0.45/0.70), about 0.74. So the ranking model behaves as if VR-versus-control were about +1.18. That does not prove the sign of the published -1.18 is wrong, but it does mean the load-bearing number cannot be relied on.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-23 ... set assumption_id=KA-23; keep the star-network/indirect-contrast caveat verbatim.' Partly right that an immersion-advantage belief exists in the corpus (P-642 introduction; P-841), but its reason for keeping the record fails. The caveat it preserves ('The VR decline is a versus-CONTROL estimate, which is the arm that does not depend on transitivity, so it survives that caveat') assumes the versus-control MMSE estimate is sound, and that is exactly the number the paper's own indirect estimate and rankings contradict. KA-23 was also written from IA-50 itself, and its 'one intervention family' element is unattested. Registering KA-23 would not rescue a record whose disproving evidence is internally inconsistent; demote.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not met (not applicable). P-642 is a network meta-analysis reporting mean differences on MMSE, MoCA, ADL and GDS; it reports no AUC or accuracy and is not in the Section 3.5 performance-validity flag list.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Demote because the evidence does not test the prior reliably. The prior is only half attested: the immersion-advantage belief appears in P-642's introduction and in P-841, but the 'one intervention family in synthesis and guidelines' half does not. The record's disproof rests entirely on P-642's VR-versus-control MMSE estimate (-1.18). In a star-shaped network with no closed loops, that estimate cannot coexist with the paper's reported VR-versus-SG estimate (0.45 = 1.63 - 1.18) or with its ranking (control 99% likely lowest; VR 24.6% likely best). MoCA and GDS show the same arithmetic pattern, and the GDS forest plot disagrees with the text. Either the VR-versus-control signs are reversed, in which case VR improved MMSE, or the indirect estimates and rankings are wrong. Neither reading can be settled from the source. With the load-bearing number unreliable, what remains is non-significant indirect VR-versus-SG contrasts on every outcome and a difference in significance on MoCA. Neither is a disproof of 'VR at least as effective', and the authors explicitly decline to claim superiority for either modality. No narrower bounded form survives without resting on the incoherent estimate, so this is demote, not rescope. The manuscript's 'possible harm' framing in Section 4.8 goes further than even the authors do (they call the decline a probable short-term phenomenon) and should be removed with the clause. P-642's internal inconsistency is not recorded in the P-642 summary block, which notes only the 12-of-19 counting slip. It should be added to the summary block's limitations at the next freeze. Challenger: verdict confirmed. I found no evidence that rescues a narrower form. The only other corpus source on immersion level (P-841, a review, per its summary block) found VR cognitive rehabilitation 'at least as effective as CRT regardless of the level of immersion', which is consistent with the prior rather than against it.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: A fall in plasma amyloid-beta-42 under an intervention is a favourable target-engagement signal, readable in the same direction as the accompanying cognitive improvement.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-649 (four-arm randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial, 280 community-dwelling MCI adults aged 65+, Tianjin, ChiCTR2200059641, 12 months) reports plasma Abeta42 DECREASING in all three active arms - MCT beta -3.318 (95% CI -5.571 to -1.064, p = 0.0044), DHA beta -3.218 (-5.472 to -0.965, p = 0.0057), MCT+DHA beta -2.906 (-5.160 to -0.653, p = 0.0124) - alongside cognitive gains, and the Abeta42/Abeta40 ratio falling in the MCT arm (beta -0.006, -0.023 to -0.001, p = 0.0413) while Abeta40 was unchanged in every arm. The paper reads the amyloid movement as part of a favourable mechanistic picture. But a falling plasma Abeta42, and specifically a falling Abeta42/Abeta40 ratio with Abeta40 held constant, is the direction conventionally associated with GREATER cerebral amyloid sequestration and with amyloid positivity - so the biomarker arm is at minimum directionally ambiguous and may point opposite to the cognitive arm. The paper commits to no pre-specified direction of benefit for these markers and its authors state that mechanism must be interpreted cautiously because only peripheral blood, and no cerebrospinal fluid or imaging, was collected.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Peripheral amyloid readouts in MCI intervention trials must have their direction of benefit PRE-SPECIFIED, and the Abeta42/Abeta40 ratio reported alongside the individual species, or the biomarker arm cannot be used to support a mechanistic claim in either direction. In this trial the mitochondrial readouts (mtDNA deletions falling, beta -0.370 to -0.427, p = 0.0030 to 0.0197) and the ketone readouts (serum total ketone body rising, beta 5.884 to 13.186, all p < 0.0001) are unambiguous target-engagement markers; the amyloid readouts are not.
invalidated_assumptions.rehabilitation_pathway: Not a treatment-pathway record: this is a trial-reporting standard. Recommend that MCI supplementation trials pre-register the expected direction of any fluid amyloid endpoint and pair plasma measurement with CSF or amyloid PET in a substudy.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-649 summary: 'plasma Abeta42 decreased in MCT (beta -3.318, p = 0.0044), DHA (beta -3.218, p = 0.0057) and MCT + DHA (beta -2.906, p = 0.0124)'; 'the Abeta42/Abeta40 ratio fell only in the MCT group (beta -0.006, p = 0.0413)'; 'Glucose, insulin, IRI, mtDNA copy number and Abeta40 were unchanged'; author-stated limitation: 'reliance on blood rather than cerebrospinal fluid or brain imaging indicators so that the mechanism of action must be interpreted cautiously'.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: PENDING HUMAN REVIEW. Batch manual_curation_2026-07-31_P620plus. This record makes a claim about INTERPRETIVE ambiguity, not about harm: it does not assert that MCT/DHA supplementation worsens amyloid pathology, only that the paper's plasma amyloid result cannot support the favourable reading it is given without a pre-specified direction and a central (CSF or PET) anchor. G5 should check the direction convention against the current plasma-amyloid literature before confirming, since the interpretation of plasma Abeta42/40 has moved. Ties to ACTOR-G-022.
invalidated_assumptions.human_evaluation_note: NOT CONFIRMED - HELD PENDING LITERATURE VERIFICATION (operator, G5 2026-07-31). Plasma Abeta42 direction is genuinely tricky: interpretation depends on assay, the Abeta42/Abeta40 ratio, disease stage, peripheral clearance, and PET/CSF confirmation. Retained as a proposed record; must not be cited as an invalidated assumption until the direction convention is checked against the current plasma-amyloid literature.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_operator_verdict_2026_08_15: HOLD affirmed - keep at pending_literature_verification. Plasma Abeta42/Abeta40 direction conventions are assay-, stage-, and context-dependent; do not treat as confirmed or cite in confirmed tables until the direction convention is externally validated against the current plasma-amyloid literature.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Prospective interval timing is SPARED in MCI - the standing conclusion of the timing literature (Mioni et al. 2019, whose title states the lack of temporal impairment in MCI; Coelho et al. 2016; Rueda & Schmitter-Edgecombe 2009), reproduced by random-effects synthesis.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-659 (PRISMA multi-level meta-analysis; 12 studies / 14 samples / 80 effect sizes, of which 64 prospective / 562 participants) shows the null MCI result is MEASUREMENT-CONFOUNDED and therefore uninformative about sparing. TYPE OF DEPENDENT MEASURE is a directly estimated, significant moderator of whether a timing deficit is detected at all: entered alone F(2,61)=10.78, p<.0001, R-sq=.40; in the AICc-selected model accuracy beta=-0.50, p<.0001 and variability beta=-0.38, p=.002, both more sensitive than raw mean-estimate scores. Only 3 of 5 independent MCI samples used those sensitive accuracy/variability indices, against 6 of 6 AD samples, and MCI sample ages spanned a narrow 68.4-72.3y. The authors state the consequence directly: 'the current negative MCI literature cannot be treated as evidence of preserved timing.' WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: that MCI timing is impaired. The only DIRECTLY pooled MCI-vs-control estimate remains null (g=-0.08, 95% CI [-0.23, 0.07], z=-1.04, p=.309). The g=-0.41 [-0.60,-0.21] is a MODEL-FITTED prediction at age 70 with absolute error as DV, with slopes estimated largely from AD samples - not a measured MCI effect. NET: MCI prospective timing moves from SPARED (established) to UNRESOLVED (the null is uninformative).
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: The negative MCI timing literature cannot be cited as evidence that timing is preserved. Any future study testing the belief must score timing on ACCURACY or VARIABILITY indices (absolute error, percent error, bisection point, CV, SD, Weber ratio) across a wide age range and report MCI subtype; a null obtained with mean-estimate scores does not test the belief.
invalidated_assumptions.rehabilitation_pathway: Adopt accuracy/variability scoring for timing tasks in MCI research; do not exclude timing from prodromal marker panels on the strength of the existing nulls. Whether a true MCI timing deficit exists remains open and requires a directly-measured, adequately-powered MCI contrast using sensitive indices.
invalidated_assumptions.verified_by: claude_delegated_g5_judgment (operator-delegated 2026-08-02; adversarial source re-verification, 3 independent verifier-adjudicators)
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-659 [Results]: 'Split by condition, AD showed g = -0.72 ... whereas MCI did not differ from controls, g = -0.08, 95% CI [-0.23, 0.07], p = .309.' [Results]: measure type entered alone F(2,61)=10.78, p<.0001, R-sq=.40; AICc model accuracy beta=-0.50 p<.0001, variability beta=-0.38 p=.002. [Problems]: 'only 3 of 5 independent MCI samples used the more sensitive accuracy or variability measures, against 6 of 6 for AD'. [Why is it important?]: 'the current negative MCI literature cannot be treated as evidence of preserved timing.'
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: DELEGATED G5 VERDICT: ACCEPT WITH MANDATORY RESCOPE (operator-delegated, human_confirmed=false). R1 quote grounding PASSES - every statistic verbatim and in Results/Key-findings fields, not spin fields. R2 prior belief PASSES cleanly - P-659 states the standing belief in three separate fields and cites the exact sources the miner named. R3 FAILED as originally proposed: the miner asserted a directional MCI deficit from a model-FITTED counterfactual (age 70, absolute error) while the only directly estimated MCI contrast is null; the fitted value borrows measure-type and age slopes from a corpus where 6/6 AD but only 3/5 MCI samples used sensitive indices (extrapolation from AD into a sparse MCI cell); R-sq=.91 rests on only 14 independent clusters, age flips from p=.258 alone to p=.001 adjusted in a direction the authors cannot explain (collinearity signature), and residual Q(59)=84.48, p=.017 is still significant so 'negligible residual heterogeneity' overstates the fit. DECISIVE: P-659 itself refuses the directional conclusion - 'the review cannot decide whether prospective timing is genuinely spared in MCI', lists the fitted-vs-observed discrepancy as the crux open problem, and is commended in its own record for reporting the discrepancy rather than choosing the convenient value. Storing a directional reversal would contradict the source. RESCOPED AND ACCEPTED because the moderator coefficients ARE directly estimated and significant both alone and in the model, and together with the audited 3-of-5 measurement gap they establish a genuine, author-endorsed invalidation of a weaker but real kind: the inference from null to spared is broken. This is an EPISTEMIC invalidation (measurement-artifact class, cf. IA-14), not a directional one. MINER-ADDED CLAUSE DROPPED: 'so timing tasks are not useful prodromal markers' - nothing in the source attributes that corollary to the field.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Confidence MEDIUM. The accepted claim is about the INFORMATIVENESS of the existing null, not about the existence of an MCI timing deficit. Do not let downstream consumers restate this as 'MCI timing is impaired'. n=111 MCI across 5 samples (one as small as 10 vs 24 controls); MCI MMSE means ranged from below 24 to above 27 so patients were at different stages; only one sample specified amnestic subtype.
invalidated_assumptions.dedup_note: No canonical IA covers interval timing; checked IA-28/32/35/36/47 (all verified to exist) plus a keyword sweep over all 51 IA prior_beliefs - no overlap. Nearest in KIND is IA-14 (reported metrics reflect artifact rather than the construct), which is a different domain.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: Attested only in a weak, hedged form. P-659 PDF Introduction: 'Contrary to this expectation, results from the few timing studies in MCI show no differences in judgment of time between MCI patients and control groups [19,20,129]. Of note, however, it should be considered that clinical studies of timing in both MCI and AD patients are often characterized by small sample sizes, which overall challenges their conclusions.' Discussion: 'The finding of significant group differences for AD patients and the lack of significant ones for MCI patients favour the idea that temporal processing is compromised in AD but not MCI, in line with previous reports (e.g., [124]).' The record's 'standing conclusion ... reproduced by random-effects synthesis' framing is summary-block language, and the synthesis is P-659's own result. P-887 (Mioni, Wolbers, Riemer 2024; downloads/1. Clinical Assessments, Behavioral and Social Factors/1-s2.0-S2589958924000161-main.pdf) says: 'When comparing MCI patients and controls, the results are more inconsistent and depend on the patients' age, the range of tested intervals and the timing task employed'. P-887 is itself a direct aMCI timing study that reports a deficit: 'The results revealed a bias towards larger PSE values and reduced precision in aMCI patients compared to healthy controls'; Conclusion: 'The results of the present study indicate impaired timing behaviour in aMCI patients for both sub-second and supra-second intervals' (with the caveat 'The aMCI patient group is quite small'). So 'SPARED (established)' is not an attested settled belief. Registry prior KA-49 has status proposed_2026_09_09 and was generated from this record.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: Source: downloads/1. Clinical Assessments, Behavioral and Social Factors/1-s2.0-S0166432821002424-main.pdf (P-659; DOI 10.1016/j.bbr.2021.113354). Direct MCI test: 'unlike patients with MCI who did not significantly differ from healthy controls, g = -0.08, 95 % CI [-0.23, 0.07], z = -1.04, p = .309'. That agrees with the prior. The deficit is fitted only: 'with MCI, g = -0.41, 95 % CI [-0.60, -0.21] (assuming a mean age of 70 years old and using absolute error as dependent variable)'. The source adds 'a substantial discrepancy for MCI, probably due in part to the reduced number of studies that used more sensitive measures ... 3 out of 5 independent samples for MCI vs 6 out of 6 for AD'. Authors: 'the discrepant results of the random-effect and meta-regression model for MCI patients do not allow drawing firm conclusions on the question of whether prospective timing is affected in MCI. In line with previous research on this population, the results of the random-effect model could be taken indeed as evidence for the lack of a temporal impairment in MCI patients [20].' Also: 'such conclusions, at least regarding MCI patients, were not fully confirmed in a further meta-regression analysis'. The moderator stats (F(2,61) = 10.78, p < .0001, R2 = .40) are real but pooled over AD and MCI, not estimated within MCI. The record's decisive quote, 'the current negative MCI literature cannot be treated as evidence of preserved timing', is NOT in the PDF (no hit for 'cannot be treated', 'preserved', 'spared'). It is summary-block text. The review_note quote 'the review cannot decide whether prospective timing is genuinely spared in MCI' is also absent from the PDF.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'DEMOTE:the accepted claim is epistemic ('the null cannot evidence sparing'), not a disproof - the record's own rescope removed the directional claim. Demote to 'proposed' and record P-659 as a gap.' The reason holds, and the PDF strengthens it. The direct MCI estimate agrees with the prior, the deficit is model-fitted from mostly AD slopes, and the authors decline to conclude. On the gap half: P-659 already claims open gap ACTOR-G-024, so check against it before adding a timing gap. P-887's small-sample aMCI deficit could be noted there as well.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged. P-659 is a meta-analysis of standardised mean differences with no AUC or accuracy.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Demote. (1) The prior is attested only as a hedged 'few studies show no differences'. A later corpus study (P-887) calls the literature inconsistent and itself reports an aMCI deficit. (2) P-659's direct MCI contrast is null and agrees with the prior. The MCI deficit is a counterfactual fit driven by AD slopes, and the authors say they cannot conclude either way. An argument that a null is weak is a gap, not an invalidated assumption. (3) The record's decisive author quote, and a second one in its review_note, are block text absent from the PDF, so the anchor does not reconcile with the source (H.1). A 'bounded' rescope was re-tested on 'not fully confirmed' and rejected, because that is an author judgment about an inconclusive model contrast, not an MCI-measured bound. P-887 cannot be substituted as the anchor without a fresh record, attestation and power check. (4) Not flagged.

invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: [PROPOSED, REJECTED] P-615 (frequentist NMA, 53 RCTs / 4582 participants) reported digital reminiscence therapy ranked best for cognitive function (SUCRA 93.6%) and depressive symptoms (SUCRA 94.9%), with individual best for QoL (98.3%) and group best for adherence (95.6%).

invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-615 [Results]: 'Digital reminiscence therapy ranked best for cognitive function (SMD 5.02 vs treatment-as-usual; SUCRA 93.6%) and depressive symptoms (SUCRA 94.9%).' Quotation is accurate; the rejection is not about quotation.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: DELEGATED G5 VERDICT: REJECT - FALSE POSITIVE. R1 (quote grounding) is the ONLY check that passes: all three numbers are verbatim and sit in the Results field. Accurate quotation of a number does not make that number a belief-reversal. Three independent defects, each individually sufficient: (1) STRAWMAN PRIOR BELIEF. P-615 nowhere states that digital delivery is expected to be inferior; it states EQUIPOISE - 'which delivery format is most effective for which outcome was unclear, and head-to-head comparisons across formats were lacking' - and its own conclusion is the neutral 'Delivery format matters'. The corpus's actual position runs the other way: P-675 argues the effect holds across intervention labels because 'regardless of the form of group reminiscence intervention, the essence of the intervention is similar', i.e. format-AGNOSTIC. config/assumption_registry.json contains no reminiscence/delivery-format assumption. The belief was constructed in order to be knocked down. (2) THE SUCRA RESCUE IS BACKWARDS. The miner conceded SMD 5.02 is a sparse-network artifact but claimed the SUCRA ranking is the robust object. SUCRA is not independent of the estimate - it is computed by simulating from the fitted relative-effect estimates and their variance-covariance matrix, and it specifically REWARDS extreme point estimates while penalising imprecision only weakly. So SUCRA 93.6% is high PRECISELY BECAUSE of the 5.02. An SMD of 5.02 on a cognitive outcome (where real effects run 0.2-0.5) is a data-extraction fault signature. You cannot discard the estimate and keep the ranking it generated. (3) SCOPE - THE SOURCE DECLARES THE MCI QUESTION OPEN. The network pools dementia AND MCI (stated four times in the block), and P-615 lists 'MCI-specific format effects' as an OPEN PROBLEM and requests 'MCI-specific subgroups'. An MCI-specific belief-reversal is therefore contradicted by its own evidence. Reminiscence therapy is a dementia-dominated literature (P-675: 'developed and evaluated predominantly in dementia'). (4) SELF-UNDERMINING USE OF RANKINGS: individual-QoL (98.3%) and group-adherence (95.6%) are HIGHER SUCRAs from the same sparse network. Either all four rankings are trustworthy - in which case the finding is 'different formats suit different outcomes', the authors' neutral conclusion and not a reversal - or none are. NO RESCOPE POSSIBLE: strip the artifactual magnitude, the invented prior and the MCI-specific scope, and what remains is a descriptive gap-closure with no belief overturned. CONSTRUCTIVE REDIRECT: P-615's real KB contribution is (a) a GAP - the paper itself names MCI-specific format effects as open - and (b) a data-quality flag on its Best_Metric field so downstream consumers do not propagate SUCRA 93.6% / SMD 5.02 as a settled comparative-effectiveness result.
invalidated_assumptions.dedup_note: Novel vs the 51 existing IAs (no reminiscence IA); nearest IA-50 (immersive VR) correctly identified by the miner as a different intervention class. Dedup was accurate - the rejection is on evidentiary grounds, not duplication.

invalidated_assumptions.review_note: DELEGATED G5 VERDICT: REJECT - FALSE POSITIVE (credit to the miner for flagging the FDR failure itself; the record was honestly presented, and it is being rejected on exactly the ground it disclosed). (1) FAILS THE SOURCE'S OWN PRE-SPECIFIED CORRECTION. The ordered 3-group NDI omnibus in left CA1-3 - the only test capable of establishing a monotonic-direction claim - fails the paper's pre-specified Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (F=3.178, P=0.044, PFDR=0.066), in a paper where every other reported regional effect cleared it (PFDR 0.005-0.048). The design is ANCOVA + Tukey post hoc, so pairwise contrasts are conditioned on the omnibus; falling back to the nominally significant 2-group contrast selects the survivor from the very family the correction exists to police. (2) THE REVERSAL-BEARING RESULT CARRIES NO STATISTIC. The 2-group clause reports no F, no p, no effect size and no FDR status; the numbers sit in Supplementary Material 2 Tables 5-8, which the corpus record does not reproduce. (3) PLAUSIBLE FITTING ARTIFACT, AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO. NDI is a fitted NODDI/AMICO model parameter, not an assayed neurite density. It rose in the SAME region and SAME contrast where FISO also rose, and the record flags FISO as CSF-partial-volume contaminated at 2 mm z-resolution. The authors themselves call it a 'pseudo-increase in NDI'. (4) THE AUTHORS DECLINED TO CLAIM IT. The result is filed under 'Open problems', and NDI is omitted from both the paper's significance statement and its Key Novelty ('NODDI FISO/ODI ... detect CSVD-MCI damage before volume loss'). The KB must not assert as a confirmed reversal something the source authors deliberately declined to assert. (5) THE FIELD ALREADY CARRIES THE EXCEPTION. The same source sentence aligns the NDI increase WITH published gliosis-attributed NDI increases in Parkinson disease (Ogawa 2021; Wei 2024) and post-ECT (Le Berre 2025). The paper positions itself as concordant with existing literature. Extending a known alternative pattern into a new population is replication/extension, not a belief reversal. (6) MONOTONICITY IS UNTESTABLE HERE - no dementia arm exists, so the ordered impairment axis is truncated. Also cross-sectional, single-centre, V2, no replication; and the group labelling is internally unclean (MMSE did not differ across groups, F=2.461 P=0.089, despite being an inclusion criterion; CSVD-MCI MMSE mean 27.86 sits ABOVE its own stated 24-26 inclusion window; HC MoCA 26.50 < CSVD-NC MoCA 27.31). NO RESCOPE POSSIBLE: any wording faithful to the evidence stops asserting a belief was overturned, at which point it is no longer an IA. CONSTRUCTIVE REDIRECT: store as a GAP / open-question - 'direction of NODDI NDI change in hippocampal CA1-3 at the MCI stage is unresolved in CSVD' - with the FDR failure, the unquantified pairwise contrast and the authors' speculative gliosis/edema reading recorded as the reason it is open.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Physical exercise interventions have a moderate, clinically relevant effect on the cognitive function of older adults. This is the conclusion of earlier syntheses as P-249 reports them: 'previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses that recognized a moderate and clinically relevant effect of physical exercise interventions on the cognitive function of older adults'. Exercise is also regarded as among the most effective non-pharmacological strategies against cognitive decline in MCI (P-680).
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-249 is the only corpus synthesis restricted to long-term (>=12-month) RCTs in non-demented community-dwelling older adults (16 trials, 11,402 participants, low risk of bias; mostly cognitively healthy or at-risk adults, three trials in MCI). In it, exercise alone had a small effect on global cognition: SMD 0.05 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.13; p=0.25; k=9; moderate certainty). The upper bound excludes a moderate or larger benefit but not a small one. The same estimate was significant in the authors' DerSimonian-Laird sensitivity analysis (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09), so the result limits the size of the benefit rather than showing there is none. In the three MCI trials the estimate was SMD 0.06 (95% CI -0.10 to 0.21). Multidomain programmes including exercise gave SMD 0.09 (0.04 to 0.15), compared with exercise alone only indirectly. The results for incident MCI (RR 0.98, 0.73 to 1.31; very low certainty) and dementia (RR 0.61, 0.25 to 1.52; low certainty; significant only under a fixed-effect sensitivity analysis) do not test a risk-reduction belief.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Over twelve months or more in non-demented older adults, exercise alone should be expected to improve global cognition by a small amount at most. The upper bound of SMD 0.13 excludes the moderate effect earlier syntheses reported. The larger pooled effects of short programmes in diagnosed MCI answer a different question and are not contradicted. This evidence does not settle whether exercise alone lowers incident MCI or dementia. Bounded, not refuted.

verification.verifier_reason: ACCEPT WITH RESCOPE. The record's core has the shape this KB's confirmed IAs have (IA-23, IA-15): a DIRECT, MEASURED, within-synthesis head-to-head - exercise-alone (k=9, SMD 0.05, ns) versus multidomain (k=7, SMD 0.09, sig) inside ONE 16-RCT/11,402-participant, low-risk-of-bias, GRADE-assessed meta-analysis - set against a belief the field demonstrably holds and that I could quote verbatim as the standing view rather than infer. It survives the FP codes that kill most IA candidates: not a strawman (no equipoise language about WHETHER exercise helps - the corpus's uncertainty is about WHICH modality); not refused by the source (I read P-249's `What are the problems?` and `Potential gaps or limitations` - heterogeneity, publication bias, adherence, diverse batteries, no declination); not buried (the null is in Results, Key findings AND Significance); fully quantified; not a fitted value; and not a duplicate (54 IA records checked - no exercise IA exists; P-249 appears in no consensus record). Quote discipline is excellent: all 13 quotes verbatim, all fields correctly tagged, interpretive fields used only to document belief. WHAT FORCES THE RESCOPE rather than a clean accept: three defects in the statement as written. First and most serious, the belief-evidence and the disproof are in DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. The SMD/g 0.65-1.165 band comes from short, end-of-programme trials in already-diagnosed MCI; P-249 is a >=12-month prevention synthesis in non-demented community-dwelling older adults. The miner's own scope clause concedes the short-trial effects stand - which means those five estimates cannot also be the thing that got reversed. Second, "precise enough to exclude even a small benefit" is factually wrong: the upper bound of 0.13 is larger than the 0.09 the same paper

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief_pre_2026_09_26: Physical exercise on its own is a robust, established modifiable protective factor that lowers MCI/dementia risk in older adults - stated as settled in the corpus (P-251 'Why did the authors conduct the research?': 'Exercise has emerged as a robust modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline across epidemiological studies and RCTs'; P-680 'Why is it important?': 'Exercise is the most widely recommended non-pharmacological intervention for MCI'), and carried by the epidemiological ~45% AD-risk reduction (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.36-0.84) that P-251 restates.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it_pre_2026_09_26: IA. PRIOR BELIEF (demonstrably held, quotable): physical exercise on its own is a robust, established modifiable risk factor that protects cognition and lowers MCI/dementia risk in older adults - stated in the corpus as settled (P-251 `### Why did the authors conduct the research?`: "Exercise has emerged as a robust modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline across epidemiological studies and RCTs"; P-680 `### Why is it important?`: "Exercise is the most widely recommended non-pharmacological intervention for MCI") and carried by the epidemiological estimate P-251 restates from the external literature (`### What are the outcomes? (Results)`, explicitly prefaced "Epidemiological evidence (cited from other studies)"): "a meta-analysis of 16 studies (>160,000 participants) reported a ~45% reduction in AD risk with regular physical activity (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.36-0.84)". WHAT DISPROVED IT: P-249, the corpus's only synthesis restricted to LONG-TERM (>=12-month) RCTs (16 trials, 11,402 participants, low overall risk of bias, GRADE-assessed), measures exercise ALONE at SMD 0.05 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.13; p=0.25; k=9) on global cognition at MODERATE certainty, while the MULTIDOMAIN arm of the SAME synthesis is significant (SMD 0.09; 95% CI 0.04 to 0.15; p<0.01; k=7). The within-synthesis contrast is the load-bearing evidence: over >=12 months, exercise alone is indistinguishable from control on the same outcome, on the same evidence base, analysed the same way. What the interval excludes is a MODERATE-TO-LARGE benefit: the upper bound of 0.13 sits below Cohen's small-effect threshold and an order of magnitude below the SMD/g 0.65-1.165 band the corpus's short MCI-treatment meta-analyses report. It does NOT exclude a trivial benefit - 0.13 is in fact larger than the 0.09 the same paper calls "small but significant". SECONDARY, VERY-LOW/LOW CERTAINTY (carried, not asserted): exercise did not alter incident MCI (RR 0.98; 95% CI 0.73-1.31; p=0.79; very-low certainty) or dementia onset (RR 0.61; 95% CI 0.25-1.52; p=0.19; low certainty). By the source's own GRADE these are too weak to establish a reversal of the risk-reduction belief; they are directionally consistent only, and P-249's authors themselves "call for further research on exercise to mitigate MCI/dementia risk". SCOPE LIMITS (explicit, three): (i) POPULATION - the moderate-certainty null is in non-demented community-dwelling older adults, a MIXED cognitively-normal-plus-MCI prevention population; it is NOT an MCI-specific finding, and the only MCI-specific endpoint (incident MCI) is very-low certainty. (ii) EXPOSURE AND ENDPOINT - exercise ALONE, delivered as a >=12-month programme, on global cognition. It does NOT extend to multidomain packages (significant in the same synthesis) and does NOT claim that short supervised exercise programmes in already-diagnosed MCI produce no end-of-programme improvement; those effects (P-674 pooled SMD 0.65 [0.39-0.91]; P-698 SMD 0.76; P-680 1.165 [0.741-1.589]; P-613 SMD 1.04 [0.53-1.55]; P-603 Hedges' g 0.978 [0.298-1.659]) are in a different population answering a different question, and they stand. Those five are cited here only to show the magnitude of benefit the field expects, and they are NOT five independent estimates - P-698's `### Related findings` warns that P-674 and P-698 share authors (Ahn & Kim) with "overlap in included trials ... likely substantial", and P-603/P-613 pool multicomponent rather than single-modality programmes. (iii) RELATION TO VF-30 - VF-30 already holds that pooled MCI-intervention estimates are large but statistically fragile, and P-680/P-698 report prediction intervals crossing zero (-0.747 to 3.077; -0.63 to 2.15). This record's increment over VF-30 is NOT fragility but a directly measured, moderate-certainty, near-zero point estimate from the longest and largest evidence base; the fragility framing is corroboration, not the claim. PROVENANCE FLAG FOR G5: the entire disproof rests on one summary block whose earlier version was fabricated and INVERTED this exact result; it carries a 2026-06-26 correction note against PMID 39179115 that names the specific figures it replaced. The remediation reads as genuine and internally consistent, but the operator should re-verify SMD 0.05 / SMD 0.09 / RR 0.98 against PMID 39179115 before confirming.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication_pre_2026_09_26: Long-term (>=12-month) RCT evidence does not support exercise ALONE as a disease-modifying protector of global cognition; multidomain programmes retain a small but significant effect on the same evidence base. Separate symptomatic/functional benefit from disease modification when advising or designing trials.

readjudication_2026_09_26.attestation: Primary (added by challenger): the P-249 PDF itself, Discussion, reporting what the field's earlier syntheses concluded rather than its own hypothesis: 'Our findings are only partly consistent with previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses that recognized a moderate and clinically relevant effect of physical exercise interventions on the cognitive function of older adults (De Souto Barreto et al., 2018; Gallardo-Gomez et al., 2022; Northey et al., 2018).' Its Introduction records that the belief is contested: 'A recent umbrella review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) has cast doubt on the cognitive benefits of physical exercise interventions' and 'meta-analyses have failed to consistently corroborate the hypothesis that exercise interventions can effectively mitigate the risk of clinically meaningful cognitive deterioration, MCI, or the advent of dementia'. Independent corpus source: P-680 PDF (downloads/1. Clinical Assessments, Behavioral and Social Factors/1-s2.0-S0167494324002176-main.pdf), Introduction: 'Exercise is considered among the most effective nonpharmacological strategies to prevent cognitive decline in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and prevent dementia in further stages of MCI (Petersen et al., 2018).' The record's lead anchor P-251 cannot be used. data/paper_pdf_map.json maps it to downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S001048252401388X-main.pdf, and a fresh extract of that file is 'Plasma protein-based identification of neuroimage-driven subtypes in mild cognitive impairment via protein-protein interaction aware explainable graph propagational network' (Park et al., doi 10.1016/j.compbiomed.2024.109303; the same file is also mapped to P-10). The quote therefore reconciles with no corpus source. P-806 shares authors with P-249 (NI-10). The belief is attested but contested, so 'robust, established ... stated as settled' overstates it.
readjudication_2026_09_26.evidence: P-249 PDF (downloads/1. Clinical Assessments, Behavioral and Social Factors/1-s2.0-S1568163724002812-main.pdf; Reparaz-Escudero et al. 2024, doi 10.1016/j.arr.2024.102463; minus signs restored). Abstract: 'Sixteen trials, including 11,402 participants ... The risk of bias was low. Moderate-certainty evidence indicated that physical exercise interventions had modest to no effect on cognitive function (k=9, SMD: 0.05; 95 % CI: -0.04-0.13; p=0.25), whereas multidomain interventions were significantly impactful (k=7, SMD: 0.09; 95 % CI: 0.04-0.15; p<0.01). Physical exercise interventions did not alter MCI risk (k=4, RR: 0.98; 95 % CI: 0.73-1.31; p=0.79) or dementia onset (k=4, RR: 0.61; 95 % CI: 0.25-1.52; p=0.19), with very low-to low-certainty evidence, respectively.' Conclusion: 'long-term physical exercise alone did not yield any cognitive gains.' Population: 'community-dwelling older adults with a mean age >=60 years who were either cognitively healthy or diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) at baseline'. MCI trials: van Uffelen 2008 and Lam 2012 and 2015. MCI subgroup: 'a negligible impact on participants diagnosed with MCI at baseline (SMD 0.06; 95%CI: -0.10, 0.21)'. GRADE: moderate 'primarily because of inconsistency in the observed direction of effect'; 'very low for the effect of exercise interventions on the risk of MCI and low for the risk of dementia'. Omitted by the record: 'a random-effects meta-analysis was employed using DerSimonian and Laird's inverse-variance method. This analysis revealed a significant effect of long-term physical exercise (SMD 0.05; 95% CI: 0.01-0.09, p=0.02)', and 'a fixed-effects meta-analysis revealed a significant reduction in dementia risk related to exercise interventions (fixed-effects model: RR=0.65; 95%CI: 0.45, 0.93, p=0.02)'. There is no formal test between the exercise-alone and multidomain arms. What this settles: at moderate certainty, the upper bound of 0.13 excludes a moderate or larger long-term benefit of exercise alone, so the prior is bounded. P-249 does not support 'indistinguishable from control', the 0.05 vs 0.09 contrast as load-bearing evidence, any test of risk reduction or of the HR 0.55, or 'disease-modifying'.
readjudication_2026_09_26.audit_2026_08_29_assessment: Recommendation: 'ADD_NEW_PRIOR:KA-22 ... set assumption_id=KA-22 with P-249 as anchor; scope to >=12-month prevention trials as the record already states.' The scope half holds and is kept. The prior half does not, for three reasons. KA-22 was registered from IA-67 and IA-29 themselves, which is circular. It bundles exercise with BMI, diet and sleep, although P-266 found low physical activity associated with MCI. And its disproof signal sits on incident MCI and dementia, exactly the part of P-249 that is very-low or low certainty and that, for dementia, points toward a benefit from exercise. IA-67 should instead carry a separate prior on the efficacy of exercise as an intervention, worded as in new_text.prior_belief. That prior is attested by the P-249 Discussion's report of earlier syntheses and independently by P-680. The operator still has to confirm it as a registered prior.
readjudication_2026_09_26.performance_flag: Not flagged: P-249 is a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs reporting SMDs and risk ratios, with no AUC or accuracy.
readjudication_2026_09_26.reasoning: Rescope, bounded. The P-249 figures are transcribed correctly, the study is not flagged, and the prior on exercise's efficacy is attested. The record as written fails on four counts. (1) P-251 does not reconcile with any source document: its mapped PDF is the plasma-protein classifier paper, which the challenger confirmed by re-extracting it. (2) The prior is framed as a settled risk-reduction belief carried by the observational HR 0.55, which P-249 does not test. (3) 'Indistinguishable from control' is contradicted by the significant DerSimonian-Laird result, and the 0.05 vs 0.09 contrast is indirect with no formal test. (4) 'Disease-modifying' is not in the source. The challenger also changed the prior. The auditor's 'among the most effective strategies' is a relative-ranking claim that P-249 does not test, because it compares exercise only with multidomain packages that themselves contain exercise. What P-249 does test at moderate certainty is the size of the effect. The belief it limits, a moderate and clinically relevant benefit in older adults, is attested by P-249's own report of earlier syntheses and supported independently by P-680. The population scope (mostly cognitively healthy adults; an MCI subgroup of three trials) must stay explicit.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: KA-08 (assumption registry): 'Brain scans are categorically superior to cognitive and neuropsychological assessments for MCI' - i.e., imaging-based features dominate cognitive/behavioural measures for MCI-relevant classification/prognosis.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-925 (Montreal memory-clinic cohort, n=121 MCI): a purely clinical model - delayed word recall + Stroop inhibition + Coding (working memory) + complex iADL - achieves AUC 0.94 (95% CI lower bound 0.87) for dementia conversion the year before diagnosis, with the authors explicitly noting this model's advantage is that it relies on a very simple, cheap, readily available clinical assessment 'over more complex investigations that include imaging and biomarkers'. No imaging or fluid biomarker entered the model. SCOPE: the invalidation is for the conversion-prediction task (progressive vs stable MCI), not for MCI-vs-HC discrimination; KA-08's categorical-superiority claim is refuted as a general principle - cognitive + functional assessment alone matches the accuracy imaging is presumed to add.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Scoped: for MCI-to-dementia conversion prediction, cognitive + functional assessment can achieve excellent accuracy (AUC 0.94) without imaging; imaging and biomarker advantages should be evaluated head-to-head against clinical models rather than assumed categorically (aligns with VF-29 ascertainment-determinant thesis).
invalidated_assumptions.status_note: Scoped IA added at G5 2026-08-26 (delegated evaluator): KA-08 categorical imaging superiority does not extend to conversion prediction. Source-verified against pdf_extract_925.txt (AUC 0.94, no-biomarker model, authors' explicit cheap-clinical-assessment advantage framing).
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-925 summary: 'AUC 0.94 (95% CI lower bound 0.87) for dementia conversion the year before diagnosis'; 'the strength of this model is that it relies on a very simple clinical assessment which is relatively cheap and readily available... a notable advantage over more complex investigations that include imaging and biomarkers'.
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: KA-08 previously targeted by IA-70 (P-788, REJECTED for false XAI method). invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Clinical-practice convention: retention (delayed recall) should be preferred over learning (sum of free recall) for identifying incident MCI and dementia - 'the conventional practice has been to rely on retention rather than learning' (Grober et al., citing Welsh 1991, Jack 2019).
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-935 (BLSA, n=1422 cognitively normal, 187 incident MCI over median 8.1 years; Cox proportional hazards on pFCSRT+IR): learning (FR) and retention (DFR) EACH independently predicted incident MCI with similar effect sizes - about 20% decrease in the hazard of MCI per SD increase in FR or DFR, and each remained predictive in the presence of the other. The paper's explicit conclusion: 'The practice of preferring retention over learning to predict incident MCI should be reconsidered. The decision to include retention should be guided by time constraints and patient burden.' SCOPE: refutation is for incident-MCI prediction from a single baseline assessment; retention may still add value for other tasks (e.g. detecting established impairment).
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Scoped: retention testing adds no incremental predictive value over learning for incident-MCI risk stratification and can be omitted when time/burden matter; preference for retention over learning is convention, not evidence. Consistent with the corpus psychometric line (P-924/P-926) on efficient, validated assessment.
invalidated_assumptions.status_note: Scoped IA added at G5 2026-08-26 (delegated evaluator): retention-preference convention refuted for incident-MCI prediction by P-935 (FR and DFR equally predictive, ~20% hazard per SD). Source-verified against pdf_extract_935.txt.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Clinical/psychiatric convention: cognitive impairment in euthymic bipolar disorder (BD) is milder, domain-limited, and qualitatively distinct from the amnestic neurodegenerative pattern of MCI, so euthymic BD patients would not routinely meet MCI-level impairment on standard neuropsychological assessment.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-944 (systematic review, 5 studies, Trends in Psychiatry and Psychotherapy): euthymic BD patients showed cognitive impairments EQUAL to or MORE SEVERE than MCI patients across the reviewed domains - the review explicitly reports that in the included comparisons BD impairment matched or exceeded MCI-level deficit, contradicting the assumption that euthymic BD is cognitively spared relative to MCI and that standard neuropsychology cleanly separates the two.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Cognitive test scores cannot be assumed to separate euthymic BD from MCI: a BD patient meeting MCI-level impairment on a single assessment is not evidence for or against a neurodegenerative process, and MCI risk-stratification tools must either exclude/stratify primary psychiatric diagnoses or incorporate psychiatric history rather than relying on raw test scores.
invalidated_assumptions.status_note: Scoped IA added at G5 2026-08-26 (delegated evaluator): euthymic-BD-cognitive-sparing assumption refuted by P-944 (5-study systematic review; BD impairments equal/more severe than MCI). Source-verified against pdf_extract_944.txt.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Clinical assumption: hearing loss in older adults is a fixed, non-modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline - nothing can be done about it.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-961 (NACC referral cohort, N=4358): self-reported hearing impairment was associated with increased MCI risk (standardized HR 2.58, 1.73-3.84) and accelerated cognitive decline, BUT hearing-aid users were less likely to develop MCI than hearing-impaired non-users (HR 0.47, 0.29-0.74) and showed NO significant MCI-risk difference vs normal-hearing adults (HR 0.86, 0.56-1.34, p=.51). Hearing aids restored MCI risk to normal-hearing level - the risk factor is modifiable by a cheap, widely available intervention. SCOPE: observational cohort, self-reported hearing/aid use; no RCT of hearing aids for MCI prevention.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Hearing screening and hearing-aid provision should be treated as candidate MCI-risk-reduction interventions in older adults; the null-vs-normal-hearing comparison after aids suggests near-complete risk restoration.
invalidated_assumptions.status_note: Scoped IA added at G5 2026-08-26 (delegated evaluator): hearing-loss-is-fixed refuted by P-961 aid mitigation (HR 0.47 vs non-users; 0.86 ns vs normal-hearing). Source-verified against pdf_extract_961.txt.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-961: 'Hearing aid users were less likely to develop MCI than hearing-impaired non-users (HR 0.47, 0.29-0.74, P=.001). No MCI risk difference was observed between normal-hearing participants and hearing-impaired adults using hearing aids (HR 0.86, 0.56-1.34, P=.51).'
invalidated_assumptions.prior_audit_2026_08_29: DEMOTE:strawman - hearing loss is the canonical MODIFIABLE risk factor (Lancet Commission); hearing-aid mitigation confirms the field view rather than disproving one. Demote to 'proposed'; record P-961 as consensus support for hearing-aid mitigation.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Clinical assumption: apathy in MCI is a benign behavioural symptom - it burdens caregivers but carries no prognostic information about cognitive decline.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-965 (PRISMA systematic review + random-effects meta-analysis, 11 longitudinal studies, 9504 individuals): apathy in MCI significantly predicts conversion to dementia (pooled unadjusted HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.29-1.84), with subgroup analysis confirming association with progression to AD. Apathy is therefore a prognostically load-bearing symptom, not a benign epiphenomenon. SCOPE: pooled HR across heterogeneous studies; apathy measurement instruments vary; unadjusted pooled estimate.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Apathy presence in MCI should raise conversion-risk assessment priority and prompt closer follow-up, and automated apathy detection (P-612) becomes a clinically justified monitoring channel.
invalidated_assumptions.status_note: Scoped IA added at G5 2026-08-26 (delegated evaluator): apathy-is-benign refuted by P-965 meta-analytic HR 1.54 for MCI-to-dementia conversion. Source-verified against pdf_extract_965.txt.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-965: 'Apathy was significantly associated with dementia conversion: pooled unadjusted HR 1.54 (95% CI 1.29-1.84) across 11 studies/9504 individuals.'
invalidated_assumptions.prior_audit_2026_08_29: DEMOTE:strawman - apathy as a conversion predictor is established (the paper is a confirmatory meta-analysis of 11 longitudinal studies), so 'benign, no prognostic information' is not a held prior. invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Imaging assumption: static white-matter-hyperintensity (WMH) burden is the operative imaging risk factor for MCI/dementia - what matters is how much WMH is present, not how fast it accumulates.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-967 (SPRINT MIND post hoc, N=433): WMH PROGRESSION over 48 months - not static burden - independently predicts incident probable dementia/MCI (per-Z OR 1.51, 1.12-2.04; >=1.4 mL threshold OR 2.89, 1.23-6.81; 12.8% vs 4.7% event rates above/below threshold). The analysis was explicitly framed as testing progression against static burden. SCOPE: single post hoc analysis, small event count (33), SPRINT MIND BP-trial subset.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Serial WMH measurement (change over ~2-4 years) should complement single-timepoint burden in dementia-risk stratification; WMH-progression thresholds are candidate trial endpoints.
invalidated_assumptions.status_note: Scoped IA added at G5 2026-08-26 (delegated evaluator): static-burden-primacy refuted by P-967 WMH-progression OR 2.89. Source-verified against pdf_extract_967.txt.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-967: 'Dementia/MCI occurred in 12.8% (20/156) of patients with >=1.4 mL WMH progression vs 4.7% (13/277) with <1.4 mL (p=0.002)... WMH-progression Z-score was associated with dementia/MCI (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.12-2.04, p=0.007).'
invalidated_assumptions.prior_audit_2026_08_29: DEMOTE:incremental finding - the block shows progression predicts events but never shows static burden fails; the stated prior is not contradicted. Demote to 'proposed'; log as complementary to WMH-burden findings.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Clinical/biomarker convention: serial (longitudinal) amyloid PET is required to monitor MCI progression - a single baseline scan is insufficient because change over time should add predictive value.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-974 (Chosun Univ, N=75 MCI, [18F]Florbetaben PET, mean 24-mo follow-up): baseline amyloid burden significantly predicted MCI-to-AD conversion (HR 10.0, 95% CI 1.15-85.39, p=0.04) whereas longitudinal amyloid-burden change did NOT (HR 0.2, 95% CI 0.02-1.18, p=0.07); ROC for conversion was 65.2% (longitudinal) vs 59.6% (baseline), difference not significant. Conclusion explicit: a single baseline amyloid PET could be sufficient. SCOPE: single centre, 75 MCI (17 converters), wide CIs on the baseline HR.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Do not require serial amyloid PET when a baseline scan is available; reserve repeat imaging for trials with pre-specified change endpoints. Contrast with WMH where progression IS the signal (IA-81 / P-967).
invalidated_assumptions.status_note: Scoped IA added at G5 2026-08-26 (delegated evaluator): serial-amyloid-necessity refuted by P-974 baseline HR 10.0 vs change HR 0.2. Source-verified against pdf_extract_974.txt.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-974 summary: baseline amyloid HR 10.0 significant; longitudinal change HR 0.2 ns; ROC no better; conclusion single baseline scan suffices.
invalidated_assumptions.prior_audit_2026_08_29: DEMOTE:strawman-ish convention (baseline amyloid PET is already the prognostic standard) and single-centre N=75 with 17 converters and a baseline HR CI of 1.15-85.39. invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Clinical convention: apparent MCI reversion to normal cognition indicates genuine recovery or a benign course - the individual no longer carries MCI-level pathology.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-971 (ADNI, N=329 MCI): practice effects (PEs) inflate apparent reversion - adjusting for PEs cut reversion by 28.8% (57 vs 80 reverters) and raised MCI prevalence 9.2%; among 'false reverters' (CN by PE-unadjusted scores but MCI after PE adjustment), 72.2% were positive for amyloid or tau. Reversion is therefore substantially a measurement artifact, and many apparent reverters retain biomarker evidence of AD pathology. SCOPE: ADNI cohort; PE estimation relies on test-naive matching.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Treat reversion as a hypothesis to verify with biomarkers or alternate tests, not as proof of recovery; PE-adjusted classification should be standard in MCI monitoring and trials.
invalidated_assumptions.status_note: Scoped IA added at G5 2026-08-26 (delegated evaluator): reversion-as-recovery refuted by P-971 (28.8% of reversion is PE artifact; 72.2% of false reverters biomarker-positive). invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-971 summary: PE adjustment reduced reversion 28.8% (57 vs 80), 72.2% false-reverters biomarker-positive.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Diagnostic-criteria assumption: MCI reversion rates are artefacts of the loose one-test-per-domain Petersen operationalisation; stricter two-test neuropsychological criteria would materially reduce reversion and stabilise the diagnosis.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-986 (GAS/SNAC Sweden, head-to-head): reversion 43.4% under Petersen (n=744) vs 48.3% under the stricter NP criteria (n=375) - tightening the impairment rule did NOT reduce reversion (incidence slightly higher: 76.2 vs 63.0/1000 person-years); only removing the complaint requirement pushed reversion to 54.7%. SCOPE: population cohort 60-102y, no biomarker adjudication.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Criterion tightening is not a substitute for prognostic stratification; reversion should be framed by domain-count and subtype membership (CF-232), not by choice of impairment rule.
invalidated_assumptions.status_note: Confirmed by delegated evaluator (G4/G5 2026-08-26).
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: Reversion rates 43.4% vs 48.3%; incidence 63.0 vs 76.2/1000py; no-complaint variant 54.7%.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: MCI is adequately detected in routine clinical practice using standard cognitive screening tools, with detection rates stable across ethnicity, gender and clinical settings.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-1036 (Mian et al. 2024, Ageing Research Reviews 98:102335) systematically reviews >100 articles and documents (i) ethnicity disparities in MCI prevalence with underdetection in some populations, (ii) gender differences in cognitive trajectories that affect detection sensitivity, and (iii) MMSE underdetects early MCI compared to MoCA, meaning standard screening tools miss a substantial fraction of MCI cases, especially in early stages and in under-served populations. The synthesis argues that "overlooked cases of MCI" represent a major missed opportunity for early AD intervention.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Replace MMSE-only screening with MoCA-based screening in routine primary-care practice for MCI detection, especially in early-stage cases and in populations at higher risk of MMSE-based underdetection; integrate ethnicity- and gender-specific MCI detection pathways into clinical guidelines to reduce overlooked cases.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_chain: Narrative systematic review of >100 articles (P-1036) covering ethnicity, gender, lifestyle, comorbidity and diagnostic-tool evidence for MCI detection; review explicitly argues that overlooked MCI cases are a major missed opportunity for early AD intervention.
