invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: MCI detection in routine US clinical care is broadly adequate (i.e., the majority of expected MCI cases are diagnosed).
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-1046 100% US Medicare FFS + Advantage 2015-2019 observed/expected analysis showed only 6.2-7.9% of expected MCI cases were diagnosed (i.e., 92% undiagnosed) and that detection in Black (0.039) and Hispanic (0.048) beneficiaries was less than half the rate in non-Hispanic White beneficiaries (0.098).
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: DMT access in early symptomatic AD will be substantially constrained by detection infrastructure; equity-targeted detection improvements are required to realise the population benefit of lecanemab/donanemab.
invalidated_assumptions.rehabilitation_pathway: Equity-targeted detection programmes in primary care; integration of brief cognitive screening and plasma p-tau into routine Medicare annual wellness visits; audit-and-feedback for low-detection provider groups.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-1046 abstract: 'detection rates for MCI cases increased from 2015 to 2019 (0.062 to 0.079), the results mean that 7.4 of 8 million (92%) expected MCI cases remained undiagnosed. The detection rate for MCI was 0.039 and 0.048 in Black and Hispanic beneficiaries, respectively, compared with 0.098 in non-Hispanic White beneficiaries.'
invalidated_assumptions.review_note: PENDING HUMAN G5. Strong evidence base; single study. Consider promotion to confirmed after cross-validation in non-Medicare or non-US population.
invalidated_assumptions.g5_caveat: Single US Medicare study; ICD-coded MCI may underestimate true prevalence especially in non-White groups with documented access barriers; HRS prediction model uses 2000-2016 data; cross-sectional design cannot establish mechanisms.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Amyloid is the primary upstream driver of MCI impairment and progression; tau, metabolic and cognitive signals are clinically meaningful only downstream of amyloid positivity (KA-17, assumption_registry.json).
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: P-1296 (600 subjects, seven international cohorts - Knight ADRC, AIBL, HUB, HCB, CITA, HSCSP, HGH): blood mtDNA methylation (D-loop, ND1) in a Random Forest model predicts MCI-to-ADD progression with AUC-ROC 0.903 (independent test set, V3; test accuracy 83.2%, sensitivity 95.1%), explicitly independently of beta-amyloid status, with D-loop methylation differences present in comparisons detectable even before beta-amyloid positivity - the source itself frames the model as working 'even in initially beta-amyloid-negative patients'. P-1386 (real-world memory clinic, n=90) independently corroborates at the non-amyloid-marker level: whole-brain cortical diffusion AngleR (a diffusion-MRI microstructure marker, not an amyloid or tau measure) distinguishes stable vs converting amyloid/tau-negative (A-T-) MCI with AUC 0.8 and improves negative predictive value by +21.25 percentage points, while 40% of A-T- MCI progressed (to a mix of AD and non-AD dementias) - so clinically meaningful prognostic signal exists in amyloid-negative MCI that is carried by a non-amyloid, non-tau marker. SCOPE: this is a prognostic-signal claim (non-amyloid markers carry progression-relevant signal in amyloid-negative MCI), not a claim that amyloid is irrelevant; P-1350's subthreshold-amyloid SUVR finding (AUC 0.762 within visually A- aMCI) shows part of the A- progression signal is still amyloid-linked, which bounds the claim.
invalidated_assumptions.clinical_implication: Blood-based non-amyloid prognostic markers (mtDNA methylation; diffusion-MRI cortical microstructure) can stratify progression risk in amyloid-negative MCI, where amyloid-centred prognostic panels lose purchase; prognostic work-up for A- MCI should not default to amyloid-status-only counselling.
invalidated_assumptions.rehabilitation_pathway: In A- MCI cohorts, pair a blood mtDNA-methylation or cortical-diffusion prognostic marker with standard clinical assessment for progression stratification; validate both markers jointly in a prospective cohort with conversion endpoints.
invalidated_assumptions.evidence_from_summary: P-1296 summary: 'The model distinguishes cognitive decline from stability in MCI independently of beta-amyloid status'; 'Differentially methylated sites identified in the D-loop region ... detectable even before beta-amyloid positivity'; 'Random Forest ... AUC-ROC 90.3% ... for predicting MCI-to-ADD progression independent of beta-amyloid status'. P-1386 summary: '40% of MCI A-T- progressed to a mix of AD and non-AD dementias (poor NPV)'; 'Adding whole-brain AngleR as an N marker gave good differentiation between stable and converting MCI A-T- patients (AUC 0.8) and substantially improved negative predictive value (+21.25%)'.

invalidated_assumptions.demoted_at_audit_2026_09_14: STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF. Every load-bearing figure verifies (block L161265 Results; L161283 Key findings; pdf_extract_1110.txt L31-35 abstract HRs/CIs, L225-227 '66 participants progressed to DLB while 2412 did not', L364 'adjusted for age, education, race, and MCI type') and the operator's 2026-09-10 PDF check was genuinely performed - the numbers are NOT in question. What fails is the other half of an invalidated assumption: a field-held prior that the paper disproves. The P-1110 paper's own literature review states the OPPOSITE of KA-50 as the pre-existing position (pdf_extract_1110.txt L418-426: 'parkinsonism and falls are more prevalent among individuals with MCI-LB (compared to other MCI subtypes) and increase the hazard of progression to DLB in a considerable manner. The odds of having impaired gait, tremor, bradykinesia, and rigidity are two to five times higher among those with MCI-LB versus those with MCI-AD'); parkinsonism is a core clinical feature of the DLB consensus criteria the paper cites (extract L619 'fourth consensus report of the DLB consortium'); the authors describe their result as 'confirmed' (extract L297-299 'No motor domain predicted the hazard of progressing to VaD ... Hence, the specificity of the aforementioned associations for DLB was confirmed'), never as contrary to expectation; their stated novelty is sign-level granularity (extract L78-80 'only rarely researchers have focused on the differential prognostic properties of different motor signs (not composite scores) on incident DLB') and sex interactions. Block L161256 frames the motivation the same way ('had not been explored in prodromal/MCI stages'), not as a contrary belief. Grep of the extract for surpris|unexpected|contrary|nonspecific: zero hits. KA-50 was registered the same day from this very record with no independent citation ('corpus prior confirmed by IA-NEW-1110-01'), i.e. the prior is circular. Demoted to pending_human_review for operator re-disposition.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: The source's own framing, quoted verbatim above: P-748 'defines itself against the generic-variable tradition it summarises' and describes those variables as the ones that 'dominate the automated-speech-analysis literature', naming its members (speech rate, MLU, error counts, pronoun-noun ratio, idea density, type-token ratio, fluency measures), its studies (Forbes-McKay and Venneri 2005; Ahmed et al. 2013a, 2013b; Taler and colleagues; Mueller et al. 2016; Emery 2000; de Lira et al. 2011) and the ML classifiers built on it (Fraser, Meltzer and Rudzicz 2016; Orimaye 2017). The corpus corroborates only the weaker parent position, VF-12, that speech and language channels detect MCI - it records no independent statement that the generic surface measures specifically are the markers. The assumption registry has no entry for connected-speech markers, so a new KA is proposed rather than an existing one reused.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: On 105 age- and education-matched picture-description transcripts (35 HC / 35 MCI / 35 AD), four generic surface measures computed without manual syntactic analysis - utterance count (omnibus p .788), MLU (.063), type-token ratio (.252) and formal grammatical error rate (Fisher pairwise p 1) - fail to separate the diagnostic groups univariately, while hand-annotated referential-grammar variables on the SAME transcripts return Bonferroni-corrected moderate-to-large effects (adjunct clause ratio, MCI d .93); the type-token null replicates in an independent Spanish five-group cohort (P-747). This is a univariate measurement-level dissociation within one study and one replication; it does not by itself show that the generic feature SET carries no signal in multivariate combination, since P-748 builds no classifier and the dominant pipelines are multivariate.

evidence_quotes.quote: The paper defines itself against the generic-variable tradition it summarises: speech rate, syntactic complexity indices such as mean length of utterance and error counts, pronoun-noun ratio, idea density, type-token ratio and fluency measures, used bottom-up across studies
evidence_quotes.supports: The prior is field-held and named by the source itself, with a citation trail, not constructed by the miner.

evidence_quotes.quote: every generic variable that dominates the automated-speech-analysis literature - utterance count, utterance length, type-token ratio, formal error rate - returned null

evidence_quotes.quote: All four generic linguistic measures were null: number of utterances (12.886/12.886/12.971; omnibus p .788), MLU (11.14/9.500/9.928; ANOVA omnibus .063), type-token ratio (0.656/0.648/0.618; omnibus .252) and formal grammatical errors (printed 0.1289/0.0095/0.0179; all Fisher pairwise p at 1).
evidence_quotes.supports: The contradiction is directly estimated and fully quantified - four omnibus tests with printed group means, no fitted or derived quantity.

evidence_quotes.quote: its adjunct-clause result (MCI d .93) is the number most likely to be cited forward
evidence_quotes.supports: The within-sample positive control: the same 105 transcripts, same variance structure, yield a large MCI-stage effect, so the four nulls are not a blanket power failure.

evidence_quotes.quote: Fine-grained grammar of referential specificity separates MCI/AD speech where generic measures fail
evidence_quotes.supports: The authors themselves claim the reversal - it is the paper's stated Key Novelty, not a limitation, an open problem or a miner's elevation.

fp_codes_cleared: STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF: the prior is not constructed here. P-748 names the tradition, lists its measures (speech rate, MLU, error counts, pronoun-noun ratio, idea density, type-token ratio, fluency), cites its studies and names the ML classifiers built on it, and calls those variables the ones that 'dominate' the literature. See residual_risk for the remaining half of this concern.

MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: every number is a directly estimated group mean or an omnibus/pairwise test on observed data. No model-fitted counterfactual, no covariate-conditioned prediction, no meta-regression slope anywhere in the paper.
SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION: the opposite - the dissociation is the paper's stated significance and its Key Novelty line. The authors do not file it under open problems or limitations.
DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: no rank, ratio, SUCRA or composite is involved; the reversal rests on primary group contrasts.

SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: MCI and AD are analysed as separate groups with separate pairwise contrasts, not pooled. The MCI-versus-HC contrast is available on its own for all four generic measures and for the adjunct clause ratio (d .93 in MCI).

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: Bonferroni correction is applied and corrected p values are printed. Correction can only make a null MORE likely, so the nulls do not depend on it; the positive control (adjunct clause ratio) is a CORRECTED effect, i.e. it survives the paper's own pre-specified correction.
AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM: the claim is in the abstract-level significance statement and the registry Key Novelty field, not in supplementary material or speculation.

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: P-748 does not position itself as concordant with a known exception. It positions itself AGAINST the tradition and reads the generic nulls as the reason a different measurement level is needed. It is not extending a previously reported alternative pattern to a new population.
UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE: four exact omnibus p values, three sets of group means and a Cohen's d are printed on the face of the record; nothing defers to unreproduced supplementary tables.
invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk: The field uses these generic measures as INPUTS to multivariate classifiers, not as univariate discriminators - Fraser/Rudzicz-style pipelines feed dozens of surface features into a learned model and never claim any one of them separates groups on its own. P-748 builds no classifier and computes no discrimination statistic at all, so four univariate omnibus nulls do not test, and cannot overturn, the actual operative claim that the surface feature SET carries signal in combination. An operator could reasonably re-scope this from an invalidated assumption to a narrower record ('generic surface measures do not discriminate univariately'), which is a much weaker statement than the one the source's own framing invites. Two secondary weaknesses feed the same objection: MLU at omnibus .063 is a marginal rather than a clean null, and P-748's Primary Limitation is that 'The pooled three-source sample confounds provenance with diagnosis, and no analysis addresses it' - three sources with different recording, transcription and diagnostic conventions add within-group noise that suppresses exactly these aggregate counts, so some of the null is plausibly measurement heterogeneity rather than absence of signal.

invalidated_assumptions.original_claim_before_narrowing: The generic surface measures that the automated speech-analysis literature is built on - utterance count, mean length of utterance, type-token ratio (lexical diversity) and formal grammatical error rate - do not separate MCI or mild-to-moderate AD from healthy controls in connected speech. On 105 age- and education-matched picture-description transcripts (35 HC / 35 MCI / 35 AD) all four returned null omnibus tests (utterance count p .788, MLU .063, type-token ratio .252, formal grammatical errors Fisher pairwise p at 1), while on the SAME transcripts theory-selected referential-grammar variables returned Bonferroni-corrected moderate-to-large effects, the adjunct clause ratio reaching Cohen's d .93 already at the MCI stage. The MCI/AD speech signal therefore sits at the level of referential grammar, not at the level of aggregate surface counts; the within-sample positive control is what makes this a measurement-level dissociation rather than an underpowered null. The type-token null replicates independently in a Spanish clinical sample (P-747, five diagnostic groups).

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: The source paper's own framing, in two separate fields of its block, is the anchor. (1) Rationale field: 'the study tests whether salivary GFAP, the astrocytic cytoskeletal protein overexpressed in reactive astrogliosis, could diagnose MCI and AD' - GFAP is sought BECAUSE the standing biology says astrogliosis raises it. (2) Related-work field: 'Saliva reflects changes in CSF per earlier work (Bermejo-Pareja 2010, Sabbagh 2018); increased GFAP in plasma and brain in AD contrasts with the salivary decrease' - the transfer assumption is asserted by citation to two named prior studies, and the plasma/brain increase is stated as the established finding. (3) The source then labels its own result 'opposite to plasma GFAP literature'. No part of this prior was constructed by the miner, and no KA-NN in assumption_registry.json covers cross-biofluid direction transfer, hence NEW_KA_PROPOSED rather than an anchor to an existing id.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: The standing view that GFAP rises in MCI/AD because it is the astrocytic protein overexpressed in reactive astrogliosis - and that an accessible peripheral biofluid therefore reads that rise in the SAME direction as CSF/plasma - does not hold for saliva. In the first systematic salivary GFAP evaluation (P-1234; 20 amnestic single-domain MCI, 20 AD, 20 cognitively healthy controls, AHEPA/GAADRD Thessaloniki), directly measured salivary GFAP FALLS monotonically with impairment - controls 13.35, MCI 6.82, AD 3.56 ng/mg protein - a roughly 49 percent reduction already at the MCI stage, and the source itself states the direction is opposite to the plasma GFAP literature. The reversal is analyte-specific rather than a whole-sample normalisation artefact: in the same samples, under the same total-protein normalisation, salivary p-tau, Abeta42, COX-2 and caspase-8 ROSE while GFAP and the pro-inflammatory cytokines FELL. CANDIDATE ONLY, pending_human_review, gate_verified=false. What this record asserts is bounded: biofluid compartment can reverse the SIGN of a GFAP-based MCI marker, so 'GFAP is elevated in MCI' cannot be carried across biofluids as a direction-preserving belief. It does NOT assert that the plasma GFAP literature is wrong, and it deliberately excludes P-1234's flagged discrimination claim (Youden J=1.0, sensitivity 100 percent, specificity 100 percent from 20 per group with in-sample cut-offs), which carries the authors_overclaim flag and forms no part of this record.

evidence_quotes.supports: THE SOURCE'S OWN 'CONTRARY TO EXPECTATION' FRAMING. The authors, not the miner, identify their result as running against the standing literature.

evidence_quotes.supports: INTERNAL CONTROL against the strongest alternative explanation. If the decrease were a total-protein normalisation or salivary-flow artefact, every normalised analyte would fall together; four analytes rose in the same samples under the same normalisation, so the direction is analyte-specific.

evidence_quotes.supports: CLEARS EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: there is no pre-existing salivary GFAP series in which a decrease is an established, catalogued exception. This is the first such measurement, so the reversal is new information rather than an extension of a known alternative pattern.

evidence_quotes.supports: DISCLOSURE, carried in the record itself: the evidential weight of the reversal is one single-centre cross-sectional cohort of 20 per group.

The prior is stated twice by the source in its own words - GFAP as the protein 'overexpressed in reactive astrogliosis', and 'Saliva reflects changes in CSF per earlier work (Bermejo-Pareja 2010, Sabbagh 2018)' - and the source then names its own result as 'opposite to plasma GFAP literature'. The source does not frame the direction as unclear or in equipoise, and no corpus paper records the opposite position (zero corpus hits for GFAP or saliva).

MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: does not apply. The contradiction is three directly measured ELISA concentrations in ng/mg protein, corroborated by a second platform (Dot Blot, agreement r=0.801) and a semi-quantitative Western Blot. No regression, no fitted counterfactual, no value read off a model at chosen covariate levels.

DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: does not apply. No rank, ratio or composite is used. The record explicitly EXCLUDES the paper's flagged quantity - the Youden J=0.95/1.0, sensitivity 95-100 percent, specificity 100 percent discrimination claim fitted in the same 20-per-group sample, which is what carries the authors_overclaim flag - and rests only on group concentrations, which are not a function of those cut-offs.

SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: does not apply. MCI is reported as its own group (20 amnestic single-domain MCI) with its own concentration (6.82 ng/mg), separate from the AD group (3.56) and the controls (13.35). The claim is made at the MCI stage, not read off an MCI-plus-dementia pool.

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: does not apply. The block states this is 'the first systematic evaluation of salivary GFAP' and that 'salivary biomarker data in AD/MCI are scarce', so a salivary GFAP decrease is not an already-established, separately cited exception that the source is extending to a new population.

SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION: does not apply TO WHAT THIS RECORD CLAIMS. The measured direction is asserted firmly in the block's Results and in 'Key findings reported' ('Salivary GFAP decreased in MCI and AD'), and the discordance with plasma is stated as fact, not as a possibility. What the authors DO file as unresolved is the MECHANISM ('mechanism of salivary GFAP decrease (salivary-gland production vs blood diffusion)'), and this record makes no mechanistic claim. DISCLOSED WEAKNESS: they place the discordance sentence under 'What are the problems?', so an operator could read the framing as a self-limitation rather than as a correction to the field.

AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM: does not apply in the sense the code polices. The decrease is the paper's central measurement, present in Results, in 'Key findings reported' and named in 'Primary Limitation'; it is not a buried supplementary contrast the miner elevated to a headline. DISCLOSED: the direction is NOT in the block's one-line 'Key Novelty' field, which names the assay comparison instead.

UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE: does not apply. The reversal-bearing sentence carries three numeric concentrations with units, a stated significance verdict, a monotonic ordering across three groups, and a second-platform agreement statistic (r=0.801). DISCLOSED: no p-value or confidence interval for the group contrast reaches the corpus record.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: cannot fire, and this is disclosed as a weakness rather than claimed as a strength. The source pre-specifies no multiple-comparison correction anywhere in the record, so there is no correction the result fails; equally, there is none it survives. The record is therefore not selecting a nominally significant survivor out of a corrected family - it is reporting the paper's primary analyte.
invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk: The contradicted arm was never measured in these subjects. P-1234 quantifies salivary GFAP but takes the plasma/brain increase from the literature, and the corpus contains no plasma GFAP measurement at all - so the reversal is a between-study, between-assay comparison, and the single most economical explanation is not compartment biology but that the salivary indirect-ELISA/Dot-Blot measurand normalised to total protein is simply not the same analyte as plasma Simoa GFAP. Nothing in the record excludes that: n is 20 per group at a single centre, no p-value or multiple-comparison correction reaches the corpus, and the paper's own 'What can be improved' asks for precisely the missing test ('comparison with plasma GFAP in the same subjects'). An operator may therefore reasonably rule that until one cohort measures both compartments, the honest record is the absence (T04_blood_omics_p4-gap-01) rather than a belief reversal, and reject this as premature.

That record asserts an absence; this one asserts a belief reversal. They are different record types off one observation and an operator may reasonably want only one - if so, gap-01 is the safer keep, because it does not need the plasma arm to have been measured.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Field-held prior: 'total creatine is metabolically stable across MCI/AD and can therefore serve as the internal concentration reference for brain MRS, so Cr-referenced ratios (NAA/Cr, mI/Cr, Cho/Cr) are valid MCI markers.' Evidence it is held rather than constructed: (a) P-1195's own framing - it 'cautions against using Cr as an internal reference since Cr itself declines', which only makes sense against a standing practice, and it carries 'resolving Cr-referencing methodology' as an open problem for the field; (b) P-1195 pools NAA/Cr and mI/Cr as literature-level outcomes across 79 studies, which is only possible because the primary MRS literature reports Cr-referenced ratios as its readout; (c) corpus paper P-850, a randomised MCI trial, lists 'MRS NAA/Cr Ratio' among its baseline/outcome measures. No part of this prior is stated in my own words first and then attributed to the field.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: Creatine is not a stable internal reference in the MCI brain. In the largest pooled MRS synthesis in the corpus (79 1H-MRS studies; 40 MCI studies, 1238 MCI patients vs 1473 healthy controls), total creatine itself fell 6.4% in MCI and 6.9% in AD relative to controls - so the denominator of the Cr-referenced ratios that the MRS literature reports as its primary MCI readout is itself a disease-varying quantity, and the authors of P-1195 explicitly caution against continuing the practice.

invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk:
[T05_mri_pet_imaging_p3-conf-01] The Cr decline may not be a creatine-specific effect at all. P-1195 reports every absolute metabolite falling together in MCI - NAA -9.6%, Cho -4.3%, Cr -6.4% - which is the signature of a shared bias on absolute quantification (partial-volume / grey-matter tissue-fraction loss, coil loading, or water-referencing error) rather than of a real change in creatine concentration. If that is what is happening, Cr referencing is the CORRECTION for the shared bias and the ratios are the better-behaved measure, so the paper's caution would invert the correct methodological conclusion and this IA would be recording the opposite of the truth. The digest supplies nothing that discriminates the two readings: no confidence interval, no I-squared and no Hedges' g is quoted for the Cr estimate specifically, and the paper itself concedes that 'Cramer-Rao lower bounds not reported in most studies (data quality unverifiable)' and that platform, sequence and quantification differences were left uncorrected. A human gate should demand the per-metabolite dispersion statistics and a tissue-fraction-corrected subgroup before promoting this.

[T13_evidence_synthesis_p3-conf-01] The strongest objection is EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD in a form the corpus cannot adjudicate: instability of creatine under neurodegeneration is a long-standing methodological caveat among MRS methodologists, and the very existence of absolute-quantification MRS exists partly because of it. If an operator judges that the field already holds 'Cr may not be stable' as an accepted caveat rather than holding 'Cr is stable' as a belief, this record collapses from a belief reversal to a quantification of a known caveat - real and useful, but not an IA. Nothing in the corpus settles this: P-1195's digest cites no prior warning about Cr referencing, and the only corpus corroboration of the practice (P-850) is a single baseline-table row in a paper that carries authors_overclaim on a different claim. Two secondary weaknesses feed the same objection. First, no confidence interval, p value or heterogeneity statistic is printed for the Cr estimate anywhere in the digest - the digest reserves the word 'significantly' for GSH - so the 6.4 per cent MCI decline is a point estimate with no precision attached, which is close to UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE territory. Second, the ratio pools and the absolute-concentration pools are not the same study sets (a study contributes to whichever it reported), so the mI +6.3 versus mI/Cr +16.2 divergence is not a clean arithmetic decomposition of a moving denominator and must not be presented as one - part of that gap is between-study composition, and the record should not be read as having isolated the denominator's contribution.

invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: SCOPED TO INSTRUMENT DISCRIMINABILITY. The standing view P-749 itself cites - that the Token Test is a useful tool for differentiating MCI patients from cognitively healthy elderly - does not survive its own test: in 119 clinically diagnosed elderly Brazilians (34 controls / 22 aMCI / 45 naMCI / 18 AD) the Token Test separated NO diagnostic group, means spanning only 33.2 to 32.5 with a linear mixed-model group coefficient of -0.288 (t -0.975, 95% CI -0.867 to 0.292), and the same null held for constrained sentence production on the Northwestern Anagram Test (means 8.3 to 8.8). The reversal is not attributable to an insensitive cohort: the SAME participants in the SAME session separated strongly on MoCA (F 36.28, p below 0.0001; means 27.0 / 23.4 / 24.2 / 19.4) and on every 3W3S memory sub-item (immediate words F 13.65, p below 0.0001). The record claims ONLY that the Token Test failed to discriminate - including against AD - and does NOT claim that syntactic processing is preserved in MCI, which P-749's own appraisal flags as outrunning its evidence.

invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk: A ceiling effect on the administered short forms is not excludable and would convert this from a belief reversal into a measurement artefact. Token Test means span 33.2 to 32.5 with standard deviations of only 0.3 to 0.7 - an order of magnitude tighter than the demographic and clinical-scale rows in the same table - and P-749 never prints a maximum score for either the Token Test or the Northwestern Anagram Test, so the corpus cannot tell whether all four groups sat at the top of the scale. The fact that even the AD group (MoCA 19.4) failed to differ is the specific pattern a ceiling would produce. If the operator judges the ceiling more likely than the reversal, the correct disposition is to reject this as an IA and retain it as a documented instrument-sensitivity limitation. A secondary, smaller risk: the null is single-centre, in Brazilian Portuguese, whose word-order flexibility required loosening the NAT's scoring, so part of the production null may be language-specific and would not transfer to the English-language literature the prior comes from.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Two independent strands, neither supplied by the miner. (1) The corpus record for this paper states the belief as the standing view of the field and frames the paper as a test of it: 'a direct, if small, test of a claim the field increasingly makes by assumption: that plasma phosphorylated tau is the practical prognostic tool for MCI.' (2) The source's own framing: the authors do not treat their null as unremarkable but as something requiring explanation, and the explanation they offer is a frailty phenotype in which biomarker relations differ from those 'in Alzheimer's disease or in non-frail cognitively impaired individuals' - an explanation that presupposes an expected relation in the non-frail case. The assumption registry has no plasma-biomarker entry (KA-17 concerns amyloid primacy in pathology, not blood-based prognosis; KA-16 concerns whether non-cognitive data carry any screening signal at all), so a new KA is proposed rather than an existing one reused. Proposed wording: 'Plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau181) is the practical prognostic marker for MCI-to-dementia conversion and can substitute for, or outperform, bedside cognitive and functional assessment.'
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: The field's working assumption that plasma phosphorylated tau is the practical prognostic tool for MCI does not hold in the oldest old. In a consecutively screened hospital geriatrics MCI cohort (59 patients, median age 82.7, 27 of 59 progressing to dementia within 24 months), baseline plasma p-tau181 on a Quanterix SIMOA platform failed every prognostic test the paper ran: no baseline group difference (sMCI 23.47 +/- 2.24 pg/mL versus pMCI 25.49 +/- 2.32 pg/mL, F = 1.03, P = 0.53), no prediction of progression by binomial regression (p = 0.4), no correlation with MMSE (p = 0.38), and AUC 0.57 +/- 0.09 with a 95 per cent CI of 0.39 to 0.74 that spans chance - while three cheap bedside clinical instruments (Lawton's Index, MMSE, Clock Drawing Test) carried the paper's predictive signal. The authors state the negative themselves in their conclusion. The record is deliberately scoped to a transfer failure, not to an absolute one: it does not establish that plasma p-tau181 lacks prognostic value in the oldest old (the authors call that an open question and the corpus holds no positive oldest-old estimate to set against it); it establishes that the assumption has never been tested in the age band where MCI is most often assessed and that the one direct test in this corpus is null.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: the paper pre-specifies no multiple-comparison correction, and none is needed here - the reversal rests on nulls, and correction can only make a null more secure. UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE: four printed statistics with an interval and group means. Nothing defers to unreproduced supplementary tables. (The paper's separate, unquantified 23.2 pg/mL 'shows promise' claim is excluded from this record precisely because it carries no statistic.)

STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF: PARTIALLY cleared and flagged. The prior is not the miner's construction - the corpus record states it as a claim the field 'increasingly makes by assumption', and the source's own frailty-phenotype explanation is only intelligible as an explanation of divergence from an expected relation. What is missing, and the operator should note it, is an explicit contrary-to-expectation sentence printed by the authors themselves; the truncated extract does not reproduce the introduction's literature claims verbatim.

SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION: cleared for the SCOPED claim only. The authors assert their own null but explicitly leave open 'Whether plasma p-tau181 has any prognostic value in the oldest old at all'. The claim above is therefore written as a transfer failure plus an untested-assumption finding, not as a demonstration that the marker is prognostically inert. An operator who reads the record as the stronger statement should reject it under this code.

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: NOT fully cleared - the strongest FP risk after the power objection. The authors explain their null by appeal to a frailty phenotype in which biomarker relations differ, using the definite article ('it is plausible they fall within this phenotype'), which suggests a phenotype already described somewhere in the literature; if p-tau attenuation in frailty is an established, cited exception, this is extension rather than reversal. Two facts push back: the authors hedge the phenotype attribution rather than asserting concordance with it, and they list the oldest-old prognostic question as OPEN, which an established exception would have settled.
invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk: The null is underpowered and its own interval does not exclude the prior. Every p-tau statistic rests on at most 47 patients while every clinical statistic rests on 59, and the AUC interval runs 0.39 to 0.74 - an upper bound that would be a clinically useful discriminator. A 95 per cent interval that contains both chance and a usable AUC is a failure to detect, not a demonstration of absence, so an operator could reasonably rule that the paper establishes a GAP (no adequately powered oldest-old estimate exists) rather than an invalidated assumption. The same paper then weakens its own negative by offering a 23.2 pg/mL cut-off that 'shows promise' with no test statistic attached, so the source is not univocally negative about the marker even inside its own discussion.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: The prior is embodied in practice and stated by the source, not constructed by the miner. (a) Source framing: 'Prevention trials need an endpoint, and for AD prevention the natural endpoint is the clinical transition itself.' A phase 3 registration trial adopted MCI due to AD as a primary endpoint event, which presupposes the transition is determinable by trained investigators. (b) Source-stated safeguard: 'The endpoint definitions were asymmetric by design: MCI due to AD required meeting core clinical criteria at two consecutive visits and follow-up visits, whereas AD dementia required NIA/AA criteria at a single visit.' The asymmetry exists precisely because the field believed the two-consecutive-visit requirement made the MCI determination dependable - and that is the subset on which agreement fell to 40.5 percent. (c) Source-stated stake: 'Reliable, accurate assessment of clinical events is critical for prevention trials and may mean the difference between success and failure.' (d) Corpus behaviour, offered as context and not as quoted evidence: the corpus's confirmed record IA-14 catalogues near-ceiling MCI classification accuracies (P-200 AUC 0.9992, P-197 98.86%, P-119 98.84%, P-1 98.81%) reported against clinically assigned MCI labels - performance that treats those labels as exact. [Rescoped 2026-09-14: context only, not part of this record's narrowed claim - whether clinical MCI labels are reliable ground truth is a construct-level question this record does not decide, and no annotation of IA-14 follows from it.] REGISTERED PRIOR KA-51 (narrowed 2026-09-14 to the operator's G5 scope): 'Investigator-only endpoint ascertainment does not miss clinically adjudicated MCI-due-to-AD events, so endpoint adjudication in an AD prevention trial can be confined to cases the site investigator has flagged as having reached MCI due to AD.' The originally proposed wording ('... reliable enough to serve as a trial endpoint event and as a ground-truth diagnostic label') carried the construct-level reading the operator excluded and is withdrawn.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: Endpoint adjudication in an AD prevention trial cannot be confined to cases the site investigator has flagged as having reached MCI due to AD: investigator-only endpoint ascertainment misses clinically adjudicated MCI-due-to-AD events. In the TOMMORROW trial, adjudication limited to investigator-flagged cases would have lost 41 of the trial's 96 events - a consequence the authors state themselves. In the phase 3 TOMMORROW prevention trial a blinded three-stage expert committee, working from the same case dossiers as the examining site investigators, agreed with investigator determinations only 71.0 percent of the time (Cohen's kappa 0.327 for MCI due to AD). Disagreement was bidirectional and was WORST where the field's own safeguard is strongest: on cases the investigator had personally diagnosed as MCI at two consecutive visits, agreement fell to 40.5 percent. In the other direction, 41 of the 410 cases whose investigator diagnosis did not support an endpoint were declared events by the committee, and those 41 are 42.7 percent of every endpoint event in the trial. Caveat carried onto this figure (block Problems section, L132022): investigators never gave endpoint opinions, so 'did not support an endpoint' is an inference the authors construct from the investigators' provisional diagnoses, and the 410-case denominator sits inside that inferred category - 41/410 therefore inherits the same construction as the kappa. The 40.5 percent figure, by contrast, is on cases the investigator actually diagnosed as MCI due to AD at two consecutive visits and is exempt. The practice conclusion stands because the authors assert it ('These are events that would have been missed if the adjudications had been limited only to cases when the investigator felt an endpoint had been reached'), not because the 41/410 figure is construction-free. The specific practice assumption this overturns is the standard trial-design one - that endpoint adjudication can be confined to investigator-flagged cases - which on these numbers would have lost almost half of the trial's events. This record does NOT claim that the MCI-due-to-AD construct is unreliable or that clinical MCI labels cannot serve as ground truth: the authors leave construct reliability raised without settling (block L132044) and offer a committee learning-curve alternative for the headline kappa. Scope: MCI due to AD, NC->MCI transition, cognitively unimpaired high-risk older adults; the AD-dementia contrast is reported separately (kappa 0.539 combined) and is not part of this claim.

fp_codes_cleared: MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: kappa, 71.0%, 40.5% and 41/410 are computed directly from the full cross-tabulation of 648 adjudicated dossiers. No model is fitted anywhere in the paper (card: Architecture/Method Family A8, 'no computational learning architecture'), so there is no fitted counterfactual standing in for a measured contrast.

DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: no rank, ratio, SUCRA or composite is used. The paper does carry one flagged artefact - the unpublished neural-network imputation that '83% of participants who progressed to MCI due to AD were plaque-positive' - but that claim concerns amyloid status and no clause of this record depends on it.

SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: the claim is scoped to the MCI-due-to-AD determination in cognitively unimpaired high-risk older adults. The paper reports a separate combined statistic that pools MCI due to AD with AD dementia (kappa 0.539); this record deliberately uses the MCI-specific 0.327 and states the combined figure only to show which one it is not using.

UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE: every clause of the claim carries a printed statistic - kappa 0.327, 71.0% overall agreement, 40.5% on twice-diagnosed cases, 41 of 410 cases, 42.7% of 96 events - all from the paper's own Key findings and Results, none deferred to unreproduced supplementary material.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: the paper pre-specifies no multiple-comparison family; these are descriptive agreement statistics on the trial's complete adjudication record, not one survivor selected from a tested family, so there is no correction being evaded.

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: the digest records that 'no external benchmark for adjudication agreement in AD prevention trials is cited, which is consistent with their claim that this endpoint had not been used this way before'. The paper cites six prior AD adjudication precedents for the PROCEDURE but none reporting agreement for this endpoint, so these numbers are not a re-report of an already-catalogued exception.
invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk: The strongest argument against: the authors decline the general version of this conclusion. P-866's card records assumption_challenged = 'none', and its open_problem records that 'whether the MCI due to AD construct can be operationalised reliably enough for registration trials at all is raised without being settled'. They also supply a benign alternative explanation - agreement rose from about 50% to 80-90% after roughly 100 cases - which frames the low overall kappa partly as committee learning rather than construct unreliability. A gate could reasonably read this as AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM and route the material to a gap instead of an IA; the claim above is scoped to the narrow statements the authors do assert, but the boundary is a judgement call and belongs to the operator, not to me. Second, independent objection, which the paper itself raises: investigators were never asked for an endpoint opinion, so the kappa compares committee decisions against endpoint support INFERRED from six-category provisional diagnoses - 'The kappa statistics inherit that construction' - meaning some unknown share of the measured disagreement is an artefact of that inference rather than genuine clinician disagreement. Third: the trial stopped early for futility with 96 of an anticipated 202 events, and panel-level event rates varied 9.2% to 23.6% without a formal test, so the agreement estimates rest on fewer events than planned and on panels whose spread was never shown to be within chance.
invalidated_assumptions.dedup_note: Checked against every IA in the brief's registry (IA-01 to IA-94, IA-NEW-1046-01, IA-NEW-1110-01) and against the 25 KA priors: none anchors on the reliability of the MCI diagnostic LABEL itself. Nearest neighbours and why they are different: IA-94 (P-1036) and IA-NEW-1046-01 (P-1046) concern under-DETECTION of MCI in routine care - cases never diagnosed - not disagreement between two expert determinations on the same case with the same information. IA-14 (P-200) and IA-17 (P-329) concern whether reported model performance is real or generalises; they assume the labels and question the model, whereas this record questions the label. IA-02 (P-584) concerns whether a static cognitive score is the diagnostic gold standard, not the reproducibility of a clinician's diagnosis. VF-29 (supporters P-654, P-657, P-648, P-650, P-924, P-926, P-937, P-955, P-962, P-971, P-982) says ascertainment moves group-level ESTIMATES such as prevalence by a factor of two; this record is about within-case inter-rater disagreement on one participant's dossier, a different construct, and P-866 is not among its supporters. In existing_gaps.md, G-21 records label noise as an artefact of forcing trial data into discrete cross-sectional labels (an ML-input problem), and ACTOR-G-034 records missing test-retest reliability of ML INPUT FEATURES - neither addresses the reliability of the diagnostic determination. Direct grep of existing_records_core.md, existing_gaps.md, T07_neuropsych_instruments_existing_gaps.md and conflict_pool.md for 'P-866' returns nothing, so this paper has never been used in any relational record.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Not constructed by the miner. Three corpus papers state the adverse direction as the standing position of the literature in their own rationale or discussion sections: P-827 (DO-HEALTH secondary analysis) writes that its findings 'align with previous cross-sectional ... and prospective studies ... regarding the adverse impact of polypharmacy on cognitive function'; P-1012 opens its rationale with 'Polypharmacy has been linked to cognitive decline' and its background with 'Prior work linked polypharmacy and specific drug classes to cognitive decline'; P-970 records that 'Prior work recognised MCI risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, depression, polypharmacy, benzodiazepines) globally'. The source itself frames its own result as running against that literature ('Prior studies reported increased cognitive decline with polypharmacy or no difference; this longitudinal MCI cohort finds a protective/modest association'). Proposed new registry entry, wording for the operator to accept or reject: KA-NEW [Geriatric prescribing] Predictor_Surprise :: Polypharmacy (>=5 concurrent medications) is an adverse exposure for cognition in older adults, so a higher medication count marks higher risk of cognitive decline and of progression from MCI to dementia.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: The field-held prior that polypharmacy is an adverse exposure for cognition - a standing risk factor whose presence should raise expected cognitive decline - does not hold for the MCI-to-dementia transition, where the directly estimated association reverses sign: in 237 Taiwanese MCI patients followed a median 34 months, baseline polypharmacy (>=5 concurrent prescriptions) carried an adjusted hazard of progression to dementia of 0.49 (95% CI 0.31-0.78), with higher dementia-free survival in the polypharmacy group (Kaplan-Meier p=0.005). No prior report cited by the source, and no corpus paper stating the prior, reported a protective direction. The record asserts the sign reversal for this transition only; it does not assert that medication causes the protection, and it deliberately excludes the paper's secondary drug-class attribution.

evidence_quotes.supports: Scope: every participant carried an MCI diagnosis at baseline, so this is an MCI-specific estimate and not a pooled MCI-plus-dementia analysis.

evidence_quotes.quote: The prevalence of MCI was greater among participants with polypharmacy compared with those with no polypharmacy (MCI <26: 53.5% vs 35.3%, P< .0001; MCI <24: 34.9% vs 17.2%, P<.0001; Figure 1 AeB).
evidence_quotes.supports: The raw direction that the field reads as confirming harm, and against which P-1157's protective hazard is a reversal.

evidence_quotes.quote: The exposure is measured once, at baseline, is not randomised, and is a direct proxy for the multimorbidity and depression that the fully adjusted models remove - so once those confounders are controlled, every one of the paper's twelve fully adjusted odds ratios is null, and the design cannot separate an effect of medication burden from an effect of the illness that produces it.
evidence_quotes.supports: Independent non-reproduction of the harm association after adjustment, in a second cohort on a second continent.

evidence_quotes.quote: 89 (37.6%) progressed to dementia over follow-up. Kaplan-Meier showed higher dementia-free survival in the polypharmacy group (p=0.005).
evidence_quotes.supports: The direction reversal is present in the unmodelled survival curves as well as in the adjusted model, and the event count that supports it is stated.

evidence_quotes.quote: Observational single-country (Taiwan, veterans system) cohort; confounding by indication; no dose-response per drug; relies on annual CDR which may lag true dementia onset.
evidence_quotes.supports: The source's own limitation list, which this record's narrow scoping respects - it is why the record refuses to assert that polypharmacy protects.

fp_codes_cleared: STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF: the prior is stated in the corpus by two papers other than the source - P-827 in its own Discussion ('the adverse impact of polypharmacy on cognitive function', anchored to a named 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis) and P-1012 in its own rationale ('Polypharmacy has been linked to cognitive decline'). It is not reconstructed by me. NOTE HONESTLY: unlike IA-65, where the source stated equipoise AND a second corpus paper recorded the opposite field position, here both other corpus papers record the SAME harm-direction prior; the equipoise language is inside the source's own introduction only, and is addressed under residual_risk.

MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: cleared. HR 0.49 is a directly estimated adjusted Cox coefficient on the whole 237-patient cohort, not a fitted counterfactual at chosen covariate levels, and the unadjusted Kaplan-Meier contrast (p=0.005) runs the same way.

SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION: cleared. The conclusion is the paper's own significance statement ('Indicates polypharmacy is associated with lower MCI-to-dementia progression risk'), not something the paper files under open problems. The paper's open problems are external validation, dose-response and drug-class clarification - refinements of the claim, not withdrawals of it.

AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM: cleared. The protective association is the paper's headline, its Key Novelty line and its significance statement, and the authors state the contrast with prior harm reports themselves.

SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: cleared. All 237 participants had MCI at baseline; the endpoint is progression to dementia within that MCI cohort. No dementia-at-baseline or cognitively-normal participants are pooled in.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: cleared. The HR is the paper's single pre-specified primary contrast, not a survivor selected out of a corrected family; the count-threshold analyses are reported as a set with no threshold surviving, which is the conservative reading.

DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: cleared. The record rests on a primary hazard ratio, not on a SUCRA, a ratio of ratios or an importance ranking. The paper's ranked drug-class interpretation IS its flagged overclaim, and this record deliberately excludes it - the claim is scoped to the direction of the polypharmacy association and does not assert that type matters more than count.

The corpus's other polypharmacy paper (P-827) reports a null after adjustment, not a benefit, and positions itself as concordant with harm; no corpus paper and no source citation reports polypharmacy as protective for cognition, so this is not an extension of an already-excepted pattern.
invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk:
[T07_neuropsych_instruments_p5-conf-01-merged] [T07_neuropsych_instruments_p5-conf-01] Confounding by indication running in the protective direction, compounded by ascertainment. Polypharmacy in a veterans-home and outpatient-geriatric system indexes sustained medical contact and treated - rather than untreated - cardiometabolic disease, and dementia was staged by ANNUAL CDR, so the group under closest medical supervision is also the group whose transitions are adjudicated on a different schedule; the paper concedes that 'the exact onset of dementia may have preceded the recorded diagnosis date' (annual CDR staging) and that 'the delay between biological onset and confirmed diagnosis could not be determined'; it does NOT use the phrase 'confounding by indication' - that structure is this record's own inference from the surveillance channel, not a paper concession (corrected 2026-09-10, see pdf_provenance_check.misattribution_corrected). A competing and entirely benign reading of HR 0.49 is therefore that low prescription count marks frailty, disengagement from care or end-of-life de-prescribing, not that medication protects cognition. If the operator accepts that reading, the correct record is not an IA but a documented confounding artefact, and the honest version of the reversal is narrower: polypharmacy is not usable as a risk MARKER for MCI-to-dementia progression, which is weaker than the claim that the field's prior is overturned.

[T09_epidemiology_risk_p2-conf-01] Confounding by indication running in the protective direction, which the source concedes and cannot remove. In a veterans-home and outpatient-geriatrics system, a patient on five or more chronic prescriptions is by construction a patient with treated, monitored, largely cardio-metabolic disease and regular clinical contact; the patient on none or one is disproportionately the untreated, disengaged, or frail-and-deprescribed patient. The card's appraisal sharpens this into a surveillance channel: outcome staging is by ANNUAL CDR, so the group in more frequent medical contact is also the group whose transitions are ascertained differently, and no covariate in the adjustment set (age, sex, CCI, education, smoking, sensory impairment, Barthel, GDS-15, MNA-SF, recruitment source) indexes care intensity or treatment access. On that reading HR 0.49 measures access to care, not medication burden, and the field prior about medication burden is untouched. A second, independent objection: P-1157's own introduction describes the prior evidence as inconsistent - 'several prior studies reported harm, others found no difference' - which an operator may read as EQUIPOISE and reject under STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF exactly as IA-65 was rejected, notwithstanding that P-827 and P-1012 both record the harm direction as the position they are working against. The record is therefore proposed at medium confidence, with the reversal claim deliberately bounded to 'the count-as-harm prior fails' rather than 'polypharmacy protects'.

[T11_comorbidity_p1-conf-01] Confounding by indication runs in exactly the direction of the finding and the paper does not address it. In a Taiwanese veterans-home and outpatient system, >=5 concurrent prescriptions marks a person whose hypertension and hyperlipidemia are diagnosed and treated and who is in regular medical contact; <5 marks a person who is either untreated, unengaged with care, or already being deprescribed because of frailty or approaching end of life. The corpus's own second polypharmacy paper shows how load-bearing this is: P-827 records that 'The exposure is measured once, at baseline, is not randomised, and is a direct proxy for the multimorbidity and depression that the fully adjusted models remove - so once those confounders are controlled, every one of the paper's twelve fully adjusted odds ratios is null, and the design cannot separate an effect of medication burden from an effect of the illness that produces it.' In P-827 that structure moved a strongly harmful raw association to null; the same structure operating one step further in a 237-patient cohort with 89 events, single centre, no external validation, and annual CDR staging that lags true onset, is a sufficient explanation for a protective HR 0.49 without any belief being overturned. The card's appraisal names the same mechanism from the surveillance side and states it 'runs in exactly the direction of the protective finding'. If the operator judges that a confounding artefact the authors concede cannot invalidate a belief, this record should be rejected rather than downgraded.

[T11_comorbidity_p1-conf-01] P-1157's own Introduction frames the prior evidence as inconsistent - 'several prior studies reported harm, others found no difference' - which is the exact equipoise wording that got IA-65 rejected as STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF. The prior therefore rests entirely on one sentence in P-827's Discussion, and P-827's authors themselves read their twelve null odds ratios as ALIGNING with the harm literature rather than contradicting it, so no source in this record actually says the field belief has failed. If the operator judges that a field whose own papers call the evidence inconsistent has no standing view to overturn, this record dies on the same code as IA-65 and should be re-filed as a documented non-reproduction rather than an invalidated assumption.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Three independent witnesses, all quoted verbatim above. (1) The source's own framing: P-859 states 'A standing objection to the whole cognitive-training literature is that its effects are driven by expectancy, engagement, motivation and novelty rather than by training', and separately that 'Cognitive training is widely marketed on the strength of trials whose control conditions are weaker than their active arms, and expectancy is the standing objection.' (2) P-759, an MCI acupuncture meta-analysis, applies the belief as an operative judgement, downgrading every outcome because 'the primary outcomes are examiner-administered scales, so the entire efficacy signal is currently confounded with assessor and participant expectancy'. (3) P-700, a VR training study in MCI, applies it in the same way: 'expectancy and attention effects are not separable from any specific effect of the virtual environment'. PROPOSED REGISTRY TEXT for the new prior, phrased as the field states it, not as I would phrase it: 'Non-specific expectancy, engagement, motivation and novelty - rather than the trained content - drive the apparent cognitive benefit reported by unblinded non-pharmacological intervention trials in MCI.' Category: Mechanism_Reframing.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: Therapeutic expectancy is not the mechanism that generates cognitive-training benefit in MCI. In the two-site COG-IT randomised trial (n=107, ADNI-criteria early/late MCI), patients rated the computerised arm significantly higher than the crossword arm before randomisation (86.0 per cent vs 78.5 per cent High Expectancy; chi-square [2, n=107]=6.7, p=0.010), yet the crossword arm produced the superior global-cognition outcome, and measured expectancy predicted no change in ADAS-Cog or any secondary measure at week 12 or week 78 (least-squares mean difference -0.78, 95% CI -2.47 to 0.92, p=0.368). This contradicts the standing objection - named by the source itself and treated as the operative confound by other corpus intervention studies - that cognitive-training effects in this population are driven by expectancy, engagement, motivation and novelty rather than by training. SCOPE, and it is load-bearing: the reversal is carried by the DIRECTIONAL dissociation (arm-level expectancy measured within-subject before a randomised allocation, with the less-expected arm winning), NOT by the null association, which the source's own appraisal calls weak evidence of absence.

evidence_quotes.quote: A standing objection to the whole cognitive-training literature is that its effects are driven by expectancy, engagement, motivation and novelty rather than by training
evidence_quotes.supports: The prior belief is field-held and is named as such by the paper itself, not constructed by the miner. This is the clause that clears STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF.

evidence_quotes.quote: The longitudinal result is null throughout. Expectancy was not associated with change in ADAS-Cog or any secondary measure at week 12 or week 78; the primary contrast was a least-squares mean treatment difference of -0.78 (95% CI -2.47 to 0.92, p=0.368) at 78 weeks.
evidence_quotes.supports: The contradiction is a DIRECTLY ESTIMATED null with a confidence interval, not a fitted value, a derived rank, or an unquantified clause.

evidence_quotes.quote: Nor did expectancy interact with treatment: within the CCT arm the 78-week ADAS-Cog difference was -2.40 (95% CI -5.97 to 1.18, p=0.188), and within the CPT arm -0.79 (95% CI -2.98 to 1.40, p=0.476).
evidence_quotes.supports: The moderation route by which expectancy could still act is separately tested and also null.

evidence_quotes.quote: 86.0% of patients were High CCT Expectancy against 14.0% Low; 78.5% were High CPT Expectancy against 21.5% Low; and on the combined index 72.0% were High Total Expectancy against 28.0% Low. The preference for CCT over CPT was significant (chi-square [2, n=107]=6.7, p=0.010).
evidence_quotes.supports: The dissociation that makes this more than a null: expectancy was measurably HIGHER for the arm that subsequently performed WORSE, so the placebo account predicts the opposite of the observed ranking.

evidence_quotes.quote: CPT demonstrated superior efficacy to CCT for improving global cognition. Everyday functioning worsened and hippocampus volume decreased more with CCT than with CPT.
evidence_quotes.supports: The parent trial's outcome, quoted by this paper, supplies the direction the expectancy account cannot explain.

evidence_quotes.quote: The preference for CCT over CPT was significant (chi-square [2, n=107]=6.7, p=0.010).
evidence_quotes.supports: Quantified first limb of the dissociation: patients expected significantly more from the computerised arm than from the crossword arm.

evidence_quotes.quote: CPT demonstrated superior efficacy to CCT for improving global cognition.
evidence_quotes.supports: Second limb: the arm that was expected to help less is the arm that won on the randomised comparison.

evidence_quotes.quote: Expectancy was not associated with change in ADAS-Cog or any secondary measure at week 12 or week 78; the primary contrast was a least-squares mean treatment difference of -0.78 (95% CI -2.47 to 0.92, p=0.368) at 78 weeks.
evidence_quotes.supports: Directly estimated, interval-reported null association between measured expectancy and outcome (supporting, not load-bearing, limb).

evidence_quotes.quote: That CPT demonstrated greater effects than CCT despite patients having lower expectation for improvement using CPT provides evidence against the notion that expectancy effects were responsible for the benefits of CPT.
evidence_quotes.supports: The source authors actually claim the reversal (criterion 3); it is not a miner inference.

evidence_quotes.quote: expectancies are not a universal phenomenon in CCT, nor are they the sole driver of CCT's effects
evidence_quotes.supports: The authors' own generalisation of the reversal, and the exact scope limit the record must keep - not a claim that expectancy never operates.

evidence_quotes.quote: meeting Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative criteria for early or late MCI
evidence_quotes.supports: Scope match (criterion 4): the sample is MCI-specific, with no dementia or cognitively-intact population pooled in.

evidence_quotes.quote: the primary outcomes are examiner-administered scales, so the entire efficacy signal is currently confounded with assessor and participant expectancy
evidence_quotes.supports: A second corpus paper states the expectancy account as the operative standing objection to this intervention literature.

evidence_quotes.quote: expectancy and attention effects are not separable from any specific effect of the virtual environment
evidence_quotes.supports: A third corpus paper, in a different intervention family, states the same standing objection.

evidence_quotes.quote: That does not overturn the conclusion, which is buttressed by the independent argument that the less-expected treatment outperformed the more-expected one, but it does mean the null association on its own is weak evidence of absence.
evidence_quotes.supports: The source record's own adjudication, which is why this candidate is built on the dissociation limb and explicitly refuses to rest on the null.

fp_codes_cleared: STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF: cleared. The paper states the standing objection in its own Introduction; the prior is quoted, not authored by the miner.

MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: cleared. Every figure cited is a directly estimated contrast from a random-intercept linear mixed-effects model of observed outcomes, reported with a 95 percent CI. No SUCRA, no fitted value at chosen covariate levels.

SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION: cleared. The authors assert the conclusion in the title ('Expectancy Does Not Predict 18-month Treatment Outcomes with Cognitive Training in Mild Cognitive Impairment'); they do not file it under open problems.
SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: cleared. The sample is MCI only - ADNI criteria for early or late MCI, MMSE >= 23, no dementia or cognitively-intact arms pooled in.
AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM: cleared. It is the paper's headline claim, not a footnote.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: not applicable. The claim rests on a null, so selecting a nominally significant contrast from many is not the failure mode; if anything the multiplicity concern runs the other way.
DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: not applicable. No ranking statistic is involved.
UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE: cleared. Point estimates, 95 percent CIs and p-values are printed for the primary contrast and for both within-arm interactions.

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: cleared. The paper describes the expectancy literature in this field as 'sparse, with mixed findings, and has been restricted to cognitively intact adults' - so an MCI-population test is not an extension of an established exception.

STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF: the prior is quoted from the source as a 'standing objection to the whole cognitive-training literature' and is independently operative in two other corpus papers (P-759, P-700 quoted above; P-689, P-691 and P-787 use the same reasoning). It is not miner-constructed. DISCLOSED CAVEAT: P-859 also records that the empirical expectancy literature in this field 'is sparse, with mixed findings, and has been restricted to cognitively intact adults', so the belief is a widely-voiced objection rather than a settled empirical finding; an operator may reasonably judge that closer to equipoise than to a field-held positive claim.

MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: every number used is a directly estimated contrast on observed data - a chi-square on the observed expectancy distribution and a least-squares mean difference with a confidence interval. No fitted counterfactual at chosen covariate levels appears anywhere in the record.

SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION and AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM: the conclusion is the paper's title and is stated in its Discussion in the quoted sentence. It is not filed under open problems, limitations or speculation. The authors' own hedge ('nor are they the sole driver') is carried into the claim verbatim.
DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: no rank, SUCRA, ratio or composite quantity is involved.
SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: the sample is exclusively ADNI-criteria early or late MCI with MMSE at least 23; no dementia, no cognitively-intact adults, no pooling across stages.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: this record deliberately does NOT use the paper's one nominally significant secondary association (ADAS-Cog with Total Expectancy, OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-0.99, p=0.035), which the digest flags as fragile because secondary outcomes were not corrected for multiplicity. The two statistics used are the prespecified expectancy-distribution contrast and the trial's primary longitudinal contrast.

UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE: PARTIALLY CLEARED, and the residue is disclosed rather than hidden. The expectancy limb (chi-square 6.7, p=0.010) and the null limb (LS-mean -0.78, 95% CI -2.47 to 0.92, p=0.368) both carry statistics, but the outcome limb - CPT superior to CCT - is quoted from the parent trial with no effect size anywhere in P-859's record, so the MAGNITUDE of the dissociation is not quantified in this corpus.

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: PARTIALLY CLEARED and disclosed. P-859 records that 'every study that manipulated expectancy after enrolment through varying training instructions found no difference in cognitive gains. All of that work was in cognitively intact adults.' Those studies MANIPULATED expectancy post-enrolment in intact adults; none measured naturally occurring pre-randomisation expectancy, and none was in MCI - and the field nonetheless still raises the objection, as P-759 and P-700 show. An operator could still rule this replication-and-extension rather than reversal.

AUTHORS_OVERCLAIM HANDLING: P-859's card carries authors_overclaim and instructs 'Do not use this paper as the strong arm of any conflict'. That flag is specific to the title's flat-absence claim built on an underpowered null. This record is not a conflict, and it is written so that the flagged quantity (the null) is explicitly demoted to a supporting limb; the claim rests on the dissociation, which the card's own text names as the independent buttressing argument.

NON-INDEPENDENCE / DUPLICATE: grep across all corpus digests for 'COG-IT', 'NCT03205709' and 'crossword' returns P-859 only, so the parent trial's main-outcomes paper is not in the corpus and no shared-participant record exists. P-859's card lists no cross_paper_claims and no duplicate_of. P-759 and P-700 are cited only as prior-belief witnesses, not as evidence for the reversal, so their independence from COG-IT is not load-bearing (they are unrelated acupuncture and VR studies).
invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk:
[MANUAL-ia-01] The null is underpowered for the contrast it rests on. Expectancy was ceilinged - 86.0 percent High for CCT and 78.5 percent for CPT - so the Low-expectancy comparison group is roughly 15 and 23 patients respectively out of 107, and only six patients anticipated any worsening at all. A single pre-randomisation 5-point Likert item, dichotomised, is also a crude instrument, so an insensitive measure could produce this null without the underlying placebo account being false. The card additionally flags that the title asserts a flat absence ('Does Not Predict') that an underpowered design cannot establish. The defensible reading is therefore narrower than the title: expectancy as measured here does not explain the CPT-over-CCT advantage, and the direction of the expectancy gradient is opposite to what the placebo account requires. A reviewer could reasonably hold this at 'weakens' rather than 'overturns'.

[T08_intervention_trials_p2-conf-01] The expectancy contrast this design actually delivered is narrow and pinned near the ceiling, so it may never have tested the objection at all: 86.0 per cent versus 78.5 per cent High Expectancy after dichotomising two unvalidated single-item Likert questions, in a sample where 'Only six patients anticipated any worsening at all.' A defender of the expectancy account can say both arms were expected to help, that a 7.5-point gap between two near-ceiling proportions is not the high-versus-low expectancy contrast the objection concerns, and that the crossword arm's advantage is therefore compatible with expectancy driving benefit in both arms roughly equally. That objection is hard to rebut from the corpus alone, because P-859 prints no effect size at all for the CPT-over-CCT superiority, so the size of the dissociation cannot be weighed against the size of the expectancy gap.

No existing IA and no registry prior concerns expectancy, placebo or non-specific treatment effects. Nearest neighbours, all distinct: IA-33 (P-253) is about far transfer between trained and untrained cognitive domains, not about why any effect occurs; IA-50 (P-642, KA-23) is about immersive VR versus non-immersive delivery format; IA-65 (P-615) is about reminiscence-therapy delivery format. Grep of existing_records_core.md, existing_gaps.md and T08_intervention_trials_existing_gaps.md for 'expectanc' returns zero hits, and P-859 appears in no existing conflict, CF, VF or gap record. This is also not a restatement of the corpus's general 'unblinded trials are confounded' gap material: those records assert the confound is unresolved, whereas this record asserts it was measured in MCI and ran the wrong way.

invalidated_assumptions.scope_operator_review_2026_09_14: Operator scope decision 2026-09-14. If this record is ever confirmed it must be confirmed NARROWED: it files against the EXPECTANCY construct only, at 'weakens / bounds', not 'overturns'. KA-53 names four constructs - expectancy, engagement, motivation and novelty - and COG-IT measured exactly one of them, via two dichotomised single-item Likert questions with no validation, no test-retest and no internal-consistency estimate. That one construct was ceilinged: 86.0% High CCT Expectancy and 78.5% High CPT Expectancy, so the low-expectancy arms that carry the contrast are 15 and 23 of 107 (exact counts re-derived from the source PDF's Table 2, pdf_extract_859.txt L106-109: CCT 0+3+12=15 Low, CPT 2+4+17=23 Low; the block's 'roughly 15 patients' at summaries.md L130672 is confirmed). Engagement, motivation and novelty are untested by this design, so nothing here bounds them. The record's own residual_risk already concedes 'A reviewer could reasonably hold this at weakens rather than overturns' - this note makes that the operator's scope, not an option.
invalidated_assumptions.blocker_operator_review_2026_09_14: Operator blocker 2026-09-14: the load-bearing statistic is UNRECONCILED and the record cannot be confirmed until it is re-derived. The block prints 'chi-square [2, n=107]=6.7, p=0.010' (summaries.md L130658, repeated L130654); df=2 with chi-square 6.7 gives p=0.0351, while p=0.010 corresponds to df=1 (chi-square 6.635 is the df=1 0.01 critical value; the df=2 0.01 critical value is 9.210). This limb is the DIRECTIONAL dissociation, which the record itself names as what carries its scope, so it is not a cosmetic defect. CHECKED AGAINST THE SOURCE PDF, and the check does NOT clear it: pdf_extract_859.txt exists at the repo root (211 lines) and prints the same statistic verbatim at L90 - 'Patients were significantly more likely to report higher expectancy for CCT than CPT (chi2 [2, n=107]=6.7, p=0.010).' So the inconsistency is in the published source, not a summarisation or transcription error introduced by this pipeline, and it cannot be resolved by re-reading the local extract. Nor can 6.7 be re-derived from the printed marginals: on Table 2 (pdf_extract_859.txt L106-109) the full 2x5 table gives chi-square 3.68, the collapsed 2x3 Worsen/NoEffect/Improve table gives 2.23, and the unpaired 2x2 High/Low table gives 2.05 - none is 6.7. The plausible reading remains a '[2,' typo for df=1 on a binary High/Low design (p=0.010 is exact for df=1), but a paired McNemar test on discordant pairs is the only route that could yield 6.7, and the discordant counts are printed nowhere. Clearing this therefore needs the published table/erratum or author correspondence, not a local re-read.
