invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Two independent, non-constructed sources. (1) assumption_registry KA-22 [Prevention epidemiology]: 'Modifiable lifestyle factors - physical exercise alone, BMI, diet, sleep - are robust primary protective/risk factors that lower MCI/dementia incidence' - the registry text itself treats MCI and dementia incidence as one endpoint for modifiable-risk factors, which is precisely the assumption this record breaks. (2) The source's own framing, quoted above: P-1165 records that its result 'Aligns with Dutch 16-year, Finnish 30-year and European harmonised-cohort LIBRA findings; diverges by showing weaker MCI predictive validity', and that 'Prior LIBRA validations covered Dutch, English, Finnish and French cohorts and pooled European analyses'. A paper can only diverge on MCI predictive validity from a literature that reported MCI predictive validity, and the paper's own title applies the index to 'mild cognitive impairment and dementia' as a matched pair of endpoints.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: A modifiable-risk index validated for dementia does not transfer to the incident-MCI endpoint, so the routine fusion of 'MCI/dementia incidence' into one prevention outcome is not warranted. In the MYHAT population cohort, the LIBRA / LIBRA2 index was consistently associated with incident dementia across weight sets (HR 1.04-1.40 per point, all P<0.05 under joint modelling) but was not consistently associated with incident MCI - only the top quartile of one index variant reached significance. The null is not a power artefact: the MCI analysis carried 136 incident events against the dementia analysis's 79, i.e. 1.7x more events on the endpoint that failed. The authors themselves conclude the index 'functions as a dementia-risk rather than MCI-risk marker at the population level'.

evidence_quotes.quote: Higher baseline LIBRA was consistently associated with increased incident dementia risk across weight methods
evidence_quotes.supports: The dementia arm of the dissociation is positive and directly estimated in the same cohort under the same models.

evidence_quotes.quote: only the highest quartile of LIBRA2[MCI] predicted incident MCI
evidence_quotes.supports: The MCI arm is null apart from a single top-quartile contrast, across two index versions and three weight sets - the contradiction of the prior.

evidence_quotes.quote: 712 cognitively normal for incident MCI (136 events) and 1,118 dementia-free for incident dementia (79 events) over 8 years.
evidence_quotes.supports: The MCI null cannot be dismissed as underpowered relative to the positive dementia result: the failing endpoint had 136 events against the succeeding endpoint's 79.

evidence_quotes.quote: shows the index functions as a dementia-risk rather than MCI-risk marker at the population level
evidence_quotes.supports: Criterion 3 - the source authors themselves assert the endpoint dissociation, in the significance statement rather than under open problems.

evidence_quotes.quote: Aligns with Dutch 16-year, Finnish 30-year and European harmonised-cohort LIBRA findings; diverges by showing weaker MCI predictive validity, which the authors attribute to population-level heterogeneity of MCI aetiologies.
evidence_quotes.supports: Criterion 1 - the source's own framing of the result as a divergence from a literature it is otherwise concordant with, i.e. the prior is field-held and not miner-constructed.

evidence_quotes.quote: Prior LIBRA validations covered Dutch, English, Finnish and French cohorts and pooled European analyses
evidence_quotes.supports: The prior is a validated, repeatedly replicated index, not an untested proposal - which is what makes an endpoint failure a belief reversal rather than a negative pilot.

fp_codes_cleared: STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF: the prior is not constructed here. It is written into assumption_registry KA-22 as a single fused endpoint ('lower MCI/dementia incidence'), and the source itself records that it 'diverges by showing weaker MCI predictive validity' from the Dutch, Finnish and European harmonised-cohort LIBRA literature it otherwise aligns with. The source does NOT frame the MCI endpoint as equipoise - it frames its own result as a departure from an established, replicated validation record.

SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION / AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM: the dissociation appears in the paper's own significance statement ('functions as a dementia-risk rather than MCI-risk marker at the population level') and in its Key Novelty line, not under open problems or speculation. What the authors do file under open problems is the remedy (MCI-specific risk indices), which presupposes rather than retracts the failure.

SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: nothing is pooled. MCI and dementia are estimated in two separate, non-overlapping analysis samples (712 cognitively normal for the CDR 0 -> 0.5 MCI transition; 1,118 dementia-free for the CDR < 1 -> >= 1 dementia transition), so the MCI-specific reversal comes from an MCI-specific analysis.

MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: no fitted counterfactual or covariate-conditioned prediction is involved. Both arms are directly estimated Cox proportional-hazards models on observed incident events, with the same joint attrition model applied to both.
DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: no rank, SUCRA, ratio or composite derived quantity carries the claim - the claim rests on the primary hazard estimates and on the event counts.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: the record does not select a nominally significant survivor out of a corrected family. It rests on the ABSENCE of association across two index versions and three weight sets, with the single quartile contrast that did reach significance treated here as part of the null pattern rather than as the finding.

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: no corpus paper records the field as already holding that dementia-validated risk indices fail on the MCI endpoint. The nearest record, P-981, states only that 'Dementia risk scores (e.g., CAIDE) exist, but no risk-score system targeted MCI itself' - an absence of an MCI-specific instrument, not a documented failure of transfer, and P-981 offers no LIBRA or transfer test.
invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk: The reversal-bearing quantity is never itself quantified in the corpus record. The only statement of the MCI result is 'only the highest quartile of LIBRA2[MCI] predicted incident MCI' - no hazard ratio, no confidence interval, no p-value for the MCI arm anywhere in the block, while the dementia arm gets a full HR range. Under UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE a reviewer can hold that the record asserts a reversal off an unreported estimate, and the honest answer is that the MCI hazard ratios would have to be read out of the source PDF before this can be confirmed. Secondary objection, weaker but real: the authors attribute the divergence to 'population-level heterogeneity of MCI aetiologies' in a single cohort with baseline mean age about 79 from one low-socioeconomic US region, so the failure may be a property of that late-life population rather than of the index - which would make this a scope restriction on KA-22 rather than a reversal of it.
invalidated_assumptions.dedup_note: Checked against every IA anchored on modifiable-risk / prevention epidemiology: IA-29 (P-266) claims BMI, diet and sleep are not the primary MCI risk drivers; IA-67 (P-249) claims physical exercise alone is not robustly protective; IA-86 (P-982) claims routine cardiovascular risk variables alone do not identify MCI adequately; IA-31 (P-96) claims MCI screening does not require cognitive assessment. All four are about WHICH FACTORS carry MCI risk. This record makes no claim about which factors matter - it claims that a composite index whose factor set is already accepted, and which works on the dementia endpoint in the same participants under the same models, fails on the MCI endpoint. That is an endpoint-transfer claim, structurally the same shape as IA-44 (A+T+N- and A+T+N+ MCI cannot be merged for progression modelling), and no existing IA makes it. Also checked: the corpus has no existing gap statement mentioning LIBRA (grep of all 534 gaps and of the T09 theme gap file returns nothing); P-1165 appears in the corpus only as the existing complementary-findings pair P-1165xP-1159 (sleep and cognition in chronic heart failure), which is unrelated; and none of the genuine conflicts C-80, C-204, C-227, C-232, C-234 involves either endpoint transfer or a risk index.

invalidated_assumptions.review_note: 2026-09-10 G5 consolidated verdict (data/g5_consolidated_ia_verdicts.csv): REJECTED as invalidated assumption (2/2 not-confirmable). The reversal-bearing quantity is never quantified: no MCI hazard ratio, CI or p-value is provided (dementia HRs 1.04-1.40, 79 events; the MCI association appears only in the highest quartile of one LIBRA2[MCI] variant, 136 MCI events). A dementia-risk index not transferring to incident MCI may be endpoint-specific rather than an index reversal. Defensible re-file: 'LIBRA/LIBRA2 transfer to incident MCI is unvalidated - a dementia-risk index is not automatically an MCI-risk index' as a transfer limitation / evidence gap. KA-22 is NOT invalidated by this record. Status set to rejected_g5_belief_not_disproved.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: Two independent anchors, both inside the source rather than constructed by me. (1) The method statement: 'The PGSA aims to partially replace randomized placebo-controlled trials (RPCTs) by using historical control groups, reducing the number of participants exposed to lengthy placebo treatment - ethically problematic in AD prevention trials.' A method that substitutes historical controls for a randomised placebo arm is only valid if the historical MCI trajectory transports to the trial sample; that validity condition IS the prior. (2) The study rationale: 'Because PGSA algorithms were originally derived only from ADNI, the authors sought more generalizable algorithms by pooling diverse MCI databases, testing whether MCI samples are comparable enough for historical-control designs.' The authors set out to broaden the premise, not to refute it, which is why the refutation counts. Proposed registry entry, wording for the operator to accept or reject: KA-NEW [Trial design / MCI natural history] Predictor_Surprise :: MCI samples defined by conventional criteria are comparable enough across databases and recruitment settings that an untreated progression trajectory derived in one can serve as a historical or simulated control group for another, provided the samples match on baseline demographics and cognition.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: The historical-control (Placebo Group Simulation Approach, PGSA) premise for MCI prevention trials - that an untreated MCI control trajectory derived from one MCI database transports to another once the samples are matched on baseline characteristics - is contradicted by its own generalisation attempt. Across five harmonised MCI databases with individual patient data (ADNI 395, NACC 4328, InDDEx trial 831, CNG 726, BS-MC 1558; approx 7,838 participants), baseline demographic and cognitive data converged MORE than the differing inclusion criteria predicted, while the untreated trajectories diverged: MCI-to-dementia progression was about 10% at 4 years in the drug-trial sample against over 30% in the other four samples, and the trial sample showed no verbal-fluency decline over 3 years while every other sample declined. Baseline comparability therefore does not license transportability of MCI progression, and the authors conclude that conventional MCI criteria - and, in their judgement, newer 'MCI due to AD' criteria too - cannot produce internationally comparable MCI samples.

evidence_quotes.quote: The PGSA aims to partially replace randomized placebo-controlled trials (RPCTs) by using historical control groups, reducing the number of participants exposed to lengthy placebo treatment - ethically problematic in AD prevention trials.
evidence_quotes.supports: The prior is a real, published, in-field trial-design method whose entire rationale depends on an MCI control trajectory being reusable across studies.

evidence_quotes.quote: Because PGSA algorithms were originally derived only from ADNI, the authors sought more generalizable algorithms by pooling diverse MCI databases, testing whether MCI samples are comparable enough for historical-control designs.
evidence_quotes.supports: The source states cross-database comparability of MCI samples as the working premise it set out to establish - the prior is the source's, not the miner's.

evidence_quotes.quote: Baseline demographic and cognitive data varied less than expected despite differing inclusion criteria.
evidence_quotes.supports: The non-obvious half of the reversal: the matching condition that historical-control designs rely on was actually SATISFIED, so the failure cannot be blamed on unmatched baselines.

evidence_quotes.quote: relatively few drug-trial patients progressed from MCI to dementia (about 10% after 4 years), in contrast to the other four samples with progression rates over 30%
evidence_quotes.supports: The directly estimated, quantified contradiction: a threefold divergence in the very quantity (untreated MCI-to-dementia progression) that a simulated placebo group would have to reproduce.

evidence_quotes.quote: did not deteriorate on verbal fluency over 3 years, whereas patients in the other samples did
evidence_quotes.supports: A second, independent trajectory endpoint diverging in the same direction, so the reversal does not rest on the dementia-conversion endpoint alone.

evidence_quotes.quote: Conventional MCI criteria were insufficient to create well-defined, internationally comparable MCI samples; even newer MCI or "MCI due to AD" criteria are unlikely to remedy this.
evidence_quotes.supports: The authors themselves assert the reversal in their significance statement and extend it to the successor criteria - this is not a miner elevating an open problem.

fp_codes_cleared: STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF: the prior is not constructed by me. P-937 states the PGSA premise twice in its own words (the method 'aims to partially replace randomized placebo-controlled trials ... by using historical control groups'; the study exists to test 'whether MCI samples are comparable enough for historical-control designs'). PGSA is a published, in-field method, so this is a design assumption held outside the source, not a rhetorical foil.

MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: the 10% vs >30% figures are observed progression proportions from Kaplan-Meier curves on individual patient data with proportional-hazards models, not values fitted at chosen covariate levels. The verbal-fluency result is a meta-analysis of observed change-from-baseline scores.

SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION and AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM: the authors assert the conclusion in their significance statement and strengthen it prospectively ('even newer MCI or "MCI due to AD" criteria are unlikely to remedy this'). The reversal is the paper's headline, not a limitation or a speculation.
DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: no SUCRA, ranking, ratio or composite is involved. The reversal quantity is the primary endpoint of the comparison.

SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: all five datasets are MCI samples and the endpoint is MCI-to-dementia progression. Nothing is pooled with an AD or dementia baseline population, so the MCI-specific scope holds.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: the cross-sample progression comparison is the paper's pre-stated primary analysis, not a nominally significant survivor selected from a corrected family. No multiplicity correction is at issue.

UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE: quantified on three separate quantities - progression about 10% vs over 30% at 4 years, a 3-year verbal-fluency change contrast, and an education hazard ratio of 0.71 in CNG against approximately 1 elsewhere.

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: PARTIALLY cleared only - see residual_risk. Cleared to the extent that the specific proposition defeated here (baseline-matched MCI databases yield transportable trajectories) is the operating premise of an active method, not an acknowledged exception.
invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk: EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD is the strongest objection, and P-937 hands it to the objector: under its own problems section the paper writes that the 'drug-trial sample behaves differently (likely healthy-volunteer/selection effects)'. Trial participants being healthier and slower-progressing than cohort participants is long-established clinical epidemiology, so a gate can reasonably rule that no field belief was overturned and that P-937 merely quantifies a known selection effect in MCI. Two facts compound this. First, the whole reversal rests on ONE outlying dataset: four of the five samples agree (>30%), and only InDDEx dissents, so the record is a single-cohort result dressed as a five-cohort comparison. Second, that one dissenting dataset is contaminated by design - the digest records 'InDDEx (rivastigmine trial, all patients treated as untreated since no drug effect)', so any real rivastigmine effect on conversion is being read as a sampling difference. If the operator accepts either the already-known-exception reading or the single-outlier reading, this should be recorded as a supporter of VF-29 (where P-937 already sits) rather than as an invalidated assumption.
invalidated_assumptions.dedup_note: Checked against every IA in existing_records_core.md (IA-01 to IA-94, IA-NEW-1046-01, IA-NEW-1110-01) and against the 25 assumption_registry priors KA-01 to KA-26. No IA and no KA anchors on cohort transportability of MCI progression or on historical/external-control validity. Nearest neighbours and why they differ: IA-17 (src=P-329) is about published ML models' DISCRIMINATION not generalising off ADNI - a claim about classifier performance, whereas this record is about the untreated natural-history rate itself; IA-14 (src=P-200) is about near-ceiling accuracies; IA-85 (src=P-986), IA-77 (src=P-957) and IA-83 (src=P-971) are all about REVERSION and its criteria dependence, not progression transportability. Grep of existing_gaps.md and themes/T13_evidence_synthesis_existing_gaps.md for 'historical control', 'placebo group simulation', 'PGSA' and 'external control' returned zero hits, and no gap statement mentions P-937. HONEST OVERLAP, stated rather than hidden: P-937 is already the 7th of 11 supporters of VF-29 ('How MCI status and its correlates are ascertained is a first-order determinant of the reported estimate ... the measurement source and the case definition move prevalence estimates by a factor of two or more'). VF-29 is about PREVALENCE estimates and states the general ascertainment principle. What this record adds that VF-29 does not state is (a) the dissociation - baselines converged while trajectories diverged, so baseline matching is not a sufficient remedy - and (b) the specific design premise that this defeats (substituting a historical control group for a randomised placebo arm). A gate that judges VF-29 to already cover it should reject this record rather than duplicate it.

invalidated_assumptions.review_note: 2026-09-10 G5 consolidated verdict (data/g5_consolidated_ia_verdicts.csv): REJECTED as invalidated assumption (2/2 reject-as-IA). Five datasets matched on baseline characteristics yet progression diverged (~10% at 4 years in the drug-trial sample vs ~30% in the other four), but ONE dataset (InDDEx) drives the divergence and the authors attribute part of it to healthy-volunteer/selection effects - a historical-control method can fail through selection effects rather than intrinsic non-transportability. Keep the narrow methodological warning: 'baseline matching alone does not guarantee transportability of MCI progression trajectories'; retain the record's role as VF-29 supporter; do not confirm the stronger historical-control-premise invalidation. Status set to rejected_g5_belief_not_disproved.

invalidated_assumptions.prior_belief: The source paper's own framing, in two places. (1) Prior-work section: 'increased variability in metabolic/lipid parameters (Moser 2018, Chung 2018) was associated with dementia risk' - P-1222 reports this as the established position it is testing against, naming the two studies that hold it. (2) Comparison section: its result 'contrasts with Moser et al. and Chung et al. who reported HIGH TC/triglyceride variability with increased incident dementia risk'. The paper further treats the discrepancy as one the field must resolve, listing 'reconciling direction of VIM association (low TC/non-HDL-C variability here vs high variability in Moser/Chung) via harmonised methodology' among its open problems - which is only coherent if the high-variability direction is the standing position. No corpus paper states the prior (a grep of every digest for lipid/cholesterol/visit-to-visit variability and VIM returns P-1222 alone), and no assumption_registry entry covers it, so the prior rests on the source's own framing and would be a NEW KA if the operator accepts it.
invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: The standing lipid-variability prior - that HIGH visit-to-visit variability in blood lipids marks elevated dementia/cognitive-impairment risk - is reversed in the decade before symptom onset: in a propensity-matched EHR case-control study the LOWEST variability-independent-of-the-mean (VIM) quintile carried the highest risk, for MCI (lowest non-HDL-C VIM quintile, OR 2.2, 95% CI 1.3-3.8, P=0.004) and for AD (lowest total-cholesterol VIM quintile, OR 2.5, 95% CI 1.5-4.0, P<0.001), with the direction retained in both PRS-adjusted and APOE-adjusted models. The reversal is directional, not a magnitude disagreement, and the source paper itself names the prior literature it contradicts.

evidence_quotes.quote: increased variability in metabolic/lipid parameters (Moser 2018, Chung 2018) was associated with dementia risk

fp_codes_cleared: STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF: the prior is not miner-constructed. The source's own 'What has been done?' section states the high-variability position as prior work with citations (Moser 2018, Chung 2018), and its 'Related findings' section states its result 'contrasts with' that position. The source does NOT record equipoise on the variability axis - the equipoise it records is on lipid LEVELS (midlife high vs late-life low), a different construct.

MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: this record deliberately rests ONLY on the VIM quintile ORs, which are empirical quintiles of a statistic computed from measured routine lipid draws. It does NOT rest on the HDL-C trajectory-group ORs, which come from model-fitted latent classes (traj plugin, posterior probability >=0.85) fed downstream as if observed - the card flags exactly that weakness, and the trajectory ORs are excluded from the claim.

DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: VIM is derived, but the quantity it derives from (measured serum lipid concentrations) is not conceded artifactual anywhere in the source; no SUCRA-style rank or ratio-of-fitted-values is involved.

SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: the AD cohort (215 cases/483 controls) and MCI cohort (116 cases/435 controls) are separate analyses with separate ORs. The MCI-stage claim comes from the MCI cohort alone; nothing is pooled across MCI and dementia.
UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE: both reversal-bearing contrasts carry a point estimate, a 95% CI and a p-value in the source's own results section (OR 2.2 [1.3-3.8] P=0.004; OR 2.5 [1.5-4.0] P<0.001).

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: low-variability-as-risk is not positioned by the source as an established alternative pattern it is joining - the source lists reconciling the direction as an OPEN PROBLEM, i.e. it treats the direction as unexplained rather than as a known exception. The genuinely established exception in this field (low late-life cholesterol LEVELS) is a different measure, and VIM is constructed to be independent of the mean.

AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM: PARTIALLY cleared and stated as such. The authors DO claim the finding - 'low TC VIM risk' is in their Key Novelty line and low variability is named in their significance statement - so the reversal is not miner-elevated from a limitations paragraph. They do NOT claim the prior literature is wrong; they attribute the difference to VIM window, case definition and logistic-vs-survival modelling and file reconciliation under open problems. The claim above is therefore scoped to a directional reversal in pre-onset routine-care data, not to a refutation of Moser/Chung.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: PARTIALLY cleared. The only correction the digest records is Bonferroni on the AUROC comparisons, not on the ORs. The AD-arm contrast (P<0.001) survives Bonferroni over the five lipid measures and over all 25 lipid-by-quintile contrasts; the MCI-arm contrast (P=0.004) survives Bonferroni over five measures (0.01) but not over 25 (0.002). An operator who requires family-wide correction across all contrasts should treat the AD arm as the load-bearing evidence and the MCI arm as supporting.

STRAWMAN_PRIOR_BELIEF: the prior is not constructed by the miner. P-1222's own prior-work section states 'increased variability in metabolic/lipid parameters (Moser 2018, Chung 2018) was associated with dementia risk', and its comparison section states that its result 'contrasts with Moser et al. and Chung et al.'. The source names the position and names its own disagreement with it.

MODEL_FITTED_VALUE_AS_MEASURED: the record rests on VIM quintiles, which are empirical strata of variability computed from each patient's measured serum lipid draws, entered into covariate-adjusted logistic regression. It deliberately does NOT rest on the group-based trajectory classes, which are model-assigned latent memberships. The directly estimated contrast is the one being claimed.

SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION: the paper does not decline the finding. It states it in 'What is the significance?' ('low TC/non-HDL-C variability - independently improve AD and MCI risk prediction beyond APOE and PRS') and in Key findings reported. What it files as open is the METHODOLOGICAL reconciliation with Moser/Chung, not the existence or direction of its own estimate. (This is the closest FP code to firing - see residual_risk.)

AUTHORS_DECLINED_TO_CLAIM: the reversal-bearing quantity is present in the paper's Key Novelty line verbatim as 'low TC VIM risk'. IA-66 was rejected precisely because its reversal quantity was absent from the source's significance and novelty statements; here it is present in both.

DERIVED_RANK_INHERITS_FLAGGED_ARTIFACT: no derived rank, ratio or composite is involved. A VIM quintile is a stratification of a measured quantity, and the paper concedes no artefact in the underlying estimate.

SCOPE_POOLED_POPULATION: the AD cohort (215 cases / 483 controls) and the MCI cohort (116 cases / 435 controls) are separate analyses with separate case and control sets. The MCI-specific reversal comes from the MCI cohort, not from an MCI-plus-dementia pool.

FAILS_SOURCE_OWN_CORRECTION: the source's stated multiple-comparison correction (Bonferroni) is applied to its AUROC model comparisons, not to the quintile odds ratios, so the record is not selecting a nominal survivor out of a family that a pre-specified correction was policing. Multiplicity across five lipid measures remains a live concern and is named in residual_risk.

EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD: the established exception in this literature concerns lipid LEVELS - the paper itself records 'midlife high TC/LDL-C to AD risk and late-life low levels to dementia risk'. VIM is constructed to be independent of the mean, so the low-LEVEL exception does not pre-empt a low-VARIABILITY reversal, and no other corpus paper reports any lipid-variability measure.

UNQUANTIFIED_REVERSAL_CLAUSE: the reversal-bearing sentences carry point estimates, 95% confidence intervals and p-values for both cohorts (MCI OR 2.2 [1.3-3.8], P=0.004; AD OR 2.5 [1.5-4.0], P<0.001), reproduced in the digest rather than deferred to supplementary tables.

invalidated_assumptions.residual_risk:
[T04_blood_omics_p3-conf-01] Low visit-to-visit lipid variability over a decade of EHR draws is a plausible proxy for stable, adherent, well-managed primary care rather than a biological risk state, and the source itself offers that reading - it 'supports the hypothesis that stable low lipids reflect medication/health status, consistent with lipid-lowering therapy-dementia associations in meta-analyses'. Propensity matching was exact on lipid-lowering medication USE, but not on dose, intensity, adherence or visit frequency, and VIM was computed from 'irregular, clinically obtained measurements' whose spacing is itself a function of how sick and how closely followed the patient was. If that confound drives the estimate, the prior is not reversed at all: Moser and Chung measured variability in cohorts with protocol-scheduled draws, and P-1222 may simply be measuring care intensity under the name of variability. The authors' own attribution of the direction difference to 'VIM measurement window, clinically confirmed vs ICD-coded cases, and logistic vs survival modelling' is a second, independent reading in which the reversal is a design artefact rather than a belief overturned.

[T14_reversion_trajectory-conf-01] SOURCE_REFUSES_CONCLUSION is genuinely arguable. P-1222 lists the direction disagreement twice as something unresolved - once under 'What are the problems?' ('findings contrast with Moser et al. and Chung et al. ... methodological differences: VIM window, case definition, survival vs logistic models') and once under open problems ('reconciling direction of VIM association ... via harmonised methodology'). An operator could reasonably hold that the authors are reporting an unexplained discrepancy attributable to their own retrospective, single-health-system, >91% Caucasian design rather than claiming a reversal of the field, in which case the KB would be asserting as overturned what the source calls unresolved - the exact error that sank IA-64 and IA-66. Two secondary objections point the same way: low visit-to-visit variability in routinely collected EHR draws may mark stable, well-managed patients or simply a sparser and more regular measurement pattern rather than a biological state (the paper itself flags 'potential confounding by lipid-lowering medication use' despite exact-matching on it, and its own reading is that 'stable low lipids reflect medication/health status'); and the MCI arm is restricted to stable MCI of at least 5 years, so the MCI-specific reversal is established in a non-converting subgroup and may not transfer to incident or progressive MCI. If the operator judges (1) decisive, this record should be downgraded from an invalidated assumption to a documented cross-study direction discrepancy awaiting a harmonised replication.

invalidated_assumptions.what_disproved_it: KA-17 ('Amyloid is the primary upstream driver of MCI impairment and progression; tau, metabolic and cognitive signals are clinically meaningful only downstream of amyloid positivity') is contradicted by a within-study multivariable head-to-head in biologically-defined MCI. In P-1409, 197 A+T+ ADNI MCI participants were modelled for 2-year dementia progression: the independent predictors that survived were CSF t-tau (AUC 0.684), MoCA (0.716), FAQ (0.762) and study-partner ECog language (0.705), while the amyloid and tau burden measures themselves dropped out. P-1330 corroborates from the other direction: A+T-(N+) 'mismatch' MCI - amyloid-POSITIVE - declined at rates comparable to amyloid-NEGATIVE neurodegeneration-only MCI, so amyloid positivity did not mark an AD-driven course. Together these match KA-17's disproof_signal clause 'amyloid-PET adding nothing over clinical/gait models'. ST

evidence_quotes.quote: Independent baseline predictors of 2-year dementia progression were CSF t-tau (AUC 0.684), MoCA (0.716), FAQ (0.762) and study-partner ECog language (0.705); A and T biomarker levels alone did not retain predictive significance.

Shows that within amyloid-and-tau-positive MCI, neurodegeneration/functional markers (t-tau, FAQ, MoCA, informant language complaints) - not A/T burden - drive short-horizon progression prediction, refining trial enrichment beyond ATN staging.

Mismatch MCI was less "AD-like" than prodromal AD and generally resembled neurodegeneration-only MCI: less baseline episodic-memory loss; slower decline across all cognitive domains; smaller baseline posterior-hippocampal-volume deficit and restricted (medial-temporal-lobe) rather than widespread cortical thinning; slower longitudinal MTL volume loss. Mismatch and neurodegeneration-only MCI declined at comparable rates.

Challenges the assumption that amyloid positivity in MCI implies AD-driven symptoms and demonstrates that non-tau neurodegeneration profiles have distinct trajectories, informing personalised prognosis and trial design.
